Just how large is the county behind these tax bills?

Large enough to work as several markets at once. These headline numbers:

  • Land area: 1,899.90 square miles.
  • Mid-2025 population estimate: 2,802,029.
  • Housing units: 1,125,274, with a 52.2 percent owner-occupancy rate.
  • Typical owned home, 2020 to 2024: $463,000.
  • Household income in that span: $71,753, in 2024 dollars.

Roughly half the housing stock is rented, and the distance between home prices and paychecks explains why caps and exemptions get so much attention here.

Who do I call first about a Miami-Dade tax question?

Match the question to the desk. Three county offices split the job.

  • Property Appraiser: value, exemptions, portability and classifications. The main office is in the Stephen P. Clark Center, 111 NW 1st Street, Suite 710 (305-375-4712). The Cutler Bay branch is at 10710 SW 211 Street, 2nd Floor (305-232-3810). Each is staffed on weekdays during business hours.
  • Tax Collector: prints and collects the bill, with 13 service locations, 24 hour online payment and mobile offices that visit neighborhoods.
  • Clerk of the Courts: records deeds, takes value petitions and runs tax deed auctions.

The appraiser says outright that it does not send tax bills and does not set or collect taxes, so a gripe about the size of a bill is really a question for the taxing bodies that levy millage.

How did the 2026 Miami-Dade roll take shape?

The appraiser published a June 1 estimate of $540.7 billion in countywide taxable value, a 5.5 percent rise on 2025 and 3.2 percentage points slower than the year before. Estimates guide city and county budget planning; they are not final.

A July 1 preliminary certification followed. Then the County Commission ordered the roll extended on September 1, 2026, and the appraiser certified it on October 16, 2026. That certification is the first one, before any changes the Value Adjustment Board makes after appeals.

2026 roll steps posted by the Miami-Dade Property Appraiser

June 1 estimate$540.7 billion taxable, up 5.5%
July 1Preliminary certification sent to taxing authorities
September 1, 2026County Commission orders the roll extended

Source: Property Appraiser of Miami-Dade County.

Why can two Miami-Dade neighbors pay such different rates?

Because the total comes from stacked taxing bodies, and the city layer varies widely. The appraiser's 2026 millage chart runs from 14.9007 on one North Miami Beach line to 24.1893 in Biscayne Park, with unincorporated areas at 16.8983.

Other totals on the chart: Miami 19.9544, Miami Beach 18.6681, Hialeah 18.6134, Coral Gables 18.1518 and Doral 16.9487. Some rows add debt service or special district lines, which is why you should match your own address to a row rather than quote a city figure.

Separate tax guides cover Miami and Miami Beach.

Which cities sit at the low and high ends of the chart?

The chart lists more than three dozen taxing areas, from Aventura, Bal Harbour and Bay Harbor Islands through Key Biscayne, Pinecrest, Sunny Isles Beach and Surfside to West Miami, plus the unincorporated area. Looking only at each city's own operating line:

  • Lowest: Doral at 1.5994 mills, Sunny Isles Beach at 1.6514, Aventura at 1.7261.
  • Middle: Homestead at 5.9604, Hialeah at 6.3018, Miami Gardens at 6.9363.
  • Highest: Biscayne Park at 9.2000, Opa-locka at 8.9797, El Portal at 8.0500.

A low city line can still sit on a heavy total once school, county, fire and library lines are added. Read the bottom number.

What does the county's economy add to the roll?

Census data for 2023 count 98,394 employer establishments with 1,055,440 employees and about $71.6 billion in annual payroll, a 4.6 percent employment gain on 2022. For 2022 the Census lists $67.1 billion in retail sales, $15.4 billion in lodging and food service, $30.3 billion in health care receipts and $38.5 billion in transportation and warehousing. Permits issued in 2025 numbered 16,535.

Businesses carry their own bill. Owners of furniture, equipment and similar property file Form DR-405 with the appraiser by April 1, and the appraiser runs a lookup for tangible property by business name, address or folio.

When is the Miami-Dade bill due, and what does paying early save?

Bills land in November, and the best discount, 4 percent, belongs to that month alone. It steps down by a point each month through February, and anything unpaid on April 1 is delinquent. The tax collector promotes the November discount with a "Save the Max" campaign and takes payment online, at its 13 locations or at its mobile offices.

  • August: the proposed-tax notice previews the bill.
  • Twenty-five days from that notice: the last chance for a value petition at the clerk's desk.
  • Thirty days after a denial letter is mailed: the window to challenge an exemption denial.
  • May 1: the cutoff for asking the collector for installments.

What happens when a Miami-Dade bill goes unpaid?

Unpaid balances turn into tax certificates, which the collector auctions to whoever will accept the lowest interest, bidding down in quarter-point steps. Certificates nobody bids on pass to the county at the top rate, and the sales wrap up by June 1. A homestead parcel owing less than $250 skips the auction and goes to the county. The collector retains a 5 percent commission.

Deed pressure comes slowly: a holder must wait out two years from the April after issue, then pay a $75 application charge. At the later auction the top bidder posts a deposit of 5 percent or $200, whichever is larger, and settles the rest inside 24 hours on business days. The tax collector lists a Tax Certificate Sales service; ask the clerk about auction dates.

How fast can a Miami-Dade assessment climb?

Homestead value is held to the smaller of 3 percent and inflation. Rentals, second homes and commercial parcels face a 10 percent annual ceiling. A sale wipes out both cushions, since the new owner is assessed at market the following January 1.

A constitutional amendment that voters approved in November 2026 is already built into the appraiser's estimator, which shows Amendment 3 figures for 2027 and 2028. Run your own folio through it before guessing at a future bill. Millage itself still comes out of budget hearings held in the fall.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Which breaks can a Miami-Dade homeowner claim?

The base homestead exemption reaches $50,000 and is claimed with the appraiser by March 1. Other breaks target particular owners.

  • Seniors: an extra exemption, as large as $50,000, where a local ordinance provides it and household income stays under the cap.
  • Service-connected disability at 10 percent or higher: a $5,000 reduction.
  • Older veterans with a permanent service-connected disability: a discount equal to the VA rating.
  • Deferral: file Form DR-570 with the tax collector by March 31 to postpone the share of the bill above 5 percent of income, or 3 percent for permanent residents past 65.

Can the appraiser's online tools save me a trip?

Often. Widow(er) exemptions and disability exemptions for veterans or surviving spouses can be filed online, and agricultural classification uses form MD-482 with uploaded papers. Appointments can be booked online, and a tax estimator and walkthrough video sit on the home page.

Two protections stand out. The clerk runs a free alert that pings an owner within a day when a deed or mortgage is filed under that name, and the appraiser's compliance team takes suspected homestead fraud reports at 305-375-3402.

What changes in the tax bill when a Miami-Dade house sells?

The title agent obtains the collector's balance and settles the year's tax at the closing table, divided as the contract says. The buyer arrives with a reassessed value and needs a fresh exemption filing.

Deed stamps here are set at 60 cents per $100, and the county adds a 45 cent surtax per $100 that state revenue officials exclude for a deed that conveys nothing but a single-family house. Ask the closing agent which line your deed falls under.

Frequently asked questions

What total millage applies in unincorporated Miami-Dade for 2026?

The chart total is 16.8983 mills. That is the combined figure for the unincorporated area; incorporated cities have their own totals.

Where can a Miami-Dade owner pay the bill?

Use the Tax Collector: its website, any of 13 locations or a visiting mobile office. The appraiser takes no payments.

How soon must a Miami-Dade value petition be filed?

Twenty-five days from the August notice of proposed taxes. File the petition with the clerk. A denied exemption follows a 30 day clock from the letter.

Does paying early cut a Miami-Dade bill?

Yes, by up to 4 percent. The reduction shrinks every month from November and is gone by March.

Is Miami-Dade subject to the Save Our Homes limit?

Yes. Homestead growth is limited to the lesser of 3 percent or inflation, and a sale resets it.

How did Broward County come to exist?

Broward was carved out of Dade and Palm Beach territory and became Florida's 51st county on October 1, 1915. According to a city of Pompano Beach history, it measured 24 miles north to south and 48 miles east to west, held about 4,700 people packed within a mile or two of the coast, and had only three incorporated towns: Dania, Pompano and Fort Lauderdale.

Opening day brought a parade, a concert and picnic lunches in Fort Lauderdale, the new seat, along with speeches by the first commissioners.

Residents had wanted to call it Everglades County. Instead it took the name of a governor who championed draining the Everglades, which the history calls ironic. Northern Dade residents had complained that their tax dollars favored Miami, and a local vote on alcohol sales also pushed Miami-area voters toward a new county.

What was here before the county?

The land passed through several counties. Under the first territorial government it belonged to a huge St. Johns County, later to Mosquito County, and then to a southeast coast county first meant to be Pinckney County and renamed Dade after the 1835 ambush that started the Second Seminole War. Palm Beach became the 47th county in 1909 and briefly reached south to Pompano.

The Florida East Coast Railway reached Palm Beach in 1894 and Miami in 1896, ending the area's isolation and bringing farm towns along the tracks. Before that, the first major road linking Miami and Lantana, a nine-foot gravel track, was built in 1892.

How big and varied is Broward today?

The county now includes 31 municipalities. Fort Lauderdale serves as seat and biggest city, covering more than 33 square miles with 183,146 residents, according to the city. It was incorporated on March 27, 1911, and sits framed by seven miles of beach and the Everglades, with the Intracoastal Waterway, the New River and a canal system running through the middle.

The city names Las Olas Boulevard and the Riverwalk arts district, with the Broward Center for the Performing Arts, the Museum of Discovery and Science, the NSU Art Museum and History Fort Lauderdale, and notes downtown campuses of Broward College, Florida Atlantic University and Florida International University.

For a seller, the variety shows up in values. A canal-front home near Las Olas and a condo in a western city share a county appraiser and tax collector but not a market.

Which Broward office does what?

The property appraiser sets assessed values and approves exemptions. It states plainly that it does not mail tax bills and does not set or collect taxes. Billing and collection belong to the Broward County Tax Collector, reachable at (954) 357-4829 or revenue@browardtax.org, as printed on the appraiser's home page.

Deed recording runs through the county's official records, and the appraiser's FAQ page has a deed topic for questions on adding or removing an owner or getting copies of recorded documents. Counter service is on weekdays.

When can Broward owners file for 2027 homestead?

The appraiser prints a timely filing period of March 3, 2026 through March 1, 2027 for the 2027 exemption. It applies to owners who held title and made the house their permanent home after January 1, 2026.

Someone who misses March 1 has until September 20, 2027, and the office notes that s. 196.011(8) allows no later date, even with good cause. Because the dates belong to one tax year, use the appraiser's page as the reference for later years.

What free tools does the Broward appraiser offer to sellers and buyers?

The site carries several that a house sale can use.

  • A Home Buyer's Tax Estimator that approximates the bill after a reassessment, which helps a seller explain why a buyer's taxes will differ.
  • A Portability Estimator for owners moving a homestead benefit to a new Florida home.
  • Owner Alert, a free message when a filing that changes who owns your parcel reaches the appraiser, built to flag scams.
  • A catastrophic structural damage report form for a home left uninhabitable for at least 30 days by a catastrophic event.
  • Tabs for Senior Citizens, Appeals and Petitions, Market Sales and Important Dates, and a posted Property Owner Bill of Rights.

The appraiser's site menu also lists Exemption Express, Download Forms, Tangible Property, Maps and Aerials, Data Requests and a Report Fraud page. A seller who rents out furnished space can start at the Tangible Property tab, and anyone who suspects a forged deed can use the fraud page and the Owner Alert subscription together.

Its crucial buyer notice tells purchasers not to expect the seller's taxes to carry over, since the new owner starts at full market value.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

How does moving or selling affect a Broward homestead?

The sale ends the homestead cap on the old house. Someone buying another Florida home can file Form DR-501T alongside the new application, provided the new homestead starts inside the three-year window. A 2026 act amends the portability section for the 2027 roll, so ask the appraiser's portability staff what applies to your move.

Rentals face a yearly ceiling of 10 percent, so a landlord's gap between assessed and market value is usually narrower than a long-time homesteader's.

Which relief programs can a Broward owner ask about?

Age and veteran relief varies by ordinance and service record, so the Senior Citizens tab on the appraiser's site is the quickest place to learn what a particular address can claim. The state also offers a $5,000 reduction for disabled former servicemembers, and a deferral through the collector with a March 31 filing date.

What if a Broward bill goes unpaid?

Delinquency starts April 1, and the collector auctions certificates for the lowest bid rate by June 1. If a tax deed notice shows up, call the collector at once. A seller who clears the balance before any deed application avoids the auction altogether, and the title agent can pay it from proceeds. Homestead rules on small balances and opening bids sit in s. 197.502.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Where does a Broward value challenge go?

The appraiser's Appeals and Petitions section explains the route. A formal petition goes to the clerk. Property owners get 25 days from the August notice, and an exemption denial carries its own 30 day clock from the letter.

What should heirs or owners with unwanted occupants know?

An heir can call the appraiser at (954) 357-5579 to learn how a transfer on death is treated, since some transfers are exceptions to the reset.

Uninvited occupants are a separate matter. The sheriff handles a verified complaint under s. 82.036, which carries conditions such as no tenancy and no pending litigation, and adverse possession (s. 95.18) needs seven years.

Frequently asked questions

Which office collects Broward tax?

The Broward County Tax Collector. The appraiser says it neither sends bills nor collects taxes.

What is the late-filing limit for a 2027 Broward homestead?

September 20, 2027, with no later date allowed under s. 196.011(8).

Can I file my Broward homestead online?

Yes, through the appraiser's online homestead page at bcpa.net. Email, fax, mail and phone help are also listed, and staff can set a virtual meeting for owners who want help with the forms.

What does Owner Alert do?

It is a free service that notifies you when a document changing your property's ownership is received by the appraiser. Subscribers use the appraiser's app, and it is meant to help protect a parcel from scams or fraud.

When does a Broward bill turn delinquent?

April 1, per the state calendar, with certificates sold by June 1.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Whom do I call about a Hillsborough County property tax question?

It depends on the question. The Hillsborough County Property Appraiser handles value and exemptions. The Hillsborough County Tax Collector handles money, receipts and payment plans.

The appraiser's downtown Tampa office is on the 15th floor of the County Center, 601 E. Kennedy Boulevard, reachable at (813) 272-6100 Monday through Friday from 8 to 5. The collector publishes bills, payment options and a property search on its real estate tax page. A board separate from both offices, the Value Adjustment Board, hears value and exemption disputes.

  • Property Appraiser: just value, homestead filings, the assessment cap, portability and the TRIM notice.
  • Tax Collector: bills, installment applications, partial payments and tax certificates.
  • Clerk of the Circuit Court: recorded deeds, liens and the tax deed auction.

The appraiser's site also promotes a free Property Fraud Alert that flags new recordings made in your name. Heirs holding an empty Tampa Bay house are the people most likely to want it switched on.

How does a Hillsborough County bill and its early payment discount work?

Hillsborough tax notices land in November and can be paid from the 1st. The collector's FAQ says an account still open on April 1 picks up 3% interest and advertising costs.

Early payers get a cut of 4 percent in November, 3 in December, 2 in January and 1 in February, and March is full price. A winter seller should ask the closing agent which of those months the closing date falls in, since the sale proceeds may be what pays the bill.

Smaller checks are possible through the installment plan, which needs an application before May 1 and starts with a June payment. Paying in July keeps the plan alive but forfeits the discount. If nothing arrives by July 31 the account leaves the plan and the whole balance is payable the next November, with the 4 percent break. A separate partial payment option exists for current-year bills only, and an overdue real estate account has to be cleared in one payment.

Which Hillsborough County dates belong on a calendar?

Seven dates drive nearly every decision a Hillsborough County owner or seller makes.

WhenWhat it triggersPublished by
January 1Valuation date and homestead test dateFlorida Department of Revenue
March 1Exemption filing deadlineProperty Appraiser
May 1Last day to request the installment planTax Collector FAQ
By June 1Online auction of tax certificatesTax Collector FAQ
AugustTRIM notice mailed, then 25 days to petition on valueFlorida Department of Revenue
November 1Bills payableTax Collector FAQ
April 1DelinquencyTax Collector FAQ

The appraiser's home page reports that the latest TRIM mailing began August 13, with longer office hours, and links a 2026 Hurricane Damage Adjustment Form for storm-hit owners. A refused exemption produces an Official Notice of Denial by July 1, which opens a hearing before a Value Adjustment Board magistrate.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

What exemptions can a Hillsborough County owner stack?

A permanent residence can shed up to $50,000 of assessed value in two layers.

Layer one touches every levy. Layer two sits on the slice of assessed value above $50,000 and skips school taxes. A yearly growth limit then applies after the first year. The appraiser accepts filings year round, cites March 1 as the legal deadline, and says a late one may still be taken up to 25 days after TRIM notices are mailed.

  • Low income senior: unincorporated Hillsborough County and the City of Tampa allow up to $50,000, and Temple Terrace allows up to $25,000.
  • Long term resident senior: Tampa and unincorporated areas, for homes with just value under $250,000 and 25 consecutive years in residence.
  • Veteran, disability, widow and blind exemptions: these need documents, and Hillsborough County Veterans Affairs lists 813-635-8316 for help with discharge papers.

Claiming homestead on a house you have left is expensive. According to the appraiser, the exempted taxes from the prior 10 years turn into a lien carrying a 50 percent penalty and 15 percent interest, so report a move-out before the sign goes in the yard.

What did Amendment 3 change for Hillsborough County homesteads?

Voters passed the statewide property tax amendment on November 3, 2026. A statement from the Hillsborough appraiser about its passage sits on that office's home page.

On its legislative update page the appraiser describes homestead exemption amounts of up to $150,000 from 2027 and up to $250,000 from 2028, with lawmakers told to schedule more increases. That page adds that the effect varies by parcel and cannot be calculated in advance. Treat the number on today's bill as the working figure until a TRIM notice shows a new one. The tax collector keeps a property tax reform page on the same ballot item.

Sellers feel this mostly through the buyer. The first bill after a purchase begins from just value, and a new exemption amount reaches the buyer only after an application is filed.

Who pays the tax when a Hillsborough County house closes?

An open Hillsborough County bill is settled out of the seller's proceeds at the table, because the lien stays with the land. The collector says the name printed on a bill is no obstacle to paying it, since a recorded deed may not have reached the appraiser before the roll was certified.

The seller's homestead ends with the sale, and the buyer starts over at just value after the next January 1 and files a new application. What the seller can carry along is the portable savings, which attach to a replacement home.

  • Escrowed loans: the servicer pays from a list it sends the collector, and once the loan is paid off the next bill is mailed to the owner.
  • Deed stamps: the state rate applies here because Hillsborough is not Miami-Dade, and each party on the deed shares the liability.
  • Portability: the replacement homestead has a three year window and needs a DR-501T with the new application.
Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

How does unpaid Hillsborough County tax reach a tax deed sale?

A skipped bill becomes a tax certificate first, and a deed sale can come about two years after that.

The collector auctions certificates online. Bids start at 18 percent and fall by 0.25 percent per step, and the lowest bidder wins a certificate that ranks first among liens, including other government ones. Per the collector, a deed application cannot begin until up to 22 months after issue. The statute measures two years from April 1 of the issue year. When a homestead owes under $250, the county takes the certificate itself and no investor can buy it.

The clerk conducts the deed auction, and a homestead parcel's opening bid includes half of the last assessed value. An owner who is behind can still sell, since paying off the certificate at closing clears the title.

Frequently asked questions

When is Hillsborough County property tax due?

Bills are payable November 1 and go delinquent April 1. The discount is 4 percent in November, then 3, 2 and 1 percent through February. An account open on April 1 picks up 3% interest and advertising costs.

Can I pay Hillsborough County tax in installments?

Yes, if you apply before May 1. The first payment is due in June, a July payment keeps you in the plan without the discount, and missing July 31 drops the account into a single November payment with the 4 percent discount.

Who decides a Hillsborough County homestead claim?

The Property Appraiser does. Filing closes March 1, any denial notice is mailed by July 1, and an appeal heads to the Value Adjustment Board. The collector never rules on eligibility.

Are partial payments allowed on a delinquent Hillsborough County bill?

No. Only current-year bills qualify for the partial plan, and an overdue real estate bill needs the full balance. Call the collector before sending anything smaller.

What if I sell before my Hillsborough County bill arrives?

The bill is still paid at closing. The title agent requests the amount from the collector and takes it out of the seller's money, and the buyer applies for a new homestead by the next March 1.

Which Palm Beach County office should I call about my tax bill?

It depends on the question. The Property Appraiser answers anything about value, exemptions and caps. The Tax Collector answers anything about the amount due and how to pay it. The Clerk and Comptroller runs the Value Adjustment Board and the tax deed auction.

The Tax Collector says it mails more than 600,000 property tax bills by November 1, and sends each to the address the appraiser has on file. If you moved or sold, correct the mailing address with the appraiser, not the collector.

  • Property Appraiser: value, exemptions, caps, the TRIM notice.
  • Tax Collector: bills, payment, installment plan, deferral, certificates.
  • Clerk and Comptroller: appeals board petitions and tax deed sales.

How big is Palm Beach County, and who lives in it?

The Census county page counts 1,575,726 people as of mid-2025. Its housing data for 2020 through 2024 gives owners a $447,300 midpoint home value and a 70.1 percent ownership rate, with household income at $83,581 in 2024 dollars. Those 65 or older are 26.1 percent of residents, so age-based relief touches a large share of bills.

The appraiser's municipality list shows how many cities and towns levy separately. Codes begin with 00 for unincorporated land and run through Atlantis, Belle Glade, Boca Raton, Boynton Beach, Delray Beach, Jupiter, Lake Worth Beach, Palm Beach, Pahokee, Tequesta, Wellington, West Palm Beach and Westlake. The first digits of a 17-digit parcel control number carry that code, so the number on your bill reveals which city taxes your lot.

What do the appraiser's exemption charts say for 2026?

They list more than a dozen exemptions, and a few have dollar limits that change yearly. The chart prints a 2026 household income limit of $38,686 in adjusted gross income for the senior exemption, and $37,712 in gross income for the civilian total and permanent disability and paraplegic or hemiplegic exemptions. Eligibility uses the prior year's income.

Source: Property Appraiser, Exemptions: Do You Qualify. Filing closes March 1. The chart points veterans to the county Veteran Services office.

What do homestead filing and the caps require?

The appraiser asks for three things: title in your name, permanent Florida residence, and the home lived in on January 1. File by March 1, since a late filer loses that year's exemption. Online, service center and mail all work, and approval renews itself until something changes.

The first slice of $25,000 counts against every levy, schools included. A further slice of up to $25,000 starts once assessed value passes $50,000 and skips the school levy. Save Our Homes limits how far a homestead's assessment can rise in a year, using inflation or 3 percent, whichever is smaller; the state chart's 2026 entry is 2.7.

Property that is not homestead, such as a rental or second home, has a 10 percent cap on every levy except the school board's, and the appraiser notes the cap falls away the year after a sale. Report any change in ownership, marriage, divorce, death or use of the home to the appraiser.

When are Palm Beach County bills due, and how do discounts and installments work?

Payment opens November 1 and runs through March 31. Early payers save 4 percent in November, 3 in December, 2 in January and 1 in February; March carries the full amount.

April 1 starts delinquency. Per the collector, late tax is not payable online; funds must be in hand by the month's final working day to count, since a postmark stops mattering after delinquency.

The installment payment plan splits taxes into four payments due around June or July, September, December and March. The collector's 2026 deadline to apply was April 30, and enrollment for 2027 opens November 1, 2026. The collector's calendar for the current year controls the exact dates.

How does the tax work out when a Palm Beach County home sells?

An unpaid balance attaches to the parcel, so the closing table is where it ends. The title agent reads the bill and subtracts any payoff before paying the seller. Settle with the buyer how the current year's bill is split, because bills go out in November but closings occur in every month.

The deed carries state stamp tax at seventy cents per hundred dollars everywhere but Miami-Dade, and every signer answers to the state for it, whatever the contract assigns. Payment happens at the recording counter, next to the page fees set by section 28.24.

For the buyer, assessed value resets to market value from the next January 1. The seller's capped savings do not transfer, which is why a long-time neighbor's bill can differ sharply from a new owner's.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What happens if Palm Beach County taxes go unpaid?

Delinquency moves through fixed stages, and paying at any point before the auction ends it. The collector must hold an annual certificate sale no earlier than 60 days after delinquency or June 1, whichever is later. A certificate is a first lien bought by an investor who pays your tax in exchange for a competitive bid rate.

To redeem, you pay the delinquent tax, interest, advertising costs and a $6.25 collection fee added to each certificate. Certificates that draw no bidder go to the county, where the collector states interest runs at 18 percent annually.

After two years from delinquency, the certificate holder may file a tax deed application, and the clerk's office runs the sale. Redemption stays open until the sale itself. An owner behind on tax can still sell, because closing pays the balance.

What is the route for disputing a Palm Beach County assessment?

Phone the appraiser first. If the disagreement survives, file with the Value Adjustment Board. The appraiser's FAQ encourages that first call, and its records are searchable online.

On the appraiser's calendar, mid-September closes the window for market value appeals and denied portability claims, and a denied exemption has until July 31 or the 30th day after the denial notice. The state taxpayer page separately gives a 25-day limit counted from the TRIM mailing. Your own notice is the final word on timing. The Clerk runs the board independently of the appraiser, so ask for the current filing fee before you file.

Frequently asked questions

Where does my Palm Beach County tax payment go?

To the Tax Collector, which bills and collects. The Property Appraiser only sets value and exemptions.

Does paying early cut a Palm Beach County bill?

Yes. The collector's schedule starts at 4 percent for November and falls a point monthly, ending after February.

Does homestead end when a Palm Beach County home is sold?

The sale ends it for that house. Apply again for your next home, and use portability to bring part of your capped savings along if you buy within three years.

What is the Super Senior exemption?

It exempts a qualifying owner from city levies in Boynton Beach or Delray Beach only. It needs 25 years of ownership and a market value under $250,000 at application.

Which office records a Palm Beach County deed?

The Clerk and Comptroller records it and collects the documentary stamp tax at that time.

Who answers questions about an Orange County tax statement?

Orange County divides the job three ways, so the right call depends on the problem. A wrong value or missing exemption belongs to the Property Appraiser at 200 S Orange Ave, Suite 1700 in Orlando. A bill, a payment or a delinquency belongs to the Tax Collector. The rate itself is a product of local boards.

  • Value, ownership, legal description and mailing address: Property Appraiser
  • Millage: the county commission, school board, cities and special districts
  • Statements, payment plans, certificates: Tax Collector

The Tax Collector's own page says it passes the money on to 63 taxing authorities. Items such as streetlights, sewers and road work are non-ad valorem charges, priced per unit and printed on the same statement.

What is the Orange County property tax calendar?

The year's value is pinned to January 1. Statements reach owners by the first of November, and the balance must arrive at the Tax Collector before April begins.

Key tax dates in Orange County, per the Tax Collector and Florida revenue pages
WhenWhat happens
January 1Assessment date
March 1Last day to file an exemption request
AugustProposed tax notice mailed
By November 1Statements mailed
November to FebruaryFour, three, two and one percent discounts
March 31Gross amount and deferral applications due
April 1Delinquency begins
By June 1Online certificate sale

A check postmarked March 30 but delivered in April is late, because the office goes by receipt.

How much can an early payment save in Orange County?

Pay in November and the bill drops four percent. Each month after that trims one point less, ending at one percent in February, and March pays the gross figure.

Sellers who close in winter can pay the whole year at the closing table, so the month on the contract changes the net. Your title agent can quote the number for your actual closing day. When a lender escrows your taxes it may ask for the statement, and you receive a copy stamped with the lender's request. That copy does not call for a second payment.

Owners who are current and whose prior bill topped $100 can ask for the quarterly installment plan, which is applied for online at the Tax Collector's site.

Which exemptions apply to a home in Orange County?

Homestead leads the list, and the Property Appraiser says it can lower taxable value by as much as $50,000. In the state's description, the opening $25,000 touches every levy, and a second slice reaches only non-school levies above $50,000 of assessed value.

File with the Property Appraiser before March 1, and live in the house as your permanent home on January 1. Widow, disability, senior and military exemptions also exist. Once homesteaded, the assessed figure may rise each year by no more than the smaller of 3 percent or the inflation change. A sale wipes out that gap on the following January 1, so a buyer's first bill can be well above yours. The Property Appraiser's tax estimator is aimed at people weighing a purchase or sale.

Can a house with old tax debt change hands in Orange County?

You can still sell. The title agent requests a payoff from the Tax Collector, and every open balance gets cleared as part of closing.

Once April arrives, the Tax Collector adds a 3 percent minimum charge and advertising cost. Parcels are listed in a local paper for three straight weeks, then certificates go up for competitive bids that start at 18 percent and drop. To clear a certificate, pay the tax, accrued interest and advertising cost. Late payers must use certified or cashier's funds, a money order, certain attorney, title or escrow checks, or cash at the counter; personal and business checks are refused.

  • Ask for the payoff before you list
  • Confirm whether a certificate already exists
  • Compare escrow records with the county account

How long before a certificate threatens the house?

Two years. Only then can the certificate holder apply for a tax deed, and the Tax Collector says Orange County routes those sales through the Comptroller's Office.

Before that, state law bars the holder from pressing the owner for payment. Homestead land gets one more cushion, because the opening bid must include half of its latest assessed value on top of the money due. Even so, an owner facing this stage should call the Tax Collector's property tax department early and ask for a redemption total.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Can I defer homestead tax in Orange County?

Qualifying homesteaders can postpone part of the bill by applying to the Tax Collector before April. This is a different program from the exemption.

Postponed tax remains a lien on the property. Before listing, put this question to the Tax Collector: how is a postponed balance, with interest, paid off in a sale? The state ties the amount to household income and lets a permanent resident aged 65 or older defer the share above 3 percent of that income.

What can I look up on the Orange County Property Appraiser site?

The Property Appraiser's home page offers a property search by address, owner name, sale history, property use and foreclosure status. It also links a tax estimator, a map site, downloadable forms, a tax roll and millage page, an income survey for commercial owners, code tables and a property fraud alert.

  • Use the search to confirm the parcel, owner and exemptions on your record
  • Run the estimator when you want a buyer to see a likely tax picture
  • Download the exemption forms if a new owner needs to file
  • Sign up for the fraud alert to watch your record

The estimator should be treated as a planning aid, since a new owner may not keep the seller's exemptions.

Do landlords owe a second tax in Orange County?

Yes, if the rental holds furniture, fixtures or equipment. The Tax Collector describes tangible personal property tax as a levy on those items in businesses and rental property, and on structural additions to mobile homes.

These statements arrive alongside the real estate statements and carry the same discounts. Past March 31 a monthly charge of 1.5 percent accrues, and a collection firm under contract adds 15 percent on accounts left unpaid. Selling a furnished rental means asking the Tax Collector how any open account is handled.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

What do Orange County numbers say about owners?

1,528,002 people in July 2025, spread over 527,776 households. Owners live in 56.8 percent of the homes, whose middle value is $390,100. A median mortgage holder spends $2,055 monthly, against $1,775 for a typical rent.

A statement's lines shift with the home's location: inside a city, in unincorporated Orange County, or within a special district. Read those lines on your own account before quoting a tax figure to a buyer.

Frequently asked questions

Until what date can Orange County owners pay without a late charge?

March 31, counted by the day the Tax Collector receives it. A check that lands in April is delinquent.

What does a November payment save?

Four percent. The discount shrinks by a point each month until February, and March has none.

Which Orange County office fixes a wrong value or missing exemption?

The Property Appraiser. The Tax Collector bills what the certified roll shows and cannot change value, ownership or exemptions.

Can a homeowner with unpaid taxes still sell in Orange County?

Yes. Request the Tax Collector's payoff, then let the title agent settle it at closing, with certified funds if the bill is already delinquent.

Does a tax certificate transfer my house to an investor?

No. It is a lien, and you can redeem it by paying the tax, interest and advertising cost. A tax deed application cannot come until two years have passed.

Who answers property tax questions in Jacksonville and Duval County?

Two city departments split the work: the Property Appraiser values parcels and decides exemptions, while the Tax Collector bills and collects. Jacksonville and Duval County are consolidated, so both offices post on jacksonville.gov.

The appraiser's Customer Service and Exemptions Division sits at 231 E. Forsyth Street, Suite 260, and answers at 904-255-5900. The collector uses the same street, at 231 E. Forsyth Street, with a main line of (904) 255-5700 and a weekday counter that opens at half past eight and closes at half past four. Value petitions go through the Value Adjustment Board at (904) 255-5124.

Branch offices matter if you would rather not drive downtown. The collector lists Yates (main), Mandarin, Neptune Beach, North Main Street, Roosevelt, Soutel, Westside and a newer St Johns Square branch at 11160 Beach Blvd., Suite 121. That branch took over from the former Kernan and Hogan offices, which are permanently closed.

Why does a Duval parcel carry one of six district codes?

The code on a parcel tells you which set of taxing authorities applies, and Duval has six: GS and USD1 for Jacksonville, USD2 for Jacksonville Beach, USD3 for Atlantic Beach, USD4 for Neptune Beach and USD5 for Baldwin.

Each district's total millage is stacked from separate levies. Countywide, the listed authorities are the county itself, the public schools, the Florida Inland Navigation District and the St. Johns River Water Management District. The three beach cities and the Town of Baldwin add municipal levies on top. Inside one district, a business and a homeowner see the same millage unless a statute or local ordinance exempts something.

The appraiser keeps millage charts as PDFs for each year back to 1999, so a seller can compare how a district's total has moved. Public meetings that set the individual levies happen in September, and the dates are printed on the mailed notice.

Which 2026 roll milestones has the Duval appraiser posted?

The appraiser's home page lists the 2026 steps below. Dates for the exemption deadline and the notice mailing are fixed by Florida's yearly calendar, so they repeat from year to year.

Duval County 2026 roll steps as printed by the Property Appraiser
StepDate shown
Preliminary tax roll approvedJuly 24, 2026
TRIM notices mailedFriday, August 14, 2026
Final tax roll certifiedOctober 13, 2026
Prior-year roll recertified after the Value Adjustment BoardJune 9, 2026
Timely homestead filing for the 2027 rollMarch 1, 2027
Tangible personal property returnApril 1 each year

Tax bills from the collector are mailed on or about November 1. If a mortgage servicer escrows your tax, ask which bill it paid before you request a payoff.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

How do I file for homestead in Duval County?

Owners who bought and moved in after January 1, 2026 can file online for the 2027 roll, or mail a paper form to Suite 260, fax it to (904) 255-7963 or email it to the customer service address on the appraiser's page.

  • The home must be your permanent residence, or that of someone who depends on you, on the first of January that starts the roll year.
  • Some situations require extra documents mailed in; the online form prompts for them at the end.
  • A previous Florida homestead may qualify you for portability of the Save Our Homes difference.

Filing late is allowed until the 25th day after the August notices go out, which lands in early September. A sold house means the new owner starts fresh: the buyer files for the following roll, and your exemption does not follow the deed.

What can I do if I disagree with a Duval value?

Start with an informal review at the appraiser's office, then file a DR-486 petition with the Value Adjustment Board if the answer does not satisfy you. The petition deadline is printed on the TRIM notice.

Duval changed one practical detail: if your petition asks for the property record card, the card is no longer mailed. It sits online in Property Search under the TRIM record card link, just below the notice section. Call 904-255-5900 if the page will not open or print.

The Board's page warns that petitioners generally have to pay 75 percent of the ad valorem tax, plus every non-ad valorem charge, before the usual April 1 delinquency date, or the petition can be denied. Ask the Board at (904) 255-5124 what your own figure is.

Do the aerial photos on the appraiser's site settle where my lot ends?

No. The appraiser says the imagery does not always show true boundaries and should not be relied on in a purchase. Hire a surveyor and a title company for any sale.

The same page says Florida law requires the office to inspect every property in the county at least once every five years, and that the staff do not enter the interior of homes. Appraisers drive marked vehicles, wear shirts with the city seal and carry City of Jacksonville identification, which is useful to know if someone knocks and claims to represent the office.

The images are also shared with the Jacksonville Sheriff's Office, Public Works and the Airport Authority, and Realtors and appraisers use them. For a seller, that means a buyer may have studied the roofline before the first showing.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

How can Duval owners watch for fake deeds?

The Duval Clerk runs a free Property Fraud Alert. You sign up with a personal or business name, and an alert comes within 48 hours after any document is recorded under that name in Duval County.

The county's pitch is simple: scammers file bogus deeds to pose as owners and then rent or sell homes that are not theirs. An empty or inherited Duval house is an easy target, so a seller holding a vacant property gains the most from enrolling.

Report suspected exemption fraud to the appraiser's hotline at (904) 255-7964. If the name on a family house's deed is that of someone who died, unresolved ownership can affect the homestead; the appraiser's page points to Jacksonville Area Legal Aid and LISC Jacksonville for heirs' property help and notes that probate or another legal process may be needed.

What changes when a Duval home hosts short stays?

Two obligations appear. Short-term transient rentals owe additional sales and use tax to the Tax Collector every month, and furnishings in a rental become taxable tangible personal property.

  • Airbnb, VRBO and similar sites do not send the tax to Duval for users, so the owner remits it. The appraiser's page lists TouristTax@coj.net for questions.
  • Household goods for an owner's own use are excluded, but furniture and appliances in any rental, short or long, count.
  • Anyone owning such property on January 1 files a return by April 1.

Renting the home also ends the homestead, which would raise the taxable value after the next January 1.

What should a Duval seller check before closing?

Ask the collector for a payoff on every open year, confirm the parcel matches the deed, and keep the closing statement. The state deed tax runs seventy cents for every hundred dollars of price, and the recording clerk takes it.

Older owners and veterans may hold separate benefits at the appraiser. A disabled ex-servicemember with 10 percent or more disability gets $5,000 off assessed value, and a deferral under Form DR-570 is filed with the collector by March 31. Ask whether a local older-owner exemption applies to your parcel.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

Where is the Duval County tax collector's main office?

It is at 231 E. Forsyth Street, Jacksonville, FL 32202, phone (904) 255-5700, open Monday to Friday from half past eight until half past four. A newer branch operates at 11160 Beach Blvd., Suite 121.

When were 2026 TRIM notices mailed in Duval County?

They went out Friday, August 14, 2026, according to the Property Appraiser. The petition deadline for the Value Adjustment Board is printed on each notice, so check your own.

Can I file for homestead online in Duval County?

Yes. Owners who moved into a Duval home after January 1, 2026 can use the online application for the 2027 roll. The timely deadline is March 1, 2027, and late filing runs to early September.

Does Airbnb collect Duval tourist tax for me?

No. The appraiser's page states that hosting sites do not remit tax directly to Duval County for any users, so the property owner must remit it to the Tax Collector's office.

How do I get notified if someone records a deed under my name?

Sign up for the Duval Clerk's free Property Fraud Alert at duvalclerk.gov. It watches a personal or business name and emails you within 48 hours of a matching recording.

Why is Pinellas an unusual place to hold a property tax bill?

Pinellas is small and crowded. The county reports 3,425 residents per square mile over 280 square miles, the densest in Florida, with only Union County smaller in land area. It runs 38 miles long, 15 miles at its widest and carries 588 miles of coastline, with 24 municipalities inside.

The property appraiser's roll shows what that density looks like on paper: 437,624 real property parcels, of which 408,947 are residential. Counting units rather than parcels, the office lists 241,442 single-family homes, 103,445 condos, 22,112 townhomes or PUD units, 44,323 manufactured homes and 101,180 multifamily rentals. A seller in a condo tower and one in a Largo manufactured home community deal with the same two offices, yet face very different assessments.

How large is the 2026 roll, and where does the money go?

The tax collector's own release for 2026 counts 495,057 accounts worth more than $2.75 billion. Collections are divided among 56 local taxing authorities, including the school board, the county commission, cities and libraries.

Three kinds of charges can appear on one notice. Ad valorem tax follows value. Tangible personal property tax covers furniture and equipment in businesses and rentals. Non-ad valorem assessments are fixed amounts for things like storm water, street lighting, fire and rescue and solid waste, and they do not depend on value.

The appraiser keeps ownership and mailing addresses, and the collector says it does not maintain them. If no bill arrives in November, the collector asks owners to phone 727-464-7777 or search its database, because an unreceived notice does not excuse payment.

What are the 2026 discount cutoffs for each payment method?

The cutoff depends on how you pay. Online payments run until 11:55 pm Eastern on the last discount day, while counter and drop box payments stop at closing time, and mailed checks need a postmark from that month.

Which payment routes does the Pinellas collector accept?

  • Online eChecks carry no fee but are not accepted for delinquent bills. Credit and debit cards add a 2.5 percent vendor fee.
  • Checks by mail are addressed to P.O. Box 31149, Tampa, FL 33631-3149. The collector warns that USPS now postmarks at a regional processing facility, so a late drop in a local box may miss a deadline.
  • Drop boxes sit outside select offices, and payment at an office needs no appointment.
  • Multiple checks must travel in one envelope, and an unpaid check is handled through a recovery partner that may re-present it with a fee.

Online payment shows as paid at once on the collector's system, though a bank can take up to five business days to reflect it. Bills were mailed starting October 30 for 2026, with online payment opening November 1 and counter and mail payment opening November 2.

Can Pinellas owners pay in four installments?

Yes. The plan serves owners with an estimated bill above $100 and carries a discount of roughly 3.5 percent overall. Applications for the 2027 plan open November 1, 2026 and run through April 30, 2027.

  • June 30: one quarter of last year's total, discounted 6 percent.
  • September 30: another quarter, discounted 4.5 percent.
  • December 31: a quarter plus half of any adjustment, discounted 3 percent.
  • March 31: a quarter plus the other half of the adjustment, with no discount.

A missed June payment can be made by July 31 without the discount, and missing July 31 removes the account. A late second or third payment rolls into the next one and loses its discount. Once enrolled, you do not reapply each year provided the first payment arrives.

What are partial payments and deferrals in Pinellas?

A partial payment plan lets owners pay current-year tax in pieces of at least $100, but only until March 31, and the early payment discounts are forfeited. Delinquent bills are not eligible. The 2026 application stays open through March 31, 2027, and a balance unpaid by May 31 goes to a certificate sale.

Deferral suits homestead holders, since it rests on the prior year's household income. The collector stresses that deferral creates a lien and that deferred tax accrues interest every month. The 2026 application deadline is March 31, 2027, and the office answers at 727-464-3409.

What did the vote on Amendment 3 mean for Pinellas bills?

The collector's release said Amendment 3 would not change 2026 bills, and that any change would begin with the 2027 tax year. Afterward, the Pinellas Property Appraiser's home page reported updating its website for the amendment's passage. For a buyer's estimate, check the appraiser's updated exemption pages before quoting next year's taxes.

Where are the Pinellas appraiser's offices?

The county courthouse office is at 315 Court Street, 2nd Floor, Clearwater. North County is at Northside Square, 29269 US Hwy 19 North, Clearwater. Mid County shares space with the tax collector at 13025 Starkey Rd, Largo, and South County is at 2500 34th Street North, 2nd Floor, St. Petersburg. The main line is (727) 464-3207, answered on weekdays.

What should a seller do if tax is still due in Pinellas?

Ask the collector for a payoff so the closing agent can settle it from proceeds. Delinquency begins April 1, and the collector lists its 2027 certificate sale for Friday, May 28, 2027, with online payments of 2026 taxes accepted until 5:00 pm on May 27. The title agent clears any certificate. The buyer's reassessment will not follow your old bill, and a homestead sale ends the cap, though portability may help your next home.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

How did Pinellas become its own county, and what is it like now?

A local referendum separated Pinellas from Hillsborough County, and it became the state's 48th county on January 1, 1912. The name is Spanish, Punta Pinal, or point of pines, a fair description when Panfilo de Narvaez arrived in 1528. Tarpon Springs was the first city incorporated, in 1887. Clearwater is the seat, and St. Petersburg is the largest city, with 258,201 residents as of 2021.

Getting around meant bridges. The Gandy Causeway of 1924 was the first span across Tampa Bay and cut the St. Petersburg to Tampa trip from 43 miles to 19. The Sunshine Skyway opened in 1954 and tied Pinellas to Manatee County. The county today reports roughly 4,500 miles of paved road, more than 400 bridges and 35 miles of beaches.

St. Petersburg bills itself the Sunshine City, with an average of 361 sunny days a year according to the county. Key employers fall into financial services, life science and medical technology, tourism, manufacturing, defense, aviation and information technology. A flight from St. Petersburg to Tampa in 1914 is recorded as the world's first scheduled airline service.

Frequently asked questions

Which office handles the Pinellas bill?

The tax collector mails and collects it. The property appraiser sets value and keeps the mailing address.

What is the 2026 Pinellas November discount?

It is 4 percent. December is 3, January 2 and February 1, with no discount in March.

What do Pinellas installments save?

The collector says about 3.5 percent overall, with discounts of 6, 4.5 and 3 percent on the first three quarters.

Can I make partial payments in Pinellas?

Yes, in amounts of at least $100 before April 1, but early payment discounts are lost.

Does Amendment 3 touch the 2026 Pinellas bill?

No. The collector said any change would begin with the 2027 tax year.

Who bills Lee County property tax, and who sets the value?

Lee County runs property tax through two desks. The appraiser answers anything about worth, exemptions and where mail goes (239-533-6100), while the collector answers anything about paying (239-533-6000).

Sellers hit this split at closing. Neither office can do the other's job: the collector will not alter a value or exemption, and the appraiser takes no payments. Questions about a special assessment for roads, fire, water or sewer go to the authority that levied it, whose contact details sit on the tax bill itself.

  • Appraiser: parcel records, value, exemption files, mailing address.
  • Collector: bills, receipts, quarterly and partial plans, deferral.
  • Clerk: deed recording, stamp tax, and the petition filings for value disputes.

What are the Lee County tax deadlines, and does early payment pay off?

Real estate bills in Lee County open for payment on November 1 and must be settled by March 31 of the next year. April 1 turns any balance delinquent.

The state's early-pay scale starts at 4 percent off for November and shrinks by a point each month through February. A lender still printed on the notice after a payoff does not block the November discount, the collector says. March payments get nothing off.

Every Lee city shares this one calendar, from Cape Coral to Sanibel. Six ways to pay exist: web, phone, mail, in person, kiosks, and 24-hour lockers at four centers. Late tax needs more secure funds than a personal check or eCheck, so line up certified money before a closing.

What payment plans does the Lee County Tax Collector offer?

Three options exist: quarterly installments, partial payments and homestead deferral. The installment plan closes first.

Lee County Tax Collector plans, from the office's payment options page
PlanApplyKey rule
Quarterly installmentsBy April 30 of the tax year (applications open November 1)Estimated tax must exceed $100 per notice; payments due June 30, September 30, December 31 and March 31
Partial paymentsNovember 1 to March 31Up to five payments per account; none online; no discounts
Homestead deferralBy March 31Age, income and lien rules apply; deferred tax becomes a lien and fire insurance is required

Discounts step down from 6 percent on installment one to 4.5 percent, then 3 percent, then nothing on the last. Skip the first payment past July 31 and the enrollment ends. Partial payments cover only the live tax year, never delinquent tax, and an owner already on installments cannot combine the two.

A sale midway through does not end the plan, since the incoming owner carries it to year end. Mention it to the closing agent early.

How do homestead and senior exemptions work in Lee County?

Homestead wipes out the first $25,000 of assessed value for every levy. A second slice, printed by the Lee appraiser as up to $26,411 for 2026, reaches only non-school levies on value over $50,000.

File Form DR-501 with the appraiser by March 1, online at leepa.org, by email to exemptions@leepa.org, by mail to PO Box 1546, Fort Myers, FL 33902, or in person at 2480 Thompson Street, 4th Floor, Fort Myers, on weekdays during business hours The office finishes processing by July 1. Save Our Homes, the cap on yearly assessment growth, starts the year after the grant.

Each Lee taxing body picks its own senior exemption amount for income-qualified owners aged 65 and over:

  • City of Sanibel, City of Bonita Springs and City of Fort Myers: $25,000.
  • City of Cape Coral: $50,000.
  • Town of Fort Myers Beach and Village of Estero: $50,000 and up to $250,000.
  • All Lee County millages: $50,000 and up to $250,000.

The appraiser also lists exemptions for disabled veterans, disabled first responders, surviving spouses, deployed service members, and $5,000 exemptions for widows, widowers, blind owners and others with disabilities. Most renew each January 1 unless ownership or residency changes.

What happens to a homestead exemption when you sell a Lee County house?

A buyer gets nothing automatically, so a new application is needed, and the seller's exemption drops off at the next turn of the year.

The appraiser warns that a TRIM notice showing homestead in the year of purchase reflects the seller's benefit, which will be removed. Sellers should also know that renting the property long term, or changing how title is held (certain trusts or LLCs), can end the exemption, and the office asks to be contacted when ownership changes in any manner.

If you move to another Florida home, homestead and the Save Our Homes portability benefit must be applied for again at the new address. Florida's state portability rule gives a three-year window counted from January 1 of the year the old homestead was given up, and the form is DR-501T filed by March 1.

How does a Lee County TRIM notice differ from the tax bill?

TRIM is the appraiser's mid-August preview. The bill, sent by the collector generally in November, is the real charge and the only one listing non-ad valorem items like garbage, fire or water.

The notice shows market value, exemptions, Save Our Homes status and proposed tax. A value dispute goes to the Value Adjustment Board within 25 days of the notice; a denied exemption has a separate 30 days from the denial letter. Keep both papers handy for buyers who ask about carrying costs.

On the Amendment 3 question, the collector's FAQ answers that it begins January 1, 2027 and leaves the 2026 bill alone. Millage differs by address across school, city and district levies, so rely on your parcel lookup and your own notice instead of any county average.

Who pays Lee County tax at a sale?

On the settlement statement the closing agent apportions the year between the two parties. The year's bill still goes to the owner of record when the roll reaches the collector, so a former owner may receive one.

Its advice: pass the bill to the new owner or the closing agent. A transfer is recorded with the clerk and then relayed to the appraiser, so lag is normal. Unpaid tax appears in the title search and is cleared from seller funds.

Lee County deeds carry the standard Florida stamp rate, 70 cents per $100 of consideration (Miami-Dade differs). Each party to the deed answers for it, and the clerk takes payment at recording.

Who lives in Lee County, and what are homes worth?

Lee County sits on the Gulf Coast and holds about 875,607 people by the Census Bureau's latest estimate, 15.1 percent more than in 2020, across 781 square miles.

Of 479,540 housing units, 74.3 percent are lived in by their owners, and for 2020 to 2024 the Census reports a $362,200 median home value and $76,107 in median household income. Residents 65 and over make up 29.2 percent of the population, which is one reason the senior exemptions above matter in sales. The county's municipalities named by the appraiser are Cape Coral, Fort Myers, Bonita Springs, Estero, Sanibel and Fort Myers Beach, and most owners outside those limits sit in unincorporated areas billed by the same offices.

Frequently asked questions

Is Lee County property tax due every year on the same dates?

Yes, the calendar repeats yearly: open November 1, due March 31, delinquent April 1, with a shrinking discount from 4 percent in November to 1 percent in February.

Can I still join the Lee County installment plan after April 30?

No. The window runs November 1 to April 30, and a late applicant is left with the partial plan, open through March 31.

Does the buyer get my homestead exemption in Lee County?

No. Buyers apply themselves. A TRIM notice listing homestead right after a purchase shows the seller's old benefit, which is removed.

Whom should I contact if my Lee County value looks wrong?

Ring the appraiser at 239-533-6100. A formal petition on a DR-486 form is lodged with the clerk inside 25 days of the proposed-tax notice.

What happens if Lee County property tax is unpaid when I sell?

The title company clears it from seller funds, along with any added charges. Because personal checks and eChecks are refused for late tax, ask the collector which funds it takes.

Who does what on a Pasco property tax bill?

Value, billing and appeals sit with three different elected offices. The appraiser sets values, the collector sends bills and takes payment, and the clerk staffs the appeals board and records the deed.

The Property Appraiser's homepage tallies 335,946 real property parcels: 206,994 single family, 11,888 condominium units, 11,347 commercial and 3,906 agricultural. The county covers 747 land square miles plus 122 of water. Its offices are in Dade City (352-521-4433), Land O' Lakes (813-929-2780) and New Port Richey (727-847-8151).

The Tax Collector lists offices in New Port Richey, Gulf Harbors, Land O'Lakes, Wesley Chapel and Dade City, with a sixth at Suncoast Parkway and SR 52 marked as coming soon. Its tax department answers at 352-521-4338, prompt 3.

  • Pasco County Property Appraiser: value, exemptions, taxing districts list, records search.
  • Pasco County Tax Collector: bills, online payment, installment plan, partial payment, delinquent taxes.
  • Pasco County Clerk and Comptroller: Value Adjustment Board petitions and the Official Records.

When are Pasco County property taxes due?

Pasco follows the statewide cycle of a November bill, a discount window through February and April 1 delinquency. The collector's pages add the local penalty and installment details below.

Pasco also offers an installment plan for estimated tax above one hundred dollars. For tax year 2027, the collector's page says forms are available beginning November 1, 2026, with a filing cutoff of April 30, 2027, and no applications accepted May 1 through October 31. Payments fall in June with a 6 percent discount, September with 4.5 percent, December with 3 percent and March with none. The first payment must arrive by July 31 or you are out of the plan. Each parcel needs its own application, and renewal after that is automatic.

A partial payment application also appears on the collector's menu. State law leaves partial payments before the delinquency date to the tax collector's discretion, so ask the office before sending less than the full bill.

Pasco County installment plan schedule as printed by the Tax Collector
PaymentMonth dueDiscount printed
FirstJune6 percent
SecondSeptember4.5 percent
ThirdDecember3 percent
FourthMarchNone

How does a Pasco County homestead exemption work?

One filing with the Property Appraiser by March 1 lowers the taxable value of your primary residence. The Tax Collector's own page says it does not handle homestead filings and sends owners to the appraiser, who takes applications year round but applies the March 1 cutoff.

The appraiser's exemptions menu is organized into six groups: Homestead, Disability, Veterans, Military and First Responders, Agriculture, Parent and Grandparent, and Senior Aged 65 and older. State rules put the base homestead benefit at up to $50,000, with the first $25,000 applying to school taxes and the second $25,000 reaching only value above $50,000 for non-school taxes. Some seniors can qualify for an added exemption if the county has adopted it and income falls under a limit; ask the appraiser whether Pasco has.

A sale or deed ends the capped assessment. Under state rules a change of ownership brings the parcel back to market value at the next valuation date, with exceptions such as transfers between spouses. The state's 2026 Save Our Homes cap is printed at 2.7 percent.

  • File by March 1 of the year you want the benefit, with the home already your permanent residence by January 1.
  • Renting the home or moving out ends eligibility.
  • A servicemember may rent out the homestead without losing it, under state law.

What other Pasco County resources help an owner who plans to sell?

Beyond the three main offices, the Tax Collector's menu links several pages worth a look before you list the house. They include a change of mailing address form, an electronic bill and receipt signup, instructions for printing a paid receipt, and a page on tax deed sales.

The Property Appraiser's site has a catastrophic event page and a taxing authorities and districts list. Pasco's appraiser also publishes a reporting page for possible homestead fraud. If you are selling because the house is storm-damaged or inherited, those pages explain what relief exists and which districts levy on your parcel.

  • Update your mailing address with the right office before you move so notices reach you.
  • Print the paid receipt for your closing file once the tax is cleared.
  • Use the taxing districts list to see which local districts tax your parcel.

What follows if a Pasco County tax bill is not paid?

The bill becomes delinquent on April 1 with a late penalty, then a lien is sold, and after two years the property can go to public auction. The Pasco Tax Collector's delinquent page gives each step.

It states a late penalty of 3 percent of the tax amount added on April 1, followed by advertising charges. By the first of June a tax certificate, a claim against the parcel, is issued for the unpaid tax, penalties and costs. Interest on the certificate runs from a minimum of 5 percent to a maximum of 18 percent. If the taxes remain unpaid after two years, the property may be sold at public auction.

For delinquent bills the collector wants a money order, cashier's check or wire, and takes cash only at its offices. A personal or business check comes back, and the delay can add interest. Attorney, title company and mortgage broker escrow checks are accepted.

State law also bars a certificate buyer from contacting you to demand payment for two years after April 1 of the year the certificate was issued, so an early call from a stranger about your lien is a red flag.

How is the tax settled when a Pasco County house sells?

The closing agent deducts what is owed on the parcel, so you rarely walk a check to the collector yourself.

The collector's recent purchases page explains the follow-up. The appraiser reports ownership changes through the year; unpaid tax produces a duplicate notice to the new owner, and delinquent tax a reminder. The page also notes that the owner shown on the website is the owner as assessed on the certified tax roll, which is usually finished in early October.

Outside Miami-Dade the state deed tax runs 70 cents per $100 of price, and each party to the deed is on the hook whoever agrees to pay. Pasco's clerk quotes a recording charge in its FAQ, covered on our Pasco records guide.

The buyer's side changes too. Because a sale resets assessed value, the new owner's bill can be well above the seller's capped bill. Anyone buying to live in the house files for homestead by the next March 1.

What if I think my Pasco assessment is too high?

Talk to the Property Appraiser first, then petition the Value Adjustment Board, which the Pasco Clerk and Comptroller staffs, if you still disagree. Board petitions carry a non-refundable $50.00 filing fee under the clerk's FAQ.

The clerk lists two exceptions: a portability petition on the DR-486PORT form costs $15.00, and a petition over a denied homestead application, deployed military exemption or tax deferral has no fee. State rules allow 25 days from the proposed-tax notice for a value petition and 30 days from a mailed denial letter for exemption denials. That notice arrives in August, and the dates printed on it control.

Business equipment and rental furnishings fall under a tangible personal property return, which the appraiser's site covers on its own page. If you rent the house before selling, ask the appraiser whether one applies.

Frequently asked questions

Which Pasco County office takes my tax payment?

The Pasco County Tax Collector collects it, through five working offices and an online portal. Tax questions go to 352-521-4338, prompt 3. The Property Appraiser sets value and exemptions but takes no payments.

What does late Pasco County tax cost?

The Tax Collector's page says a 3 percent late penalty is added on April 1, followed by advertising charges. A tax certificate is issued on or before June 1, carrying interest between 5 percent and 18 percent.

Does Pasco County offer a payment plan?

Yes, when the estimated tax tops one hundred dollars. The 2027 plan needs an application by April 30, 2027. Payments fall in June, September, December and March, and the first must arrive by July 31.

Does a Pasco homestead pass to the buyer?

No, it stays with the owner. The buyer files by March 1, and the sale moves the assessed value up to market level at the next valuation date.

Can I sell a Pasco County house with delinquent taxes?

Yes. Delinquent tax, with any certificate redemption costs, is settled from your proceeds before the deed passes. The payoff figure comes from the Tax Collector's tax department.

Why does a Polk County tax bill look different from other Florida bills?

Because Polk packs a long list of local levies into one statement. Along with county and school millage, a parcel can carry fire, garbage, lighting, roadway and community district charges, and the Tax Collector publishes the full roster of who bills for what.

That matters when you sell. A buyer who only compares the headline value of two houses can miss the line items that follow a particular street or subdivision. If you are listing in Polk, learn which of those lines your parcel carries before the first showing, and put the answer in your listing notes.

  • The Property Appraiser at polkflpa.gov sets value and handles exemptions.
  • The Tax Collector at polktaxes.com sends and collects the bill.
  • Each taxing body named on the bill answers questions about its own rate or assessment.

Where does Polk County sit, and does location change a sale?

Polk lies between the Orlando and Tampa metro areas along the I-4 corridor, and the county's own welcome page describes the north as quickly urbanizing and the land south of State Road 60 as ranch and scrub. County news releases are datelined Bartow.

The split shows up on the bill. A house in a newer northern neighborhood is more likely to sit inside a district created for roads, drainage or amenities. A rural parcel in the south tends to have fewer special charges but may depend on a private well or septic system, which a buyer's inspector will check.

The appraiser's statistics page counts 231,135 single family parcels and 329,750 housing units countywide, so comparable sales in your own subdivision are usually easy to find. Use the parcel map search to confirm exactly which taxing areas touch your lot.

Who levies what on a Polk County bill?

The Tax Collector's taxing authorities page sorts the levies into groups, summarized below. Call the body listed for a line you do not recognize.

Sample of levies on the Polk County Tax Collector's taxing authorities page
GroupItems named
Board of County Commissioners, ad valoremGeneral revenue, environmental land acquisition, library MSTU, parks MSTU, stormwater MSTU

Ad valorem items follow your assessed value. Assessments follow a service, a district or a lien, so they can stay the same even when value drops.
