How do community development district charges affect a Polk buyer?

They add a yearly assessment that a buyer inherits, so you should disclose it. The Tax Collector's list names dozens of community development districts, among them Lake Ashton, Silverlake, Poinciana, Eagle Hammock, Towne Park and Westside Haines City, along with Haines City Water Control, West Lakeland Water Control and the Tohopekaliga Water Authority.

If your subdivision shows up on that list, your bill likely carries a non-ad valorem line that does not shrink when your home value does. Buyers and their lenders will count it as part of monthly cost.

  1. Find the district name on your tax bill or in the Tax Collector's parcel search.
  2. Ask the district manager for the current assessment and any remaining balance.
  3. Hand that figure to the closing agent so the payoff or proration is right.

PACE programs appear on the same list. A PACE assessment attaches to the property, so a seller who used one should get the balance in writing before accepting an offer.

Which exemptions can Polk homeowners claim?

Homestead is the main one, and it takes a permanent residence on January 1 plus an application by early March. The appraiser's exemption page says it cuts as much as $50,000 from the taxable base, and filing is free.

  • Senior exemption: homeowners 65 and older under the household income limit, with Polk granting the larger amount.
  • Long-time resident exemption: 25 years in the home and a just value under $250,000, applied to county general millage.
  • $5,000 reductions for widows or widowers, disability and service-connected disability.
  • Total and permanent disability and first responder exemptions for eligible owners.

Approvals renew on their own each year, and only a denial arrives by letter. A seller who leaves Polk for another Florida home can carry assessment savings forward with the portability form, up to $500,000, as the state revenue agency explains.

Can Polk owners spread payments or put off the bill?

Yes, through two programs run by the Tax Collector. Both have firm paperwork dates, so decide well before a sale.

The installment plan needs an application by April 30 of that tax year, and the prior bill must have topped $100. Once you are enrolled, the office re-enrolls you automatically. If the property sells mid-plan, check with the collector how the remaining payments pass to the buyer.

Homestead deferral is meant for owners with low income relative to the bill. The collector's page lists four tests: household income under $10,000 allows deferral of everything, taxes above 5% of income can be deferred beyond that share, owners 65 and older can defer beyond 3%, and older owners under the additional exemption income limit may defer the whole amount. Deferral is barred if deferred amounts and liens exceed 85% of just value or the primary mortgage exceeds 70% of just value. Form DR-570 goes to the collector by the end of March after the assessment year.

Deferred taxes build up as a lien, so expect them to come out of sale proceeds at closing.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What follows a missed Polk deadline?

Delinquency begins April 1, and a certificate sale on unpaid parcels takes place by June 1. Bidders start at 18% interest and bid downward, and a redemption costs at least a 5% charge.

A certificate is a lien held by an investor, not a transfer of title. The holder may apply for a tax deed once two years have passed counted from the April 1 that followed issue, and the Clerk of the Courts runs the auction. Until the sale, the record owner may pay all taxes, interest, fees and costs and keep the property. Ask the collector for a written payoff before listing, since the number grows.

What changes for the buyer after a Polk sale?

The county reassesses the parcel at just value on the following New Year's Day, so the buyer's first bill can run well above yours. Transfers between spouses are among the listed exceptions. Your homestead cap does not move with the house.

The deed stamp rate in Polk is the statewide 70 cents per $100, and the state holds every signer of the deed responsible whoever the contract names as payer. The clerk collects it at recording. The state's cap chart shows 2.7% for 2026 and 2.9% for 2025 as the limit on homestead assessment growth.

Because TRIM notices arrive in August and final rates are set by the autumn, your closing agent will prorate the year using the best figures on hand. If rates change later, the contract language decides who covers the difference.

Frequently asked questions

Is Polk County property tax billed in advance or after the year ends?

It is billed in November for the current calendar year, after rates are set that autumn. Taxes are collected for the year just assessed, and the discount runs 4% in November down to 1% in February.

When do Polk County taxes go delinquent?

April 1. A tax certificate sale on unpaid parcels follows by June 1, and the Tax Collector adds interest and an advertising charge to delinquent accounts.

Can I defer Polk County homestead taxes?

Possibly. Send Form DR-570 to the Tax Collector before March ends in the year after assessment. Eligibility turns on household income, age and how much debt and liens already sit against the home.

Do I need to reapply for Polk homestead every year?

No. Once approved, homestead renews on its own and only a denial is mailed. File a new application if you buy a different Polk home or if the use of the property changes.

What is a CDD charge on my Polk County bill?

It is an assessment from a community development district that financed local infrastructure. It appears as a non-ad valorem item, stays attached to the parcel after a sale, and should be confirmed with the district before closing.

What does Brevard County look like to someone about to sell?

Brevard stretches along the central Florida east coast for 72 miles from north to south and holds roughly 600,000 residents. The county's own profile counts 16 municipalities and names two anchors that shape local demand, Kennedy Space Center and Patrick Space Force Base.

A seller in Titusville, Melbourne, Palm Bay or a small beachside city is therefore dealing with very different local governments under one county tax system. The county itself mainly serves people who live outside city limits, and the commission has five districts. The tax bill, though, runs on county rails wherever the house sits.

Which Brevard government handles permits, and which handles tax?

Permits depend on the address, while tax billing does not. For unincorporated land, county government issues building permits, reviews plans, enforces code, maintains local roads and bridges and supplies utilities. Inside a city, the city does most of that.

  • County services that reach everyone include 9-1-1 and emergency medical services, emergency management, mosquito control, libraries and parks.
  • Value comes from the appraiser's office, and the collector's office sends the bills and takes the money.
  • The county reports about 2,350 employees across 24 offices, none of which sets your assessed value.

The county's profile also lists a Valkaria Airport, a Natural Resources Management office and a Solid Waste Management office among its departments, a reminder that unincorporated owners deal with the county for services that city residents get from city hall.

Before a pre-sale repair, confirm which jurisdiction issues the permit. The mailing address on the tax bill can name a city that differs from the one that governs the lot.

What does the Brevard tax collector's year look like?

The collector publishes a calendar by month, and its discounts run on the postmark. Here are the entries a seller is likely to need.

Can a Brevard owner pay in quarterly installments?

Yes, when estimated tax is above $100. The collector's plan splits the year into four payments, due by June 30, September 30, December 31 and March 31, with the application, Form DR-534, due before May 1.

The June and September payments are figured from last year's gross tax. Changes from new value or exemptions are folded into the December and March payments after the roll is certified. Once enrolled and current, an owner does not reapply each year, as long as the first payment lands by June 30. If it has not arrived by July 31, participation is cancelled.

The collector warns that anyone with a mortgage escrow account should not use installments, because the lender pays in November to capture the largest discount. Questions go to (321) 264-6969, and the form goes to the collector at P.O. Box 2500, Titusville, FL 32781-2500. Any amount still unpaid on April 1 follows the normal delinquency rules.

What are the payment methods and fees in Brevard?

Standard bills are mailed by November 1, and the collector asks owners to call if nothing has arrived by the second week of November. Installment payers get bills quarterly, in June, September, December and March. A duplicate can be mailed on request.

  • E-checks made online are free, and a payment sent in error can be reversed by calling before 5:00 pm that day.
  • Credit and debit cards, Apple Pay and Google Pay carry a 2.75 percent fee with a $2.75 minimum. International cards are 3.95 percent. A third-party vendor keeps the fee.
  • A returned check draws a service charge under s. 68.065: $25 under $50, $30 from $50 to $299.99, $40 from $300 to $799.99, and 5 percent at $800 or more.
  • Wire payments must name the tax account number, the owner and the property ID, and cover all bank fees.

The collector adds that a current mailing address on file protects against ownership problems, which matters most for an owner who has already moved out.

What happens in Brevard when a bill is left unpaid?

In May, the late list for real estate is printed in a local paper on three consecutive weeks, and the ad cost plus an electronic fee land on the owner's balance. Certificates go up for sale as early as June 1 or soon after. Business property that is late gets one May listing, and warrants follow July 1.

A holder who has waited out the statutory period may then apply for a deed (s. 197.502). On a homestead, the opening bid includes half of the last assessed value, and a homestead balance under $250 is issued to the county, never auctioned.

Can the sale close while Brevard tax is unpaid?

Back taxes will not block a closing. The title agent still needs the collector's payoff and any certificate costs, so request them early. A sold certificate has to be redeemed at the table.

A deed to the buyer also resets the parcel to just value January 1, which ends the homestead growth limit, so the buyer's first bill can sit far above yours. Someone moving to another Florida house should ask about portability and Form DR-501T.

Who handles a value dispute or exemption question in Brevard?

Start with the Brevard County Property Appraiser, who answers at (321) 264-6700 per the collector's page. If the record misstates something simple, such as the bedroom count, a phone call may settle it. Formal petitions use the DR-486 forms, filed with the clerk inside 25 days of the August notice, or 30 days after an exemption denial letter.

Homestead applications are due March 1. The collector's home page has flagged Amendment 3, a homestead exemption ballot item, so check the appraiser's site for current exemption amounts before you quote a buyer next year's taxes.

What relief programs might an older or veteran Brevard owner ask about?

Several programs depend on local adoption, so ask the appraiser which apply in Brevard and your city.

  • Residents 65 and older: an ordinance may add as much as $50,000 for qualifying household income.
  • Disabled ex-servicemembers: a $5,000 assessed value reduction.
  • Veterans past 65 with a lasting service-related disability: a homestead discount tied to the VA percentage.
  • Homestead tax deferral: the collector lists March 31 as the filing deadline.

What do heirs in Brevard need to check before listing?

Heirs lose the exemption once the owner is gone. Call the appraiser to learn how the transfer is treated, since certain transfers at death escape the ownership reset, and pull a payoff from the collector before the sign goes up.

Frequently asked questions

Which Brevard office mails the tax notice?

The tax collector mails the November bill. The property appraiser mails the proposed tax notice in August.

What is the Brevard delinquency date?

April 1. Taxes unpaid then become delinquent, and certificates are offered on or before June 1.

What is the minimum for the Brevard installment plan?

Estimated tax must exceed $100, and the application on Form DR-534 must reach the collector before May 1.

Do mortgage escrow owners use installments in Brevard?

No. The collector says lenders pay in November to capture the discount, so installments are not for escrow accounts.

Is the Brevard discount based on postmark?

Yes, the collector's calendar says discounts are based on postmark, with 4 percent through November 30.

What does Volusia County look like on paper?

Land area in Volusia County is 1,101.31 square miles. The 2020 census found 553,543 people, against 494,593 ten years earlier, and the mid-2025 estimate of 606,573 sits 9.6 percent above the 2020 base. Age stands out: 27.3 percent of the population has passed 65, and 46,354 residents are veterans.

The 2020 to 2024 survey counted 241,881 households, and owners occupy 73.7 percent of the homes. The midpoint owner home is valued at $313,000 and gross rent at the midpoint is $1,467. Builders pulled 2,826 permits in 2025. The numbers above are drawn from the Census Bureau's county profile. With so many older owners and veterans, the exemption categories further down are worth reading before any sale.

How does a Volusia County parcel travel from value to bill?

Three hand-offs turn a parcel into a bill. The property appraiser sets value and decides exemptions, and the county council, school board, city commissions and other levying bodies choose millage. In the collector's definition, one mill means a single dollar levied per $1,000 of value.

Once the appraiser finishes the roll and the Department of Revenue approves it, the appraiser certifies it to the tax collector, who mails each notice to the owner's last address of record. The collector also describes ad valorem tax as paid in arrears, because the year runs January 1 to December 31 and the bill arrives after it ends. You get one bill per parcel, following how the deed was recorded. The appraiser mails a Notice of Proposed Taxes in August, listing value and hearing dates.

What should a Volusia County owner do when a bill never arrives?

Ask for it. Section 197.122 puts three duties on the owner: know that tax is due each year, find out the amount, and pay before delinquency. A lost envelope is no defense.

Annual bills leave by November 1. Call the collector if yours is not in hand by mid-month. Installment participants get quarterly statements in June, September, December and March instead. A parcel whose taxes run through a lender escrow gets an informational notice saying the original went to the escrow trustee. After a move or a sale, update the mailing address on the appraiser's records, which the collector says the appraiser maintains along with the legal description.

Which dates frame the Volusia County tax year?

Last business day of May, 4:30 p.m.Cutoff to pay in an office and avoid a certificate

Source: Volusia County Tax Collector, important dates. The 4, 3, 2 and 1 percent discounts run November through February; March carries none. A payment postmarked after April 1 is priced by the day the office receives it.

How do installment payments work in Volusia County?

The plan is open to owners whose estimated tax tops $100, with the estimate taken from last year's gross tax. The Form DR-534 is available November 1 through April 30 and must reach the office at 123 W. Indiana Ave., Room 103, DeLand, before May 1.

Four quarterly statements follow. June and September amounts rest on the prior year's tax, and any change from new value or exemptions is trued up in December and March once the roll is certified. If the first payment is made by June 30, the owner does not reapply next year. Call the office if the first notice has not arrived by June 15. Anything still unpaid on April 1 is handled as a delinquent real estate tax. Mortgage borrowers should not enroll, since lenders must pay in November to earn the maximum discount.

Can a Volusia County owner make a partial payment?

Yes, before April 1, on real and business property, with a sworn affidavit mailed along with the check. A partial payment is anything below the full amount due.

  • Installment accounts cannot use it.
  • No discount applies once an agreement with the collector exists.
  • Whatever remains unpaid on April 1 becomes delinquent and is due in full.
  • A balance still open at 4:30 p.m. on May's last business day in a collector office puts a lien certificate on the parcel.

How does a tax certificate sale run in Volusia County?

The sale is held online through LienHub by June 1, and certificate information posts there in mid-May. Before it, a list of delinquent parcels is advertised once a week for three weeks, starting at the north end of the county and working south in parcel order. The paper lists more parcels than will sell, because payments arrive after the list is built.

Cost to a buyer covers the gross tax, a 3 percent fee, advertising and sale costs. A winning bid cannot exceed 18 percent simple interest and pays at least 5 percent unless bid at zero. Interest begins accruing the month after issue. Unsold parcels become county held at the top rate.

To clear the lien, an owner pays the certificate amount plus the sold rate through the redemption month, and a $6.25 fee applies from June 1. Payment may be cash, guaranteed funds or a debit or credit card. A certificate lasts seven years and can be sold between investors for a $2.25 recording fee. A buyer is forbidden to press the owner for payment during the first two years, and the collector can bar one who tries.

What must a certificate holder do before Volusia County sets a tax deed sale?

After two years, a holder who wants a deed applies through LienHub, and one certificate is enough. The collector's example counts from taxes that went delinquent April 1, 2021, which allowed an application after April 1, 2023.

The applicant first pays the redemption amounts on all other certificates, any omitted or delinquent taxes, current taxes if due, and statutory fees including an application fee and a title search fee. The Clerk of the Circuit Court administers the auction itself, and the collector refers questions there. A homeowner who spots a certificate on the parcel can still redeem it with the collector before a sale takes place.

Which exemption categories does the Volusia County appraiser list?

The appraiser's exemption page names twelve groupings and gives the records department's number, 386-736-5901, for questions.

  • Homestead, senior, disability, veteran, and widow or widower.
  • Granny flat and first responder.
  • Religious, literary, charitable and educational property.
  • Conservation, economic development and historical.
  • Agricultural classification.

Homestead is the largest. The state sets it at up to $50,000 in two layers, only the first of which touches school levies; the homestead guide adds a March 1 filing close and a January 1 residence test. The benefit belongs to one owner. After a sale, the home returns to market value the next January 1.

What should a Volusia County seller settle before closing?

Put the payoff in writing from the tax collector, with a figure good through closing. Because the year is paid in arrears, a closing in July leaves half the year's tax unbilled, and the contract decides who covers it.

Check the parcel's balance and any certificate on the collector's search first. The revenue department's stamp page gives seventy cents per $100 of price; settle in the contract which side funds it. If a tax deed application may exist on a certificate older than two years, ask the clerk as well.

Frequently asked questions

Until what day can Volusia owners pay with no penalty?

March 31. Weekend or holiday deadlines roll forward for in person and online payments, but the 3 percent charge starts April 1.

Is there a Volusia County discount if I pay in December?

Yes, 3 percent. November pays 4 percent, January 2 percent, February 1 percent and March none.

Can I redeem a certificate on my Volusia County home by card?

Yes. The collector takes cash, cashier's or certified checks, money orders and credit or debit cards, and the owner owes the rate bid at the sale.

How soon can a Volusia County certificate become a deed application?

Two years after the delinquency date that year. The holder files online with the tax deed vendor, LienHub.

Who should I call in Volusia County about exemptions?

The property appraiser's records department at 386-736-5901. The collector handles bills, installments and deferral filings.

Which Sarasota County office does what with your tax bill?

Two elected offices split the job. The property appraiser at 2001 Adams Lane in Sarasota decides what your parcel is worth and who gets an exemption, and the tax collector mails the bill and takes the money. The rate itself is voted by each taxing body, and neither office controls it.

On the collector's site the real estate notice is described as a single document that merges ad valorem taxes with non-ad valorem assessments, with fire protection and solid waste given as examples. Personal property tied to a business gets its own ad valorem only bill. If the mail brings nothing by mid-November, the collector asks to hear from you and also offers a printable copy online.

Links on the collector's page point to four municipal sites: Sarasota, North Port, Venice and Longboat Key. Counter locations are listed for downtown Sarasota, Venice, North Port and Mid County. Related pages here: Sarasota, North Port and Venice.

What are the Sarasota County tax dates for payment and delinquency?

Bills open for payment on November 1 and the gross amount is due by March 31. Whatever is still unpaid on April 1 is delinquent. The collector gives a plain example: 2025 tax not paid by then went delinquent on April 1, 2026.

Discounts step down by month: 4 percent for November, 3 for December, 2 for January, 1 for February. Lenders that collect escrow must pay within the 4 percent month, per the collector. For 2026, the appraiser certified the roll on September 29 and the collector reports bills mailed or emailed by October 30.

Hardship tools exist at state level. An owner can ask the collector for an installment plan by May 1 of the assessment year, and a homestead owner may file Form DR-570 for a deferral by March 31.

Key dates published by the Sarasota County Property Appraiser and Tax Collector
DateWhat it means
January 1Valuation date and the day exemption eligibility is judged
March 1Last timely day for homestead, senior, disability and nonprofit filings
April 1Tangible personal property returns due; earlier-year tax delinquent
June 1Income papers due for the extra senior exemption
July 1Disapproval notices mailed
Mid-AugustTRIM notices mailed, 2026 on August 17
First week of OctoberCertified roll goes to the collector

How can a Sarasota County owner contest a value?

Talk to the appraiser first if you like, but you are free to file with the Value Adjustment Board or sue in circuit court without doing so. The appraiser's page lists all three paths and says they need not be taken in order.

A value petition is due 25 days after the TRIM mailing, a date printed on your notice. After a denied exemption or denied assessment transfer, you get 30 days from the letter's mailing date. The Clerk to the Value Adjustment Board answers filing questions at (941) 861-5279.

Disagree with the board's ruling? A circuit court claim may be filed within 60 days of roll certification. Remember the board looks at value, classification and exemption only. If the tax rate bothers you, speak up at the budget hearing printed on the notice.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

What should you bring when you dispute a Sarasota County value?

Documents win these discussions. The appraiser says most issues end in informal talks, and offers sales comparisons and damage records as examples of helpful proof.

  • Your TRIM notice and parcel number.
  • Closing figures for similar houses sold close by.
  • Contractor estimates or photographs for storm or structural damage.
  • Residency papers if a homestead was denied.

The appraiser's phone is 941.861.8200. Hurricane damage has its own page on the appraiser's site.

How does the Sarasota County tax roll move from estimate to bill?

The appraiser's calendar ties each step to a Florida statute. It starts in June and ends in the spring after the bills go out.

  • By June 1: estimates of taxable value go to each taxing authority (s. 200.065(8)).
  • July 1: the appraiser certifies taxable value to each authority.
  • Within 55 days of that certification, which the page puts at August 24: TRIM notices go out by first class mail.
  • Within 101 days of certification: each authority certifies its final adopted millage to the appraiser and the state revenue department.
  • First week of October: the certified roll is delivered to the collector and the state.
  • March or April: the appraiser tells each authority how the Value Adjustment Board and corrections changed the roll.

The sequence explains why a TRIM notice shows proposed rates while the November bill shows adopted ones. Hearing dates for each authority's tentative budget appear on the TRIM notice, which is why the appraiser points rate complaints to those meetings. Keep the notice until the final bill arrives so you can compare the two.

Which exemptions can shrink a Sarasota County bill?

Homestead leads the list. You need to live in the house as your permanent home on January 1 and apply by March 1, although the office reviews late filings.

State figures describe homestead as up to $50,000, with $25,000 reaching school taxes. Afterward, Save Our Homes caps yearly growth at 3 percent or CPI, whichever is lower. The appraiser's guide adds:

  • $5,000 for a widow or widower who has not remarried.
  • $5,000 for total and permanent disability.
  • $5,000 for blindness.
  • $5,000 for a veteran rated at least 10 percent disabled.
  • A homestead discount matching the VA percentage for veterans 65 and over with a permanent combat-related disability.

The collector says voter-approved Amendment 3 reaches the 2027 bill and leaves the 2026 bill as issued.

What follows when Sarasota County tax stays unpaid?

A tax certificate is sold, and eventually a certificate holder can ask for a deed. The collector's own wording is blunt: nonpayment can mean losing the property.

Certificates go on sale by June 1. Bidding is on interest, lowest wins, in quarter-point steps (s. 197.432). A deed application can come two years after April 1 of the issue year, with a $75 fee (s. 197.502). Winning bidders at the clerk's sale put down the larger of 5 percent or $200 (s. 197.542). Our tax deed page goes deeper.

An owner who is behind can pay through closing; the title agent asks the collector for the balance.

How is Sarasota County tax handled at a sale?

The buyer answers to the collector for the whole bill. Between buyer and seller, the closing statement credits the buyer for the months the seller held title, and nothing is wired to the collector as a seller part-payment.

Mailing matters afterward. Tell the appraiser where to send your notices once you move, and forward any real estate bill for a house you sold. Business equipment is different: if you held it on January 1, that year's bill remains yours. Recording details sit in our Sarasota County records guide.

Frequently asked questions

When is Sarasota County property tax due?

Payment opens November 1, and the tax is delinquent after March 31. Early-pay discounts are 4 percent in November, 3 in December, 2 in January and 1 in February.

Where can I pay what I owe in Sarasota County?

Use the Sarasota County Tax Collector, through its website payment options or at offices in downtown Sarasota, Venice, North Port or Mid County.

Can I appeal my Sarasota County value?

Yes, with a Value Adjustment Board petition filed within 25 days of the TRIM mailing. A denied exemption allows 30 days from the denial letter.

Who pays the tax bill when a house sells?

The buyer answers to the collector. The seller's months are credited to the buyer on the closing statement.

What if I cannot pay in full?

Ask the collector about an installment plan, which needs an application by May 1 of the assessment year, or a homestead deferral on Form DR-570 by March 31.

Who sends the Manatee County property tax bill?

Two Manatee County offices split the job: the property appraiser sets the value and the tax collector sends and collects the bill. In the collector's own words, the appraiser mails each year's TRIM notice, the collector mails the bill, and the money then flows to the local taxing authorities.

That split matters when you plan a sale. A question about an exemption, a parcel record or an assessed value goes to the Manatee County Property Appraiser. A question about what is owed, which discount applies or whether a certificate has been issued goes to the Manatee County Tax Collector. The clerk of court, at manateeclerk.com, keeps the Official Records where deeds and liens are recorded.

  • Property appraiser: parcel search, homestead e-filing, tangible personal property returns, TRIM notices, value reviews and Value Adjustment Board information.
  • Tax collector: bills, payments, installment plans, delinquent accounts and the annual tax certificate sale.
  • Clerk: recorded deeds, mortgages and liens, plus tax deed sales run for the county.

When do Manatee County property taxes have to be paid?

Manatee bills go out in early November, and the discount shrinks month by month until the gross amount comes due on March 31. The tax collector's page describes the 2026 roll as opening for collection with the November 2 mailing of 220,594 annual bills and informational notices.

The collector prints a month-by-month discount schedule, shown below for the 2026 bills. Its deadline rule has three parts: in person by 5:00 p.m., postmarked, or paid online by 11:59 p.m.

Discount periods for annual payment of 2026 Manatee County bills, as printed by the Tax Collector
Payment windowDiscount
November 2 to December 34%
December 4 to December 313%
January 1 to January 312%
February 1 to February 281%
March 1 to March 31No discount, last day before delinquency

The state's revenue department describes the same ladder.

Can Manatee County owners pay in installments?

Yes. Under section 197.222 of the Florida Statutes, the tax collector offers a plan of four quarterly payments, and the prior year's taxes must have exceeded $100 to join. State guidance puts the application deadline at May 1 of the assessment year.

Manatee's installment page prints this ladder:

  • June 30, first installment: 6% discount. A first installment paid by July 31 earns no discount.
  • September 30, second installment: 4.5% discount.
  • December 31, third installment: 3% discount.
  • March 31, fourth installment: no discount, and the last day before delinquency.

A seller partway through a plan year should tell the collector, since the closing payoff must cover whatever remains.

Does the Manatee County Tax Collector send reminders?

Yes. The collector offers free property tax email alerts that go out when taxes are due, when a payment posts, when a discount period is about to end and when taxes turn delinquent. A tutorial on its site explains the signup, and a separate management page lets you change or delete alerts.

Sellers can use this during a listing period. An alert on a parcel you are about to sell confirms that a payment posted before the closing agent orders a payoff. The collector's help center also carries checklists and answers for a visit to the office, and the office lists appointments on its website.

Escrow customers should confirm with their servicer who is paying, since a lender payment and an owner payment can overlap.

What happens if Manatee County taxes are not paid?

Anything unpaid after March 31 turns delinquent on April 1 and can pick up fees, interest and collection costs. From then on, the collector counts a payment only when it is received by the month's last business day, and postmarks do not count.

Florida's revenue department says certificates are sold on all unpaid items by June 1. Manatee's collector runs one annual sale and issues a certificate against any parcel still unpaid at that point, and paying the taxes cancels it. Certificates that nobody buys at the sale default to the county, and investors can buy those later from the county-held list.

A certificate is not a deed. Under section 197.502, a holder who waits out two years can ask for a tax deed, and the collector then lists the owner, lienholders and any contract-for-deed buyer for notice. A homestead property carries a higher opening bid, because one-half of the latest assessed value is added.

Which exemptions can lower a Manatee County bill?

Manatee owners apply for exemptions at the property appraiser, whose website offers electronic filing for homestead. Paper work is Form DR-501, and the state sets the first deadline in early March.

  • Homestead takes up to $50,000 off taxable value. Only the first $25,000 reduces school taxes.
  • Once a home is homesteaded, a state cap limits how fast its assessed value can climb. The state's published chart shows 2.7% for 2026.
  • Investment and second-home parcels face a different ceiling of 10 percent a year.
  • Portability lets a long-time homesteader carry that cap benefit to a new home, using Form DR-501T.
  • Homestead tax deferral goes through the tax collector, on Form DR-570, for owners who qualify.

Renting the home out or moving away ends homestead. The appraiser also takes reports of suspected exemption fraud through a confidential form.

How can a Manatee County owner dispute a value?

Begin with the August TRIM notice. The Manatee appraiser's homepage invites owners who believe a value is wrong to request a review of their property data and assessed value, and it links the Value Adjustment Board page for owners who want a formal hearing.

The state's revenue department puts the formal petition clock at 25 days from the notice date, with one of the DR-486 forms filed through the clerk. A turned-down exemption has its own 30-day clock. Both are counted from mailing dates printed on the paper you receive, so read it the day it arrives.

Business owners with tangible personal property report to the appraiser each year by April 1 and can request a 30-day extension from the same office.

What happens to the Manatee County tax bill at a sale?

An open bill rarely stops a sale. The closing agent can settle it out of what the buyer pays, and the title company can order the payoff. The collector confirms the account standing and any certificate. Treat a certificate as a title issue to settle early.

The state's deed stamp rate is 70 cents for each $100 of price, taken by the clerk as the deed goes on record. A cash sale shortens the timeline, since no lender appraisal or underwriting has to finish first, and it leaves the tax items as they were.

Where a parcel already carries back taxes or a deed application, get the figure from the collector in writing before the closing date is set.

Will the next owner pay the same Manatee County tax?

Probably not. The seller's capped assessment ends with the sale, and the parcel moves to full market-based value the next January. A buyer who budgets from the old bill can be surprised.

The appraiser's site publishes the preliminary roll, reports and earlier years' millage for anyone who wants to compare. For the rate on one address, ask the collector or appraiser, since each taxing authority sets its own.

Frequently asked questions

Who answers questions about a Manatee County tax bill?

The Manatee County Tax Collector handles bills, payments, installments and delinquent accounts. The property appraiser handles values and exemptions, and the clerk handles recorded deeds and liens.

Does Manatee County reward early payment?

Yes. The collector's schedule for the 2026 bills gives 4% from November 2 to December 3, 3% from December 4 to December 31, 2% in January and 1% in February. March has no discount.

When do Manatee County taxes become delinquent?

April 1. Unpaid parcels then go into the collector's yearly certificate sale, and paying the taxes cancels a certificate.

Can a Manatee County owner list a house while tax is unpaid?

Yes. Closing can absorb what is owed. The title company orders the payoff, and the collector confirms whether a certificate exists.

When must I apply for a homestead exemption in Manatee County?

Apply to the Manatee County Property Appraiser by the March 1 deadline. The home must be your permanent residence as of January 1, and the appraiser accepts electronic filing.

Which Seminole County offices does a property seller deal with?

Seminole County splits the work among three elected offices. One values, one collects and one records, and a seller who calls the right one first saves days.

  • Seminole County Property Appraiser: 1101 E. 1st Street, Sanford, open weekdays 8 to 5. Call 407-665-7506 for general service or 407-665-7512 about exemptions and fraud.
  • Seminole County Tax Collector: bills, installment plans, deferral requests and certificates, with payments accepted in person, by mail or online.

The appraiser's site offers its data free in a downloads area, updated daily in Excel, Access and several GIS formats. Special data requests need 10 business days and may cost labor time.

Who buys and who holds Seminole County homes?

Census figures put the county at 491,884 residents in mid-2025, with two in three households owning. That leaves roughly a third renting, and a landlord who buys a house never qualifies for homestead. A seller marketing a rental should be ready to hand over the parcel's tax history.

When do Seminole County homestead filings open and close?

The appraiser splits filing in two: January 1 to March 1 for the current year, then pre-filing from March 2 to December 31 for the next. It lists March 1, 2027 as the next deadline and urges early filing to avoid lines.

A fall buyer can pre-file at once, and a February buyer has very little room. The appraiser also says requests to split or combine parcels, or to record plats, are held until the 2026 taxes are paid. Tell the appraiser by email once a bill is settled so the request moves.

What did the November 2026 amendment do for Seminole County owners?

The appraiser's home page reports that voters approved the constitutional amendment on property taxes on November 3, 2026, and links to an explainer. It does not say the amendment changes the roll already certified for 2026, so owners should treat the current bill as unchanged and use the explainer to plan for later years.

A seller should simply confirm which exemptions the house carries today. A larger amount reaches a buyer only after that buyer files.

How do the yearly deadlines line up for a Seminole County seller?

The appraiser's important dates page frames the cycle. Ownership and use on January 1 fix the assessment. March 1 closes homestead and agricultural filings, April 1 closes business personal property returns, and mid-August brings the TRIM notice with a short petition window.

  • November: bills mailed, board hearings start, and the early-payment discount is at its largest.

The sale ends the seller's benefits. The buyer is assessed at market value from the next January 1, and none of the seller's cap passes along. A seller who buys again in Florida can carry savings to the new homestead, capped at $500,000, if that home is set up within three years. The 2026 cap on the state chart is 2.7 percent.

Homestead lapses when a house is rented or abandoned, so call the appraiser before converting a Seminole County house into a rental.

How can an owner challenge a Seminole County value or denied exemption?

Begin by asking the appraiser to review the property record. If the dispute remains, the petition deadline is printed on the August notice, and a denied exemption or portability claim carries its own shorter window from the denial letter. A missed window means waiting a full cycle, which hurts when a sale is pending.

  • Read the notice for the exact deadline.
  • Collect recent sales and photos of defects.
  • Ask the title agent how a pending petition affects the closing.

What help does the Seminole County Property Appraiser publish for new owners?

The home page carries a First-Time Florida Homebuyer Guide, a new homeowner reminder postcard and a link to the Department of Revenue's guide to the property tax system. It also posts a Property Owner Bill of Rights that lists seven protections: to acquire, possess and protect property, to use and enjoy it, to exclude others, to dispose of it, to due process, to just compensation when property is taken for public use, and to relief when a new law or ordinance unfairly burdens it. The page says the list is not a complete statement of Florida law and does not replace legal advice.

A buyer from out of state can use those materials to learn how homestead filing works before the first January 1 passes.

What paperwork should a Seminole County seller gather?

Pull the latest bill and TRIM notice so buyers see the exemptions and caps on the parcel. Confirm whether the house had homestead on January 1 and whether any deferral or installment plan is active. Gather the deed, any lender payoff letter and open permits, and copy the TRIM notice that shows the savings you plan to port. Early gathering shortens the gap between contract and closing.

What do the deed and recording cost, and who pays?

The state stamp rate applies, with no Miami-Dade style exception. Everyone on the deed is answerable, so the contract should name who pays. Recording opens at a few dollars a page plus technology add-ons, and a personal representative's deed from a probated estate is listed as not taxable.

What if the Seminole County tax bill is unpaid at closing?

The title company can pay an open bill from proceeds. A sold certificate adds an investor who must also be paid, and the investor must wait two years before pressing the owner. A homestead owing under $250 has its certificate taken by the county. Ask for a payoff before listing.

  • Payoff statement from the collector.
  • Certificate search by the title agent.
  • Confirmation of any lender escrow.

What relief is available on a Seminole County bill?

Homestead removes up to $50,000 of taxable value in two layers, the second skipping school taxes. Seniors may qualify for more where a local ordinance applies, so ask the appraiser what Seminole has adopted. Veterans with a disability rating get further breaks, and deferral requests go to the tax collector by March 31.

Frequently asked questions

Does a Seminole County sale trigger a reassessment?

Yes. On the next January 1 the house is assessed at market value, and the seller's caps and exemptions stay behind.

When are Seminole County tax bills mailed?

In November, from the tax collector. Proposed-tax notices come first, in mid-August.

Where is Seminole County homestead filed?

At the property appraiser's office, by March 1, on Form DR-501. The home must already be your permanent residence on January 1, and pre-filing opens March 2 for the next year.

How long is the Seminole County appeal window?

You get 25 days from the August notice. The petition, on a DR-486 form, goes through the clerk to the Value Adjustment Board.

Who pays stamp tax on a Seminole County sale?

The law makes every party to the deed liable, so the sale contract should name who pays. The rate is 70 cents per $100 of consideration, handled by the clerk at recording.

Can Marion County owners pay their property tax in quarterly installments?

Yes, if they enroll on time. The Marion County Tax Collector's installment page wants Form DR534 on file ahead of May 1 in the year you join, and the prior year's bill has to have topped $100.

Once enrolled, an owner does not reapply each year, with one catch: if the first installment is missed, the account drops out and the owner has to reapply by April 30 of a later year. Four payments follow a fixed pattern, and the first two are based on the previous year's gross tax.

Marion County installment schedule as printed by the Tax Collector
PaymentDueAmountDiscount
FirstJune 30One quarter of last year's gross tax6%
SecondSeptember 30One quarter of last year's gross tax4.5%
ThirdDecember 31One quarter of this year's adjusted tax3%
FourthMarch 31One quarter of this year's adjusted taxNone

Source: Marion County Tax Collector, installment plan.

A late first payment can still be made by July 31, though without the discount. After July 31 the account reverts to ordinary annual billing.

Compare that with the ordinary route. A lump sum paid in November earns 4%, and the cut falls a point each month to 1% in February. Quarterly payers collect larger percentages on early installments but pay across a whole year, so the plan suits owners who prefer smooth cash flow over one big bill. A seller weighing the plan against an upcoming listing should remember that the discounted amounts are tied to last year's bill, which can differ from what the new year's roll produces.

What happens to a Marion installment plan when the house sells?

The plan belongs to the tax year, not to the seller. According to the collector, a property that changes hands after one or more quarterly payments must stay on the plan for that year under the new owner.

So a half-paid plan travels with the house. A buyer inherits the remaining quarters, and your title company needs to see which ones were already paid. Request a payment history from the collector and pass copies to both sides.

  • Put the plan details in the disclosure packet so no one finds them at the closing table.
  • Check that the settlement statement credits installments you already covered.
  • A buyer who prefers one annual bill should ask the collector whether the account can revert.

Where do Marion County sellers go in person for tax questions?

The Tax Collector keeps offices around the county, each open Monday to Friday from eight to four. Tax deed and certificate questions go only to the main branch, which matters if your parcel has an old balance.

  • Main office, McPherson Complex, 503 SE 25th Avenue, Ocala.
  • Dunnellon, inside the Rainbow Springs Government Complex.
  • Belleview, in the Belleview Regional Shopping Center on U.S. 441.
  • Forest, at Forest Center on State Road 40 in Silver Springs.
  • State Road 200, at Jasmine Square in Ocala.
  • North, at Ocala Springs Shopping Center on U.S. 441.
  • Summerfield, at Spruce Creek Terrace Shops.
  • Ocala Annex, which serves driver license customers only.

The office suggests midweek visits, ideally between 9:30 and 10:30 in the morning, and warns that Mondays, Fridays and month-end days run busiest. Lobby cameras on its site show the line before you leave. The shared number is (352) 368-8200.

Which Marion offices handle value, billing and records?

Three offices touch a Marion sale, and each owns a different question. All sit in Ocala, though each keeps its own website and search tools.

The Property Appraiser at 501 SE 25th Avenue determines value and processes exemptions, taking walk-ins or booked appointments. The Tax Collector issues and collects the bill. The Clerk of Court and Comptroller records deeds, hosts the Value Adjustment Board filings and conducts deed sales.

The statewide calendar sits on top of all three: January 1 fixes ownership and condition, March 1 closes exemption filings, April 1 is the tangible personal property deadline, and the proposed-tax notice lands in August. The collector's payment page gives November 1 as the due date.

Do Marion vacation rentals owe a separate local tax?

Yes. Rentals of six months or less carry a 4% Tourist Development Tax, collected from the guest and sent to the Tax Collector. The collector's page adds that Marion County has no contract with platforms such as Airbnb or VRBO, so the owner has to register, collect and remit directly.

The same page puts state sales tax at 7.5% in Marion County, made up of 6% plus a 1.5% infrastructure surtax. The tourist tax applies to rent and to fees tied to the stay, such as cleaning and pet fees.

  • The return is due on the first of the following month and is late after the 20th.
  • Operators file each month, collections or not.
  • Lateness costs 10% of the tax for each month, with a $50 floor and a ceiling of half the tax due.
  • An owner who sells or closes the business should notify the office in writing.

Past guest stays leave a paper trail. Pull your registration number, monthly returns and proof of payment together, because a careful buyer will want to see that the account is current.

What can the Marion appraiser's website do for a seller?

The site bundles a tax estimator, a request form for a mortgage estimate letter, a change-of-address form and a homestead e-file page. It adds a damage report page and a confidential channel for tips about suspected homestead fraud.

Run the estimator at a realistic sale price. A sale resets assessed value, so the buyer's first bill can differ sharply from yours, and lenders ask about that gap. Homestead trims up to $50,000 from the taxable base, with only the first $25,000 applying to school taxes, and the state cap protecting your own assessment ends at transfer.

After you move, file the address change. Notices follow the address on record, and a bill that never arrives still has to be paid.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What happens when Marion County taxes go unpaid?

April 1 marks the shift from routine billing to collection. Delinquent parcels are advertised, and certificates are sold by June 1. A certificate buyer covers the bill and collects interest, yet cannot demand money from the owner for two years.

The collector's menu offers an online tax deed application, online purchase of county-held certificates and a delinquent tax page. Homestead parcels start higher at a deed sale. Paying off a certificate sooner costs less, because interest keeps building.

Can a Marion County house with taxes owed still be sold?

Yes. Back taxes are common in estate sales and in houses left empty, and buyers expect them. Get the exact balance from the collector, and the closing agent deducts it from what the buyer brings.

The state charges seventy cents on each hundred dollars of price in deed stamps, paid at the clerk's recording desk. With an inherited house or several unpaid years, secure a written payoff before you accept anything. The Clerk's Property Alert Service sends a message whenever a document is recorded under your parcel or name, which helps spot deed fraud.

Frequently asked questions

Who sends the Marion County tax bill?

The Marion County Tax Collector. The Property Appraiser sets the value but never mails a bill, and the Clerk records deeds and handles deed sales.

What is the first Marion installment due date?

June 30, with a 6% discount on one quarter of last year's gross tax. A late first payment is allowed through July 31 without the discount.

Does the buyer keep my Marion installment plan?

Which Collier County offices handle my property tax bill?

Billing and payment sit with the tax collector. Values and exemptions belong to the appraiser, while appeals and tax deed auctions run through the clerk's office. A call to the wrong office costs time.

The tax collector's mailing address is 3291 Tamiami Trail East, Naples, FL 34112. Property tax questions go to propertytax@colliertax.com or 239-252-8171. The Property Appraiser can be reached at (239) 252-8141 for value and exemption questions.

What does paying early save in Collier County, and when is a bill late?

Bills are payable in November, and paying early earns a discount that shrinks each month. The tax collector's page starts the discount at 4% in November and drops it a point each month until it ends at 1% in February. The gross amount is due in March, and the bill goes delinquent in April.

Collier County payment months, as printed by the tax collector
Month paidDiscount
November4% off
December3% off
January2% off
February1% off
MarchGross amount due
AprilDelinquent

The collector does not accept post-dated checks. Florida's revenue department notes that certificate sales on unpaid items finish by June 1. All offices close on listed holidays, including Veterans Day, Thanksgiving and the day after, and on one training day in October.

How does the Collier County assessment and notice cycle work?

The appraiser values every parcel as of each New Year's Day. In mid-August the appraiser mails a TRIM notice, the formal proposal of next year's tax.

  • August: TRIM notice arrives, listing proposed values and tax.
  • September and October: local taxing authorities hold budget hearings.
  • November: the tax collector sends bills.

Other property faces a 10 percent yearly ceiling on assessed growth. Read the TRIM notice closely, because it is the notice that starts the appeal clock.

Where do I contest a Collier County property value?

Petitions go to the Value Adjustment Board, whose clerk is the Collier County clerk and comptroller. An assessment appeal is due within 25 days after the appraiser mails the TRIM notice, and the 2026 petition deadline of September 11 has passed.

Other petitions run on different clocks. The clerk's table lists these:

  • Exemption or classification denial: 30 days after the appraiser mails the denial, with all denials mailed by July 1
  • Tax deferral denial: 30 days after the tax collector mails the denial
  • Portability and change of ownership or control: 25 days after the TRIM notice

The filing fee is $50.00 per petition per parcel for most types and $15.00 for a portability petition. The board has two county commissioners, one school board member and two citizen members, and special magistrates hear the cases and recommend decisions. Late filing needs a good cause statement.

How should I read a Collier County tax bill?

The tax collector bills ad valorem tax, which means tax according to worth, on real estate and on a business's tangible personal property. One mill equals a dollar of tax on each thousand dollars of taxable value, and every taxing authority sets its own rate, so the county, school district, city and special districts all appear on one bill.

Three checks help before you pay or sell:

  • Match the parcel number and legal owner on the bill to your deed.
  • Confirm the homestead exemption shows on the bill if you applied by March 1.
  • See whether any non-ad valorem charge appears, because those are assessments rather than value-based tax.

The tax collector's site links to a tax search where you can pull a notice or receipt, and a mortgage lender that pays from escrow should still be checked against that record.

What homestead and exemption rules matter for a Collier County owner?

Homestead applications reach the appraiser by that March date, and the house must be your permanent home on January 1. The exemption reaches $50,000, where the first $25,000 reduces every levy, school tax included, and the next $25,000 reduces only non-school levies on value above $50,000.

Under Save Our Homes, a homestead's assessed value may climb each year by the smaller of 3 percent and the CPI change, and the state's chart prints 2.7% for 2026. After a sale the parcel goes back to full market-based value the next New Year's Day, which can make a buyer's bill very different from the seller's. Portability lets an owner bring accumulated savings along to a replacement Florida home, provided it begins inside a three-year window after the old one ended.

Homestead protection ends if the home is rented or stops being the permanent residence. Senior owners may qualify for added local exemptions, and disabled veterans have separate benefits. The appraiser can say which apply to your Naples or Marco Island address.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Can I delay or spread out Collier County property tax?

Yes, through tax deferral and the installment program, both listed on the tax collector's property tax page. Deferring homestead tax takes Form DR-570, filed with the collector by March 31 after the assessment year, and covers the part above 5 percent of household income.

A permanent resident 65 or older may defer the part above 3 percent. The installment plan under section 197.222 needs an application by the May 1 cutoff in the year of assessment. Confirm current terms with the collector, since deferred tax accrues interest and carries a lien.

Who settles the Collier County tax bill at a sale?

Unpaid current-year tax is settled at closing, normally by the closing agent from the proceeds. Request a payoff figure for your closing date, and confirm earlier years show paid.

If taxes stay unpaid, the county sells a certificate. Once two years have run from the April 1 following issue, the holder can file for a tax deed, and the clerk then runs the auction. A homestead parcel's opening bid adds one-half of the latest assessment. At the clerk's tax deed auction, a winning bidder pays within 24 hours, so a delinquent house can be lost quickly, and a seller with unpaid years should settle them before listing. For recording costs on your own sale, see the Collier County property records guide.

Where do I find Collier County tax deed and foreclosure listings?

The Collier Clerk posts both a tax deeds list and a foreclosure sale list on its records search page. The tax deeds list covers properties where the tax collector sold certificates for delinquent real estate taxes.

State law lets the tax collector award each certificate to the bidder who accepts the lowest interest rate, in quarter-percent steps, and unsold certificates go to the county at the maximum rate. The certificate holder may not contact the owner for payment until two years from the first April 1 after issue. A homeowner with a small delinquency has options before that point, since payment to the tax collector redeems the certificate, so ask the collector's office for a payoff early rather than waiting for a sale notice.

Frequently asked questions

What date marks Collier County tax as late?

Lateness begins in April, on the state's April 1 date. The gross amount is due in March, with discounts only from November through February.

What early-payment discounts does Collier County offer?

Savings shrink from 4% in the first month of payment through 1% in the last, which is February. After that the full gross amount applies, starting in March.

How long is the window to contest a Collier County assessment?

Petitions are due within 25 days after the appraiser mails the TRIM notice. The 2026 deadline was September 11, and most petitions carry a $50.00 filing fee.

Does Collier County accept post-dated checks for property tax?

No. The tax collector states that post-dated checks are not accepted for property tax bills.

What is the mailing address for Collier County tax payments?

Mail it to the Collier County Tax Collector, 3291 Tamiami Trail East, Naples, FL 34112. Questions go to 239-252-8171.

Which offices touch an Alachua County tax bill?

Three elected offices share the job. One values property and rules on exemptions, one sends and collects the bill, and one records deeds and takes the documentary stamp tax.

Taxes equal taxable value, after exemptions, times the millage rate set by each taxing authority. If no bill arrives in November, the Tax Collector's page gives (352) 374-5236 as the number to call.

Discounts follow the postmark. Once a bill is delinquent, the office says a 3 percent minimum charge is added on April 1 and an advertising charge in May, and the date the payment is received controls the amount.

What are the Alachua County millage rates?

Alachua County's own 2026 TRIM explainer lists a 2025 countywide millage of 7.6000 mills and a proposed 2026 rollback rate of 7.2107 mills, which it describes as the tenth straight year of a lower countywide rate.

Treat the 2026 figure as proposed until the final adopted rate appears on your bill or the Tax Collector's site. The same article notes that a TRIM notice carries several taxing authorities, so the county is only one line on it. Homes inside a city add that city's levy, and the explainer says that for Gainesville certain charges once on monthly utility bills now appear on the notice.

Some owners in unincorporated areas also see a Law Enforcement Municipal Services Taxing Unit line, which the county lists at a proposed 3.5678 mills. Non-ad valorem items such as county fire, solid waste and stormwater are charged by assessment, not millage.

Which exemptions and deadlines should an Alachua County owner know?

Exemption applications go to the Alachua County appraiser's office and are due March 1. Per the Florida Department of Revenue, the home must be your permanent residence by the preceding January 1.

  • Homestead takes up to $50,000 off. The first $25,000 reaches every levy, school included, and the second $25,000 reaches only non-school levies on value over $50,000.
  • Save Our Homes holds annual growth in assessed value to 3 percent or the CPI change, whichever is less. The state chart prints 2.7 percent for 2026.
  • A sale or foreclosure sends assessed value back up to just value each following January, though spousal transfers are among the exceptions.
  • Portability moves the accumulated benefit to a new homestead, if it is set up inside three years of the old one being given up.
  • Disabled veterans, deployed servicemembers and seniors can qualify for added relief. A city or county ordinance sets the senior exemption.

Renting out a homestead ends the exemption, so a seller who moved out should ask the Property Appraiser how the status stands.

Can Alachua County owners pay in installments or defer tax?

Yes. The Tax Collector offers a quarterly installment plan and a homestead tax deferral, each with its own rules.

Installments require prior year taxes above $100, and the application window closes April 30. Discounts printed on the page are 6 percent on the June 30 payment, 4.5 percent on the September 30 payment, 3 percent on the December 31 payment and none on the March 31 payment.

For deferral, the property must qualify for homestead, the primary mortgage cannot exceed 70 percent of assessed value, and the form is due at the end of March. Interest accrues on deferred tax at no more than 7 percent a year, and the whole balance falls due when homestead eligibility, use or ownership changes. That means a sale triggers payoff at closing.

What should landlords in Alachua County know about tax on rentals?

Rental houses carry two exposures: the real estate bill and tangible personal property tax on furniture, fixtures and equipment inside a rental.

The Tax Collector explains that the Property Appraiser values tangible property as of January 1 and that a return that arrives by April 1 earns an exemption of up to $25,000. Late or missing returns bring penalties and loss of that exemption. Unpaid tangible tax turns delinquent April 1 with a $10 fee and 1.5 percent monthly interest, and a 20 percent collection fee is added May 1.

Landlords selling a rental should note that, per the same page, the tangible tax lien follows the property and survives a sale, and any proration between buyer and seller is handled at closing. What happens when Alachua County taxes go unpaid?

The Tax Collector advertises delinquent parcels, then runs an online certificate sale at lienhub.com by early June, with bidding opening at 18 percent and dropping.

The winning bidder pays the tax and earns interest, and the certificate becomes a first lien on the property. After at least two years from delinquency, the page says, the certificate holder can seek a tax deed, and an unredeemed property goes to public auction. To clear a certificate, the owner pays the Tax Collector the tax, interest, costs and charges.

Florida law bars a certificate holder from demanding payment from the owner for two years after April 1 of the issue year. A seller with a certificate on the house can usually clear it from sale proceeds, and the payoff figure comes from the Tax Collector's office.

How is tax handled when an Alachua County house sells?

The bill goes to whoever is on the roll, and the two sides settle the split at the closing table.

Deeds carry Florida's documentary stamp tax, 70 cents on each $100 of consideration outside Miami-Dade, paid to the clerk when the deed is recorded. Every party to the deed is liable, whatever the contract says about who pays. A buyer whose mortgage pays taxes through escrow gets the bill through the lender, and the Tax Collector notes that lenders must pay inside the 4 percent window.

The county counted 290,028 residents in July 2025, and owners live in 54.1 percent of homes, a low share that points to a large renter base. A $288,800 median value. With college-town turnover, ask the title company early for a tax and lien search.

Around the start of November. If yours does not arrive, call the Tax Collector at (352) 374-5236.

Pay by the end of March. After that, a 3 percent minimum charge applies from April 1.

Is the 2026 Alachua County millage final?

The county's explainer calls it proposed. It shows 7.2107 mills as the proposed 2026 rollback rate against 7.6000 in 2025. Confirm the adopted rate with the Tax Collector or your bill.

Does selling my Alachua County home end my homestead?

A sale counts as a change of ownership, so assessed value returns to just value the next January. The new owner files a fresh homestead application.

Can an Alachua County owner with unpaid tax still sell?

Yes. The title company can pay delinquent tax and any certificate out of the buyer's funds. Request from the Tax Collector the payoff amount before the closing date.

Who is responsible for each part of a Bay County bill?

The Bay County Property Appraiser sets the value and decides exemptions, local governments set millage rates, and the Bay County Tax Collector prints, mails and collects the bill.

The Tax Collector's real estate page lays out the order. The appraiser assesses, the County Commission and other levying bodies set millage, the appraiser builds the roll, and the certified roll then moves to the Tax Collector. Any change to name, mailing address, location or assessed value has to go through the Property Appraiser, not the Tax Collector.   • Property Appraiser: value questions and TRIM notice questions, (850) 248-8401, as printed on the Value Adjustment Board page.
  • Tax Collector: payment, delinquent tax and tax deferral.
  • Clerk of Court and Comptroller: official records, plus the clerk work for the Value Adjustment Board.

What is the yearly tax calendar in Bay County?

The yearly cycle tracks the Florida Department of Revenue calendar, and each step belongs to one office.

  • January 1: the date that fixes value and ownership for the tax year.
  • March 1: exemption and classification applications are due.
  • August: the Property Appraiser mails the TRIM notice of proposed taxes. A value challenge goes to the court clerk within 25 days of that notice.
  • September and October: taxing authorities hold tentative budget hearings, with final budget and millage hearings in October and November.
  • November: the Tax Collector sends the bill.
  • April 1: unpaid taxes become delinquent, and certificates are sold by June 1.

For a Bay County house listed in spring, that means the prior year's bill may still be open at closing while the new roll is being built.

Where are the Bay County Tax Collector's offices?

The Tax Collector lists four service offices, and a Bay County bill can only be paid at its own offices.

  • Panama City: 850 W. 11th St., Panama City, FL 32401.
  • Panama City Beach: 10520 Hutchison Blvd., Panama City Beach, FL 32407.
  • Lynn Haven: 700 Florida Ave., Lynn Haven, FL 32444.
  • Callaway: 805 S. Tyndall Pkwy, Callaway, FL 32404.

Bring the property tax notice or the property address. Delinquent balances must be paid in certified funds, which the page lists as cash, a cashier's check, a money order or a credit card. Appointments can be booked through the Tax Collector's site, and online payment is offered too.

What does a Bay County seller do before listing?

A name that does not match, or a mailing address that is out of date, means the bill may never reach you, and the Tax Collector's page says changes to name or address must be made through the Property Appraiser.

Next, check whether non-ad valorem charges for paving, stormwater or solid waste are on the bill, since those are billed beside the tax and are owed at closing like the rest. A house that sat vacant or was repaired after storm damage can have an assessed value that no longer matches its condition, which is a reason to review the TRIM notice in August rather than wait for the bill.

Finally, ask the title company for a lien and tax search. Panama City, Panama City Beach, Lynn Haven and Callaway all sit in the same county tax system, so the same offices answer for any of them.

When are Bay County taxes due, and what discounts apply?

Apply through the Bay County Property Appraiser before the March 1 cutoff, having made the home your permanent residence by January 1.

  • After a sale or foreclosure, the property is revalued at just value each following January.

Petition the Bay County Value Adjustment Board. The 2026 petition deadline fell on September 8, 2026, and the next filing window follows the TRIM notices mailed the following August.

Section 194.014, quoted on that page, requires a petitioner contesting value to pay all non-ad valorem assessments and at least 75 percent of the ad valorem taxes, less the discount, before the taxes go delinquent. If the partial payment is missed, the board must deny the petition by April 20.

What can a Bay County owner do about a bill they cannot pay?

Florida offers a homestead tax deferral through Form DR-570, filed with the Tax Collector by March 31. It covers tax above 5 percent of household income, or above 3 percent for a permanent resident aged 65 or older.

Section 197.222 of state law also allows an installment plan, with applications due May 1 of the assessment year. Ask the Bay County Tax Collector which plans it runs and what the payoff is.

Unpaid tax turns delinquent April 1, and state law requires certificates to be sold by June 1. Two years after April 1 of the issue year, the holder is allowed to seek a tax deed. A seller in that spot can usually settle the balance out of the price paid at the table.

What happens to Bay County tax when the house sells?

Whoever holds title on the roll receives the bill, and the year is divided between buyer and seller when the deal closes. Have the title company pull the current bill, any non-ad valorem balance and the discount month in effect.

A deed documentary stamp tax applies at 70 cents per $100 of consideration outside Miami-Dade, collected by the clerk at recording. Everyone named on a taxable deed is liable, even if the contract assigns payment to one side.

A buyer starts with no inherited cap once the next January arrives, so the seller's tax history is a poor guide to what the buyer will owe. Selling an inherited or storm-worn house works the same way: clear liens and unpaid balances first, then record the deed in Panama City.

Which Charlotte County offices handle which part of the bill?

Each office has a lane: the appraiser sets value and approves exemptions, the collector issues and takes payment on the bill, and the clerk runs tax deed sales.

  • Property appraiser: values, exemptions and homestead applications, phone (941) 743-1593 for exemption questions on a notice and (941) 743-1498 for assessed value questions.
  • Tax collector: bills, discounts, installment plans and delinquent taxes, phone (941) 743-1350.
  • Clerk's office: online tax deed sales, phone (941) 637-2130.

Installment applications are mailed to the collector at 18500 Murdock Circle, Port Charlotte, FL 33948. If you sold the house, send the bill on to the buyer or return it to the collector.

What dates and discounts apply to a Charlotte County bill?

Statements go out by the first of November, and paying early earns a sliding discount that starts at 4% and shrinks one point a month.

Charlotte County billing and collection steps
StepDetail

Where an escrow account pays the tax, the collector's page says the mortgage company should request the bill and the owner receives a copy for information.

How does the installment plan work in Charlotte County?

Send the application to the collector before May 1; the first payment is due by June 30.

Skip the first payment and the plan is cancelled, leaving the whole tax due by March 31. After the first payment you owe participation for the year, and enrollment renews on its own. The office says that to leave, you simply ignore the June bill and wait for the November notice at the gross amount. Anything unpaid on April 1 is treated as a delinquent bill.

Installments one and two are each a quarter of the estimate. Numbers three and four add half of any true-up each, so the last two bills can differ from the first two.

What happens if Charlotte County taxes go unpaid?

Real estate tax left unpaid turns delinquent April 1 and heads to a certificate sale by early June.

Delinquent parcels are advertised in a local paper weekly for three weeks, and advertising and collection fees land on the delinquent account. The sale is a reverse auction on the interest rate starting at 18%, and the lowest bidder gets the certificate, a first lien. A certificate is valid for seven years. Once two years pass from the delinquency date, the holder can seek a tax deed, and the clerk conducts the sale online.

  • Only cashier's checks, money orders or cash are accepted for delinquent taxes.
  • A deed sale opens at a total that includes a $75.00 collector fee, a $150.00 ownership and encumbrance report, a $60.00 clerk fee and a $59.00 web fee, plus taxes, interest and half the assessed value.
  • Paying all taxes, costs and interest before the deed is issued stops the sale.

How does homestead work for Charlotte County owners?

The county appraiser takes homestead applications until March 1 of the year you want the benefit, and you must live there as a permanent resident by New Year's Day.

State law gives up to $50,000 off. School taxes see only the first $25,000, while the added $25,000 applies on value above $50,000, for non-school levies. Later growth in assessed value is capped at 3 percent or CPI, and the state's chart prints a 2.7 percent cap for 2026. Selling resets the figure to full just value the following January 1.

Renting the home out ends homestead, except for the servicemember rule in the statutes. Seniors and veterans may qualify for extra benefits, and the appraiser's office rules on each case.

How do incomes and rents look in Charlotte County?

Median household income is $69,952 in 2024 dollars, and per capita income is $42,592. Renters pay about $1,464, and monthly owner costs run $1,773 with a mortgage and $678 without one.

Just 43.2% of people 16 and older work or look for work, a figure that tracks the county's age profile. QuickFacts also lists 19,280 veterans, 4,601 employer establishments in 2023 and 90,542 households of 2.17 people on average.

For a seller, the ownership numbers matter most. Because 87.3% of residents stayed put over the past year, many carry capped assessments, while a buyer starts from the reset value.

What other charges does the Charlotte County collector handle?

The collector also bills tangible personal property tax, which falls on the furniture and equipment of a business or rental property and on structural additions to mobile homes. These bills go out with the real estate bills and earn the same early discounts.

On April 1 tangible tax goes delinquent and picks up 1.5% interest, a $2.00 late fee and advertising costs. Warrants are issued before April 30 on unpaid accounts, and within 30 days the office applies to the circuit court for an order allowing levy and seizure.

  • Redeeming a certificate on or after June 1 adds a $6.25 redemption fee.
  • Paper bills can be replaced with email bills through the office's Bill Express sign-up, though an undeliverable bill does not extend a discount period.
  • Email addresses given for e-billing become public records.

How is the tax handled when you sell in Charlotte County?

Your closing agent divides the year's tax between the two parties and takes anything owed, delinquent amounts included, out of the proceeds.

Call (941) 743-1350 for a payoff and ask whether a certificate was sold, since a holder has to be repaid with interest before the lien clears. The deed carries the state's 70 cents per $100 stamp tax, paid at recording, with every party to the document liable.

A buyer of a homesteaded house will not inherit the seller's exemption or capped value. Ask both offices for figures on your parcel.

Frequently asked questions

Which office mails the Charlotte County bill?

The Charlotte County Tax Collector mails it on or before November 1, using the roll certified by the property appraiser. Call (941) 743-1350 with billing questions.

What is the early payment discount in Charlotte County?

Four percent off in November, falling one point each month to 1% in February. March brings none, and delinquency starts April 1.

Can Charlotte County taxes be paid in installments?

Yes, when the estimate exceeds $100 and the application is in before May 1. Four payments follow, ending March 31.

When can a tax certificate turn into a tax deed application?

Two years after the tax went delinquent. A certificate lasts seven years, and redemption is possible until a deed is issued.

Where do I file for homestead in Charlotte County?

Send it to the county appraiser by March 1. That office decides eligibility, and the collector only bills.
