What sets St. Johns County apart in the Census data?

Income and schooling stand out. The Census Bureau puts median household income for 2020 to 2024 at $109,839 and per capita income at $57,346, with 50.9 percent of adults 25 and older holding a bachelor's degree and 5.8 percent of residents below the poverty line. Owners occupy 82.2 percent of the 115,794 households, and the midpoint owner home is valued at $489,200.

Growth is the other story. The county went from 190,039 people in 2010 to 273,425 in 2020 and reached an estimated 346,328 by mid-2025, up 26.7 percent on the 2020 base. Permits hit 4,735 in 2025, and the average commute is 26.9 minutes. Owners with a mortgage report a median monthly cost of $2,351, against $728 for those without one, which shows how much of the carrying cost for a newer buyer is the loan and not the tax. All figures are.

What does the St. Johns County property appraiser give a new owner?

A checklist, and a few useful phone numbers. The office's new owner page opens with a note that the county runs from farmland to beaches, then tells buyers to find the parcel's record card, complete the sales questionnaire and verify the name and mailing address, because the TRIM notice and bill go to that address. A button on the record card estimates the tax bill.

  • Customer service: 904-827-5500.
  • Business equipment returns: 904-827-5508.
  • Building department: 904-827-6800.
  • Planning and zoning: 904-209-0675.
  • Utility department: 904-209-2700.

The page also sends owners to the tax collector to update a Florida driver license, a step that matters because the homestead application checks that the license shows the homestead address. New business owners may need a local business tax application and must create an account with the appraiser.

Which dates does the St. Johns County appraiser publish?

The important dates page runs through the year, and the dates change what a seller or buyer can claim.

  • January 1: the status of the property sets its value for the assessment year, and ownership and residence on this day decide homestead eligibility.
  • January 1 to April 1: business equipment returns are filed.
  • March 1: filing closes for homestead, other personal exemptions, classified use, agricultural classification and organizational exemptions.
  • August and September: TRIM notices go out with proposed assessments, millage and hearing dates.
  • November: the tax collector mails bills.

A weekend March 1 pushes the cutoff to Monday, and the homestead page named March 2 for 2026.

What is the 2026 homestead figure in St. Johns County, and who qualifies?

The appraiser prints $51,411 for the 2026 tax year, now indexed to inflation. A first block of $25,000 applies to every levy, school bills among them. The remaining $26,411 applies to assessed value between $50,000 and $75,000 and leaves school tax untouched.

To qualify, an owner must be a Florida permanent resident who holds title and lives in the home on January 1. Neither spouse may take a residency-based exemption in another state, and the office wants proof of that. Applicants bring a Florida license or ID showing the homestead address and Social Security numbers for both spouses, which are required for online filing. A noncitizen needs a Permanent Resident Card. If you owned a Florida home before, give its address or parcel number. Closing after January 1 means that year's exemption is out of reach.

Once approved, the owner need not reapply unless marital status, ownership or title changes. A late application for just cause can be filed through the end of the TRIM period, which usually falls late in August.

Can a St. Johns County homeowner rent the house and keep homestead?

Renting a portion is fine; renting all of it is limited. The appraiser says the part of a home not rented stays eligible, and a garage apartment or other separate rental space can be carved out while the rest keeps the exemption. Renting the whole property for more than 30 days in two consecutive tax years ends it, and a rental lasting over six months in a tax year is presumed commercial.

Ownership structure matters too. Property held in a trust qualifies if the applicant is the trustee or the trust language gives beneficial title. Moving the house into an LLC or another business entity is treated as a change of ownership, which strips every exemption and cap. After a divorce or marriage, the appraiser may ask for a new application, and it sends notice when the deed is recorded in St. Johns County. A deed recorded elsewhere leaves the owner responsible for telling the office.

How does portability work in St. Johns County?

Portability lets an owner carry the gap between market and assessed value, up to $500,000, from one Florida homestead to another. The move must happen within three tax years, counted January through December from the sale, and a December sale counts as one tax year.

The appraiser adds several rules. Downsizing is allowed, and the transferable amount shrinks in proportion to the lower value of the new home. Everyone who owned the old home and owns the new one must apply together, and each spouse of a married couple counts. Portability can be used any number of times but never from outside Florida. Spouses who abandon a jointly titled home may split the difference with Form DR-501TS, provided they were married on the abandonment date. The benefit total appears on the TRIM notice and the record card for a St. Johns County home. Non-homestead property carries a separate 10 percent cap, and that benefit cannot be ported.

Which other exemptions does St. Johns County list, and what proof do they need?

All of the breaks below are due by March 1 and the office asks applicants to visit in person. Dollar amounts are the ones the appraiser prints.

Selected personal exemptions on the St. Johns County appraiser's page
ExemptionAmountProof asked for
Age 65 or older, limited incomeUp to $50,000Form DR-501SC and prior year household income
Widowed$5,000Mark it on the homestead form or give the death certificate
Blind$5,000Form DR-416 or DR-416B, or SSDI proof
Totally and permanently disabled civilian$5,000Form DR-416 or SSDI letter
Veteran disabled 10 percent or more$5,000DD-214 and a VA disability letter
Combat-related disabled veteran, 65 or olderEqual to the disability ratingForm DR-501DV, DD-214, VA letter

Source: St. Johns County Property Appraiser, other exemptions. The same page lists total exemptions for quadriplegics, for certain permanent disabilities with limited income, for veterans totally and permanently disabled through service, for surviving spouses of those who died on active duty and for first responders disabled in the line of duty, plus a deployment exemption on Form DR-501M. Churches, schools, hospitals, nursing homes, affordable housing and historic buildings fall under property-use exemptions. With 23,534 veterans and 22.5 percent of residents 65 or older, many sellers qualify for something here.

How does a St. Johns County owner dispute a value?

Start with a conversation at the appraiser's office; if that fails, a petition goes to the Value Adjustment Board. The TRIM notice goes out in mid-August. A petition may be filed within 25 days of that mailing, and the date is printed at the top of the notice itself.

The Clerk of the Circuit Court and County Comptroller manages the process and posts the petition form, at 904-819-3600. The appraiser's site carries a Value Adjustment Board page and a Property Owner Bill of Rights. A denied exemption, classification or portability claim has its own 30 day window under state guidance, so a seller who thinks the assessment is too high should act before listing.

What do state rules add when a St. Johns County house sells?

Stamp tax is seventy cents on each hundred dollars of price and binds every party named on the deed. The clerk charges $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each after it. Debt that stays on the house is counted in the price.

Unpaid bills turn delinquent April 1, certificates are sold by June 1, and a holder may apply for a deed after two years, with half the latest assessed value added to the opening bid on homestead land. Get a payoff from the collector and have the title company search for certificates.

Frequently asked questions

What is the 2026 homestead exemption total in St. Johns County?

$51,411, per the appraiser's homestead page. The first $25,000 reaches all levies and $26,411 applies to value between $50,000 and $75,000, excluding school taxes.

Is the March 1 homestead deadline ever different in St. Johns County?

Yes, when March 1 falls on a weekend the filing moves to the next business day. The office listed March 2 for 2026.

Does a St. Johns County buyer keep the seller's capped value?

No. A sale resets the home to market value the next January 1. The seller may port up to $500,000 of the gap to a new Florida homestead within three tax years.

Can I rent my whole St. Johns County homestead for a few months?

Renting the entire home for more than 30 days in two consecutive tax years ends the exemption. A rental beyond six months in one year is presumed commercial.

Who runs the Value Adjustment Board paperwork in St. Johns County?

The circuit clerk and comptroller, at 904-819-3600. A petition is due 25 days after TRIM notices are mailed.

What do the Census numbers say about St. Lucie County?

St. Lucie County counted 277,789 residents in 2010, 329,226 in 2020 and an estimated 402,449 by mid-2025, which the Census Bureau calls a 22.2 percent rise since the 2020 base. Land area is 571.66 square miles. Roughly one resident in four is 65 or older at 24.9 percent, so age-linked tax breaks matter here more than they do in a younger county.

Source: Census QuickFacts, St. Lucie County. With 24,969 veterans on the count and 78.6 percent of homes owner occupied, the veteran and homestead rules below reach a large share of sellers.

Which St. Lucie County office answers which tax question?

The property appraiser's office, reachable at 772-462-1000, splits its work across four departments: appraisal, mapping, tax roll and tangible property. It values parcels, tracks ownership changes, keeps boundary maps and grants exemptions. It does not set a rate. Elected county and city officials, the school board and districts for fire, roads, port, airport and water management set those.

The tax collector, at 772-462-1650 for equipment tax questions, mails bills at the start of November and collects. The Clerk of the Court records deeds and answers copy requests at 772-462-6900. The appraiser's real estate search shows a record card, a TRIM button and a map for each parcel, which is the fastest way to check what the county has on file before you list.

What does each column of a St. Lucie County TRIM notice show?

Page one of the mid-August notice compares three scenarios, and the appraiser colors them. The orange column holds last year's values and budgets, for comparison only. The blue column shows this year's tax if every taxing body raised the same dollars it did before. The green column shows the tax at each body's proposed rate, which can still shift after public hearings.

Page two lists market value for both years, then assessed value, exemptions and taxable value per taxing authority. A gray band reports reductions such as the agricultural classification, the 3 percent or 10 percent cap and any portability benefit. The notice also prints the Value Adjustment Board deadline; for 2026 the appraiser's page gave September 8. The notice is an estimate and not a bill.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

How does the appraiser get from market value to taxable value in St. Lucie County?

The appraiser's FAQ lays the chain out in five links.

  • Just market value: the price signal from sales before the January 1 assessment date.
  • Cap: a 3 percent limit on homestead growth and a 10 percent limit for other property.
  • Assessed value: just value minus the cap.
  • Exemptions: reductions for which the owner applied and qualified.
  • Taxable value: assessed value minus exemptions, which is the number each millage rate multiplies.

Some bill lines have nothing to do with that chain. Non ad valorem charges pay for services like lighting, landscaping, security and trash, and they do not track the value of the home.

Why did a St. Lucie County bill jump after a purchase?

The previous owner's protections do not travel with the house. Reassessment happens each January 1, and a new owner receives market value with the old exemptions and capped amount erased. The appraiser also notes that a neighbor's lower bill usually comes from a cap built up over years of homestead or from an extra exemption the neighbor holds.

The cap begins to accrue only after the first year of homestead, and only when market value is rising. A seller who is listing should warn buyers that the current tax figure on a listing can understate what the next owner pays.

What happens to homestead and the cap when a St. Lucie County deed changes?

Homestead cannot be handed over; a new application is needed whenever title changes or a new home is established. Adding a name to the deed normally leaves the exemption alone but can cost part of the cap, depending on the tenancy.

  • Joint tenants with survivorship who also file for homestead: the cap resets to market value and restarts the next year.
  • Joint tenants who do not file: the cap is left unchanged.
  • Tenants in common who do not file: the cap shrinks to the original owner's share, and the other share is assessed at market and then under the 10 percent limit.

Inheritance follows the same logic. An heir generally cannot keep the decedent's exemption or cap, which end with the year. Two exceptions let a cap continue: a surviving spouse who files for homestead, and a legally or naturally dependent person living in the house at the death who then files. Placing a home in a trust requires the beneficial interest language of s. 196.041 on the deed or in the trust pages, and the appraiser asks for the trust if the deed lacks it.

How can a St. Lucie County seller carry the cap to a new house?

Portability moves the accumulated gap between market and assessed value, up to $500,000, to a new Florida homestead. The appraiser's page requires a homestead exemption on the old property in at least one of the three preceding tax years, and a new homestead established by January 1 within three tax years of abandoning the old one.

File with the new homestead application by March 1, in either office location or online. A former spouse sharing the old home must file the DR-501TS share designation first. A larger new house transfers the full amount, while a smaller one carries it over in proportion.

What payment dates should a St. Lucie County owner circle?

The collector's month page gives a 2 percent discount in January for real estate and equipment tax, and January 31 as the last day to file for homestead tax deferral. That date sits earlier than the March 31 date on the state's general guidance, so confirm which applies before relying on either. November through February runs the usual 4, 3, 2 and 1 percent scale printed by the Department of Revenue.

An unpaid bill turns delinquent April 1, certificates are sold by June 1, and a holder may seek a deed two years after April 1 of the issue year. A title company will ask for a certificate search, so order one early.

Who owes equipment tax when a St. Lucie County business changes hands?

The tax follows the equipment, so the buyer and seller should check balances before closing. The appraiser's FAQ advises calling the collector on 772-462-1650 to learn whether tangible personal property tax is unpaid, and it suggests asking the closing agent to prorate.

Returns are due April 1. Late filers pay 5 percent for each month or part of a month, a missing return draws 25 percent, and unreported assets can add 15 percent. There is no minimum value, and a landlord must report furniture and appliances supplied in a rental. A thirty day extension can be requested online before April 1 with written reasons. When a business closes, the owner files a final return and an account status change form.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Does agricultural land in St. Lucie County stay classified after a sale?

No. The appraiser states that an agricultural classification does not transfer with the land, and applications are taken between January 1 and March 1. The classification lowers value, but it is not an exemption.

Use on January 1 controls the outcome, and the appraiser inspects. Evidence includes care of the land, income and expense records, a Schedule F or C, receipts for feed, seed or fertilizer, business plans and insurance. Land used mainly for residential, development or investment purposes is not eligible, and agricultural zoning does not create the classification. Owners must report any change in use or acreage or risk losing it.

What ballot item did the St. Lucie County appraiser flag for 2026?

The appraiser's TRIM page described a proposed constitutional amendment, labeled Amendment 3 (CS/HJR 1F), on the November 2026 general election ballot. The page said approval by at least 60 percent of voters would make it effective January 1, 2027. Check the appraiser's site for the result and what it means for a homestead, since the page did not describe the details.

Beware of mail that looks like a bill. The appraiser warns that letters from a county records office or property site are solicitations and not amounts due, and that those companies have no tie to the county. A real deed copy comes from the clerk or from the parcel's record card.

Frequently asked questions

Is the TRIM notice a bill in St. Lucie County?

No. It is an estimate built from proposed rates, January 1 value and exemptions. The tax collector sends the actual bill at the beginning of November.

What is the usual homestead filing window in St. Lucie County?

January 1 through March 1. The appraiser also allows pre-filing for the following year at any time, and portability is filed alongside the homestead application.

Can a St. Lucie County heir keep a parent's capped value?

Generally no. A surviving spouse who files for homestead, or a dependent living in the house at the death who files, may keep it.

Who handles deed copies in St. Lucie County?

The Clerk of the Court, at 772-462-6900, or the parcel's record card on the appraiser's site. Mailed offers for copies are solicitations.

Does St. Lucie County have an early payment discount in January?

Yes, 2 percent, according to the collector's month page, and the same page lists January 31 for homestead tax deferral.

Why is Sumter County unusual for a seller?

Seniors dominate Sumter County. The Census Bureau counts 57.6 percent of residents at 65 or above, and just 7.6 percent under 18. Headcount reached an estimated 157,772 by mid-2025, a rise of 21.6 percent over the 2020 base of 129,752.

A household averages 1.93 people, and owners live in 87.6 percent of homes. Only 25.8 percent of adults 16 and up are in the civilian labor force. Buyers in such a market tend to ask hard questions about yearly carrying costs, so a seller does well to know the tax picture.

How much is Sumter County building?

Land area comes to 557.13 square miles. Crowding is still light, though it climbed from 170.8 people per square mile in 2010 to 232.9 in 2020. The mid-2025 count of homes was 95,691, and 3,516 permits were issued in 2025.

With that much permitting, a resale can sit next to new homes. Census data for 2020 to 2024 give a typical owned home at $385,400, and owners paid a median $1,686 monthly with a mortgage against $602 without.

Which Sumter County offices handle property tax?

In Sumter the appraiser values land and decides exemptions, while a separate collector sends the bills. The county's clerk of court also keeps the file for the Value Adjustment Board.

The county's board page lists five seats: two commissioners, one school board member, and two citizens, one named by each body. It hears appeals about value, classification and exemptions, leaves rates to the taxing authorities, and may not lower a value or give an exemption because of hardship. Qualified appraisers or attorneys serve as special magistrates, hear each petition and recommend a ruling.

What dates drive the Sumter County tax year?

Sumter follows the statewide calendar. January 1 fixes the assessment, March 1 closes homestead and classification filing, and April 1 is for personal property returns.

August brings the proposed-tax notice and a 25-day clock to petition. A denied exemption or portability claim has its own 30-day clock from the date the letter was mailed. Bills show up in November with a sliding discount of 4, 3, 2 and 1 percent through February, and April 1 marks delinquency.

  • Mar. 1: file for homestead.
  • Aug.: proposed-tax notice arrives.
  • 25 days on: value petition closes.
  • Nov.: bills, top discount.
  • Apr. 1: unpaid taxes delinquent.

How do homestead and portability work for Sumter County sellers?

Homestead reduces taxable value by as much as $50,000; the first $25,000 touches school taxes, the rest does not. Be living there on January 1, then apply on Form DR-501 at the appraiser's office.

After a sale the house is reassessed at market value, so the buyer's first full bill may far exceed the seller's. A seller staying in Florida can carry up to $500,000 of capped difference to the next homestead if it is set up within three years; Form DR-501T goes in with the application. Leaving the state forfeits it, because portability only links Florida homes.

Can a Sumter County owner dispute a value without a lawyer?

Yes. The petition goes through the clerk, who also acts as clerk to the Value Adjustment Board, and a special magistrate hears the case. The magistrate is independent of the property appraiser, so you present evidence of value, such as recent comparable sales, repair estimates or errors in the property record.

The panel looks only at whether value, classification or exemption is right. A tight household budget does not move the outcome. Sellers with a contract pending should tell the title agent about any open petition so that the closing statement handles the tax correctly.

Which exemptions matter most in a county this old?

Many Sumter County sales will touch age or veteran benefits. Counties and cities may adopt an added homestead exemption of up to $50,000 for owners over 65 with limited income, and a larger one equal to assessed value for 25-year residents whose home is worth under $250,000.

  • Older veterans with a lasting service-connected disability: discount matching the VA rating.
  • Former servicemembers rated 10 percent or more disabled: $5,000 off assessed value.
  • Total, permanent service-connected disability: possibly full relief on homestead.

Ask the Sumter County Property Appraiser which local ordinances add to this list and how a surviving spouse is treated.

How does a Sumter County buyer's first tax bill differ from the seller's?

Expect a jump. The seller may have been living under the Save Our Homes limit, which holds yearly increases to the lower of 3 percent or the inflation change (2.7 percent for 2026 on the state's chart). Once the deed records, the house is valued at market on the following January 1 and the limit starts over for the buyer.

A buyer who gets homestead in the first year also needs to apply by March 1, since the exemption is not automatic. Both sides gain from knowing this before closing, because the old bill on the listing sheet is a poor guide to the new one.

  • Seller's capped value does not transfer.
  • Buyer applies for homestead after taking title and living there on January 1.
  • Seller who moves within Florida may port the savings.

What can cancel a Sumter County homestead before a sale?

Three events end it: renting the home out, ceasing to use it as the permanent residence, or no longer being a Florida permanent resident.

Owners who move away before listing should speak with the appraiser about their status. One exception: a servicemember may rent out the homestead without abandoning the exemption. Seller and listing agent should confirm the status before preparing the tax proration, and buyers should ask what exemptions the parcel carried last year.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

What does a Sumter County deed cost at closing?

Stamp tax is seventy cents for each hundred dollars of price. A mortgage the buyer takes over is added to the price.

Everyone on the deed is liable, so let the contract say who funds it. The clerk bills $5.00 on page one and $4.00 afterward, plus add-ons. A probated estate gets relief because a personal representative's deed is listed as not taxable; a family deed made only for estate planning gets none.

What happens to a Sumter County house with unpaid tax?

Overdue taxes become certificates sold by June 1, and a holder can seek a deed after two years. At the clerk's tax deed auction the winner leaves 5 percent or $200, whichever is larger, and pays the balance in 24 hours, weekends and holidays excluded.

Paying at closing avoids all of it, and a title company will normally insist on that anyway. A homestead parcel is further protected, since its opening bid in a tax deed sale includes half of the latest assessed value. Request a payoff and a certificate search before you sign a contract.

Frequently asked questions

What share of Sumter County is 65 or older?

Over half: the Census Bureau reports 57.6 percent.

When is the Sumter County homestead deadline?

March 1, filed with the Sumter County Property Appraiser.

Who hears assessment appeals in Sumter County?

The Value Adjustment Board, an independent five-member panel, with hearings run by special magistrates. The clerk serves as its clerk.

Can the board cut a Sumter County value for hardship?

No. The county's page says it cannot change an assessed value or grant an exemption or classification based on personal hardship.

Does a Sumter County seller pay a deed tax?

Yes: seventy cents per $100 of price, owed at the clerk's counter. The contract decides which party actually pays, and every signer stays liable to the state regardless.

Who bills and collects property tax in Monroe County, Florida?

In the Keys, valuation and collection sit in separate buildings. One elected office decides what a parcel is worth and who gets an exemption; another prints the notices and takes the payments. A seller in Key West and a seller in Key Largo deal with the same two offices, just at different counters.

The collector's page walks through the chain: the appraiser's January value, plus millage from the commission and other taxing bodies, becomes the roll that is certified for collection. Notices go to the address of record on that roll. Escrow lenders request the bill themselves, so the owner may only receive a copy.

Statute 197.122, quoted on that page, makes it the owner's job to learn what is due and pay it before delinquency, bill or no bill. A separate bill goes out for each parcel, matched to the way the deed is recorded, so an owner of two lots should expect two notices.

What does the Census say about housing in the Keys?

Monroe County has few people for its size. 80,406 residents for mid-2025, a 3.0 percent dip against 2020, and 983.04 square miles of land, which worked out to 84.3 people per square mile in 2020.

Price and tax planning start with the housing numbers. The five-year survey data gives $780,600 as the median value of an owner-occupied home, with 65.8 percent of units lived in by their owners and 56,009 units counted in 2025. Rent at the median is $1,999 a month. Older residents are 27.2 percent of the county, so the senior and homestead programs below see heavy use.

  • Veterans counted for 2020 to 2024: 5,674, so the veteran exemptions listed further down apply to a real share of owners.
  • Mean commute: 19.5 minutes.
  • Permits for new construction counted in 2025: 279, a small number for a county of this size.

Where can I deal with the Monroe County Tax Collector in person?

The tax collector runs five offices along the Keys, and every one of them handles property tax. The table below is taken from the office locations page and shows the property tax counters in each town.

Who lives in Monroe County, and what do they do for work?

The Census profile shows an older, higher-income and international county. About one resident in five was born abroad (19.8 percent), and 22.2 percent of those over age 5 use another language at home.

Visitor spending shows in the 2022 business numbers: accommodation and food services sales totaled $2,245,213 thousand, and retail sales were $2,157,198 thousand, or $26,430 per resident. In 2023 the county had 4,154 employer establishments and total employment of 37,134, up 5.4 percent from 2022.

  • College graduates: 38.6 percent of adults.
  • Broadband at home: 89.9 percent of households.

For a seller, this means a buyer pool that often includes second-home buyers and remote workers, who may pay a different amount in tax than the current owner does.

How should a Keys owner prepare an appeal or a correction?

Begin with the August proposed-tax notice. A value challenge uses a DR-486 petition that the clerk must receive within 25 days, so write the deadline on the notice the day it arrives.

A denied exemption has its own 30 day petition clock. Owners of furnished rentals or business equipment also file Form DR-405 by April 1.

  • Gather recent sales of similar properties on your island or key before you file.
  • Photograph any damage that existed on January 1, since value is set on that date.
  • Keep the notice and your filing receipt together.

Ask the appraiser for the comparable sales behind your value.

What is the Monroe County tax calendar for bills and discounts?

The collector's page says statements normally mail by November 1 and that March is the last month at full price.

  • November: 4 percent off.
  • December brings 3 percent.
  • January brings 2 percent, and February brings 1 percent.
  • March is the gross amount with no discount.

On April 1 an unpaid account turns delinquent, and tax certificates are sold by June 1. The collector's page lists three alternatives to a lump sum: a quarterly installment plan, a statutory partial payment plan and a homestead tax deferral program.

How do homestead and Save Our Homes affect a Keys sale?

A capped assessment is a benefit tied to the owner, and it ends when the house sells. In a county where the typical owned home is valued at $780,600, the distance between a long-held capped value and a fresh assessment can be wide.

The exemption takes up to $50,000 off taxable value if filed by March 1. Yearly growth in assessed value is held below the lesser of 3 percent or CPI, which the state chart pegs at 2.7 percent for 2026. After a sale, the next January 1 assessment starts from just value for the new owner. If you are buying again in Florida, ask the appraiser about portability, which has a three year window.

What other exemptions might a Monroe County owner have?

With 5,674 veterans and a 27.2 percent senior share, Monroe County owners often ask about relief tied to service and age. The state lists a $5,000 assessed value reduction for a disabled ex-servicemember, a homestead discount for qualifying veterans 65 and older, and a possible total exemption for permanent and total disability.

Seniors may also benefit from an optional local ordinance. Ask the property appraiser whether Monroe County or a city in it has adopted one, and what income limit applies.

How are taxes and deed costs handled when a Keys house closes?

The title company usually divides the sale year's tax between the parties on the settlement statement. A spring or summer closing happens before that year's bill exists, so the figure is an estimate.

Keys deeds carry state stamp tax at 70 cents per $100 of price (section 201.02), unlike Miami-Dade. Payment goes to the clerk. The clerk's page charges under section 28.24 start at $5.00 for the first page.

Unpaid taxes lead to a certificate sale and, years later, a clerk-run deed auction. Pay off any open year before closing.

Pay by March 31. That is when the gross amount falls due, and April 1 starts delinquency. Earlier payment, November through February, shrinks the bill by 4, 3, 2 or 1 percent.

Who answers questions about a lost Monroe County bill?

The tax collector. Its property tax page lists (305) 295-5044 for missing statements, and each parcel gets its own bill according to how the deed is recorded.

Does a Keys homeowner's capped value go to the buyer?

No. The buyer's first assessment starts at just value. You may be able to carry part of the savings to your next Florida homestead through portability.

Can I pay Monroe County taxes in installments?

Yes, through the tax collector's quarterly installment plan, a statutory partial payment option or a homestead deferral. State guidance sets May 1 as the application date.

Who runs a tax deed auction in Monroe County?

The county clerk holds the auction, as the collector's public records page says, so overbid or surplus questions go to the clerk.

Why does Nassau County's growth matter for a home sale?

106,879 residents in 2025 against 90,352 counted in the 2020 census, a rise of 18.3 percent on the revised base, inside 648.68 square miles of land.

What does the Nassau County Tax Collector say about estimating a tax bill?

The same page explains that the property appraiser can help estimate upcoming taxes, but that office does not see non-ad valorem assessments such as community development district fees. Those fees are added to the bill separately, and the estimate must come from the district itself. If your Nassau neighborhood sits inside a district, tell your buyer so that the closing numbers include it.

Sellers can use this to set expectations early. A buyer reading your old bill may expect a lower figure than reality, and a clear note about reassessment avoids a surprise at the table.

Nassau County skews toward families who own their homes and commute. Median household income of $89,804 for 2020 to 2024 and per capita income of $47,685, with 8.7 percent of residents below the poverty line. Broadband subscriptions reach 94.6 percent of households, and 87.4 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier.

Employer establishments numbered 2,261 in 2023, with total employment of 21,651. Accommodation and food services brought in $613,642 thousand in 2022, and retail sales were $1,305,109 thousand, or $13,341 per resident.

What is the Nassau County bill-and-discount schedule?

Payment runs on a sliding monthly discount that ends March 31. Anything left unpaid becomes delinquent April 1.

  • November payment: 4 percent off.
  • December: 3 percent.
  • January: 2 percent.
  • February: 1 percent.

Florida's revenue department places the property appraiser's notice of proposed taxes in August, public budget hearings in September and October, and tax bills in November. A value challenge goes to the clerk's value adjustment board petition process within 25 days of the notice of proposed property taxes.

For questions about a bill, call the tax collector's tax department at 904-491-7420, the number printed on its partial payment page.

What should a Nassau County seller tell a buyer about the tax bill?

Give the buyer the parcel's real situation, not a rule of thumb. The tax collector's own advice is that a buyer should never rely on a seller's current or past tax amount, and a clear explanation protects both sides before a contract is signed.

  • Say whether a homestead exemption and a capped value are on the roll today, and that neither carries over.
  • Name any community development district or other non-ad valorem assessment, and give the buyer the district's contact so the buyer can ask for the amount.
  • Explain whether taxes are escrowed. If a lender pays, partial payments are discouraged and the lender sets the timing.
  • Mention any unpaid prior year, since the lien follows the land.

A buyer who learns these things at the start is less likely to ask for a credit late in the deal. Sellers who offer a plain written summary, along with a printout from the property appraiser's estimate tool, make closing day smoother. A tax bill estimate from the appraiser will leave out district fees, so ask the title company to add them.

How do exemptions and capped values work for Nassau owners?

Exemptions come from the property appraiser, who takes applications each year. With 26.7 percent of residents age 65 or older and 8,635 veterans, the senior and military programs see steady use in Nassau.

A county or city may adopt an extra senior exemption within an income limit, and another ordinance may help long-term residents with lower-value homes. Ask the property appraiser which of these apply in Nassau County or its towns.

  • A $5,000 reduction in assessed value for a disabled ex-servicemember.
  • A homestead discount for veterans 65 or older with a permanent service-connected disability.

Is a partial payment allowed in Nassau County?

It is allowed, with costs spelled out by the collector. Section 197.374 allows partial payment on a current-year bill, and the office accepts them from November 1 through March 31 with the postmark counting.

  • The account loses the early-payment discount, even if the balance is later cleared in a discount month.
  • Escrowed accounts paid by a lender should not make partial payments.
  • Accounts on an installment plan should skip partial payments.
  • Whatever is unpaid on April 1 enters the delinquent process of advertising and a certificate sale.

To set one up, contact the tax department at 904-491-7420 or taxes@nassautaxes.com. Payments can be made in person, by mail or online once the account is set up.

What happens to unpaid Nassau County taxes?

The tax collector must hold a tax certificate sale on or before June 1, and it is conducted online on the LienHub platform. The table lays out the terms as the office prints them.

Nassau tax certificate terms
ItemAs printed
Sale deadlineOn or before June 1 each year
BiddingDownward on interest, starting at 18 percent; lowest bidder wins
Minimum earned5 percent until accrued interest exceeds it; zero-interest bids earn zero
Lien statusEnforceable first lien on the real estate
ValiditySeven years from issuance
Tax deed applicationWhen two or more years have passed since delinquency

To remove the lien, the owner pays the collector all delinquent tax plus interest, costs and other charges. State law also bars a certificate holder from demanding payment from the owner for two years after April 1 of the issuance year, and a deed application carries a $75 fee. Homestead land with a small delinquency goes to the county rather than to a bidder.

How do homestead rules and deed taxes affect a Nassau County sale?

The standard exemption takes up to $50,000 off taxable value, filed by March 1, and the capped assessment growth was 2.7 percent for 2026 per the state chart. A buyer's value starts over after a sale.

Deed stamps in Nassau follow section 201.02 at 70 cents on every $100 of price. Liability sits with all parties to the deed, and payment goes to the clerk at recording.

Frequently asked questions

Does a new Nassau County owner get the seller's tax amount?

No. The tax collector says the buyer does not benefit from the prior owner's assessed value, Save Our Homes cap or exemptions, so past bills are not a safe estimate.

Do community development district fees show on the appraiser's estimate?

No. The appraiser has no access to non-ad valorem assessments, so ask the district for its amount, which is then added to the tax bill.

Do I lose the discount if I make a partial payment in Nassau County?

Yes. Per the tax collector, the account is no longer eligible for discount even if the rest is paid during a discount month. Partial payments run November 1 through March 31.

When does Nassau County sell tax certificates?

The sale is held by June 1 each year on the LienHub site. Bids start at 18 percent and fall, and the lowest rate takes the certificate.

How long before a tax deed can be sought on a Nassau County parcel?

The certificate holder may apply when two or more years have passed since delinquency. Until then, the owner can redeem by paying taxes, interest, costs and charges.

Walton County, FL Property Tax Guide: Offices, Dates and Selling With Tax Due

Cash Home Buyers in Florida
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Walton County, FL Property Tax Guide: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is
  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Walton County, FL Property Tax Guide sale
  • Turn the Walton County, FL Property Tax Guide offer down and you owe us nothing

Owe Walton County Property Tax? Get a Cash Offer

We buy Walton County houses as-is.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Where do Walton County owners deal with property taxes?

Walton County owners work with the tax collector, who bills and collects, and the property appraiser, who sets values and exemptions. The tax collector's office runs three branches: the DeFuniak Springs courthouse for north Walton, the Santa Rosa Beach courthouse annex for south Walton, and a Freeport office. The mailing address is a post office box in DeFuniak Springs.

The collector's site shows the branches open on weekdays into late afternoon, with a slightly later Wednesday start. Property tax questions about the estimated tax on a TRIM notice go to the property appraiser, while payment and delinquency questions go to the collector's office.

Because the county stretches from the Gulf coast to the inland towns, a seller may live a long way from the office that holds the file. Online payment and the parcel search save the trip.

What is the Walton County property tax calendar?

The tax collector publishes a month by month list, and it is more detailed than most Florida counties. Here are the entries that matter to a home seller.

Walton County Tax Collector calendar for real estate taxes
MonthEntry on the collector's page
January2% discount
February1% discount
MarchExemptions due to the Property Appraiser by March 1; full amount due by March 31; fourth installment due March 31
AprilUnpaid real estate tax delinquent April 1 with a 3% charge; installment plan applications for next year due April 30
MayDelinquent real estate taxes advertised once a week for three weeks; certificate sale on or before June 1
June to SeptemberFirst installment due June 30, second due September 30
NovemberBills mailed; 4% discount through November 30
December3% discount; third installment due December 31

Source: Walton County Tax Collector, important tax dates. The page also notes the property appraiser mails the TRIM notice in August.

How does the Walton County installment plan work?

The plan splits the year into four payments, with a discount on the first three. The tax collector's installment page and calendar describe it this way.

  • Applications for the following year are due April 30.
  • The prior year's tax must exceed $100.00 and not be paid through escrow.
  • June 30 brings the first installment, carrying a 6% discount, September 30 the second at 4.5%, the third December 31 with 3%, and the fourth March 31 with no discount.
  • The first two payments are each one quarter of the previous year's taxes.
  • If the first payment is missed, the owner is out of the plan for the year. The calendar says the first installment must be received by July 31 or participation ends.

Enrolled taxpayers do not need to reapply each year. A seller on the plan should ask the collector for the balance left after each payment, since the later installments are adjusted after the roll is set.

What happens when Walton County taxes become delinquent?

On April 1 unpaid real estate tax is delinquent and a 3% charge is added to the gross amount. Tangible personal property tax is different: it picks up 1.5% interest per month.

The collector then runs the delinquent list in the DeFuniak Herald for three straight weeks, and the advertising and auction fee is added to the bill. The certificate sale follows, scheduled by June 1 as an online auction at lienhub.com/county/walton. Bidding starts at 18% and drops in quarter-percent steps, with a 5% minimum interest unless the bid is zero. A certificate is good for seven years.

Once the holder has waited two years from the April 1 delinquency date, an application for a tax deed is possible. The collector states that tax deed sales are set by the Clerk of Court and run online at walton.realforeclose.com, and that the owner may redeem until the clerk signs the tax deed. Delinquent taxes can be paid by cash, cashier's check, money order or card, with a convenience fee on card payments.

How do exemptions and the March 1 date affect a Walton County seller?

Exemptions follow the owner, so a sale ends the seller's homestead and the buyer must file their own. The tax collector's calendar sets the filing date at March 1 with the property appraiser, the same date the state taxpayer guide gives (link).

The state homestead exemption is up to $50,000, the first $25,000 for all taxes and an additional amount for non-school taxes on value above $50,000, according to the state homestead guide. Owners lose homestead if they rent the property or stop living there.

The tax collector also has a page on military property taxes. Servicemembers who rent a homestead out are covered by a separate state provision, so ask the collector if that applies.

Who pays the taxes when a Walton County home sells?

The contract decides, and closings in Florida normally prorate taxes to the day of closing. The title agent asks the collector for the current balance, including any certificate, and pays it from the seller's side of the statement.

The clerk collects deed stamps at filing, at 70 cents on each $100 of price, and every party to the document is liable whoever agrees to pay, per the stamp tax page. Clerk filing charges come from s. 28.24, which starts at $5.00 for a first page and adds $4.00 per further page, with extra per-page charges.

For a house with a tax certificate, the redemption has to be paid before or at closing. A buyer who sees a certificate issued more than two years ago should ask the Clerk of Court whether a tax deed application is pending.

How should a Walton County owner with unpaid taxes plan a sale?

Contact the tax collector first, because each month moves the cost. A sale before April avoids the 3% charge and the advertising fee, while one after the certificate sale carries interest and fees.

  • Search the parcel on the tax collector's payment portal for the current balance.
  • Ask whether a certificate exists and what rate it sold at.
  • Check homestead status with the property appraiser before March 1.
  • Tell the title company so the payoff is ordered ahead of the closing date.

How are Walton County tangible personal property taxes treated?

Tax on business equipment follows a harsher track than real estate. The tax collector's calendar says unpaid tangible personal property tax is delinquent April 1 and picks up 1.5% interest for each month.

Within 45 days after the March 31 deadline, those delinquent accounts are advertised in a local newspaper at the owner's cost. A list is published once in May, and warrant processing begins June 1. A landlord or small business owner selling a rental with equipment inside should ask the collector whether a personal property account sits under the same owner name.

  • Discounts match real estate: 4% in November, 3% in December, 2% in January, 1% in February.
  • Delinquent real estate carries a flat 3% charge, not monthly interest.
  • Different advertising rules apply to each, so ask which list a parcel is on.

What does a Walton County tax certificate holder have to wait for?

The holder cannot move fast. A certificate on a Walton County parcel is valid for seven years, and the holder may apply for a tax deed only two years after the April 1 delinquency date. Under state law the holder also may not contact the owner to demand payment during the first two years, per the statute on certificate sales.

For the seller, that window is time to arrange a sale. Many owners use it to list the house, find a buyer, and let the closing agent redeem the certificate from proceeds. Ask the collector for the redemption total on the planned closing date, because interest runs by the month.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

When do Walton County property taxes become delinquent?

April 1. The Walton County Tax Collector says unpaid real estate tax is delinquent on that date and a 3% charge is added to the gross amount.

What is the Walton County installment plan discount?

6% on the first installment, 4.5% on the second, 3% on the third and none on the fourth. Applications are due April 30.

Where does Walton County hold its tax certificate sale?

Online, at lienhub.com/county/walton, on or before June 1. Bidding starts at 18% and goes down in quarter-percent steps.

Can I still keep my house after a Walton County tax certificate is sold?

Yes. The owner may redeem until the Clerk of Court signs the tax deed. A tax deed application cannot be filed until two years after the April 1 delinquency date.

When is the Walton County exemption deadline?

March 1. The tax collector's calendar says exemptions are due to the Property Appraiser's Office by that date.

Putnam County, FL Property Tax Guide: Offices, Dates and Selling With Tax Due

Cash Home Buyers in Florida

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Which Putnam County offices send the bill and value the house?

In Putnam County the appraiser sets the value and decides exemptions, while the Tax Collector bills, collects and distributes the money. Changes to name, address or assessed value on the roll go through the appraiser, not the collector.

The appraiser's main office is at 312 Oak Street in Palatka, with a mailing box at PO Box 1920, Palatka, FL 32178. Crescent City and Interlachen have satellite offices that open on set days: Crescent City on Mondays and Wednesdays, Interlachen on Tuesdays and Thursdays. The exemption department's number is (386) 329-0286. The Tax Collector keeps its property tax pages at putnamtax.com and runs tax certificate sales through an online bidding site.

  • Property Appraiser: value, exemptions, tangible personal property, roll corrections.
  • Tax Collector: bills, discounts, installments, delinquent taxes and certificates.
  • Clerk of the Court: tax deed sales and recorded deeds.

Which taxing authorities appear on a Putnam County bill?

A Putnam bill can carry lines from the county, a fire district, the school board, two water management districts and one of five municipalities. The Tax Collector's property tax page lists each one with a phone number so you can ask the right office about its rate.

That list names the county, the Fire MSTU District, the Putnam County School Board, the St. Johns River Water Management District, the Suwannee Water Management District, and the City of Palatka, City of Crescent City, Town of Interlachen, Town of Pomona Park and Town of Welaka. A parcel inside a city pays that city's levy in addition to the county's.

Non-ad valorem charges sit beside the tax lines. The county enacted a solid waste special assessment for residential units, split between landfill improvements, garbage collection and recycling. The commissioners have also authorized 28 separate MSBU projects for road maintenance or paving, which charge only the properties that benefit. The Hastings Drainage District levies its own assessment. A buyer or seller can see these on the bill, and homestead exemption does not reduce them.

What is the Putnam County payment schedule?

Value is fixed on January 1 and bills usually open for collection on November 1. The gross amount is due by March 31, and any unpaid real estate taxes go delinquent April 1.

Putnam County Tax Collector discount schedule for current real estate taxes
Payment monthDiscount
November4%
December3%
January2%
February1%
MarchNone, gross amount due

The collector also offers a quarterly installment plan for owners whose estimated bill is more than $100. The application must reach the office by April 30 of the year you want to start. Payments fall due June 30 (6% discount), September 30 (4.5%), December 31 (3%) and March 31 (no discount). Missing the June payment removes the account from the plan, and under s. 197.222 the owner cannot rejoin until the next year with a new application. The first two payments use the prior year's taxes and the last two use the new roll.

What happens to an unpaid Putnam County bill?

Delinquent parcels are run in a local newspaper in three weekly ads in a row, then a tax certificate sale is held online by June 1. The certificate is a lien and does not convey ownership.

Bidding starts at 18% and drops in quarter percent steps until the lowest bidder takes the certificate. After the sale, the Tax Collector's FAQ says the owner could pay interest up to 18% a year, depending on the bid rate. After delinquency the office takes cashier's check, certified check, cash or money order, and the day it receives the payment sets the amount due.

  • In most cases, if taxes stay unpaid two years from April 1, the certificate holder can file a tax deed application.
  • Applications go through RealTDA, and the county posts a Lands Available for Taxes list for parcels that did not sell.
  • Paying the taxes cancels the lien, but all payments after delinquency must be in certified funds.

Anyone selling a house with a certificate on it needs a redemption quote from the collector, passed to the closing agent early, because interest accrues until the lien is cleared.

What homestead and senior exemptions does the Putnam County appraiser offer?

The county appraiser's exemption page says the homestead exemption removes the first $25,000 of value from every ad valorem levy, and that special assessments are untouched by it. The Palatka office takes applications year-round, and the satellite offices join in during the first two months of the year.

Every exemption has a March 1 deadline, counted from the year after you buy. After that date you must also complete an Extenuating Circumstances form. The applicant must hold title, be a Florida permanent resident and treat the home as a primary residence on the assessment date. Proof of residency includes a Florida driver license or ID showing the home address and a Florida vehicle registration. Trust-owned homes face stricter review.

  • Low income senior exemption: a county ordinance adds $25,000 against the county general millage for homeowners aged 65 and over who meet the income limit; the office tells applicants to ask for the current limit.
  • Super Senior exemption: for 25-year residents with a just value under $250,000, which exempts the whole assessed value where a taxing authority has enacted it. The page names Putnam County, Palatka, Crescent City, Interlachen, Pomona Park and Welaka.
  • Deployed service member, total and permanent disability and first responder exemptions, each with their own proof requirements.

Once approved, an exemption renews automatically, but the owner must report changes in use or status right away under ss. 196.131 and 196.161.

How does a sale change the next bill in Putnam County?

The buyer's next roll starts at just value, and any exemption you held stays behind. State rules treat a sale, foreclosure or transfer of title as a transfer of ownership, with exceptions for spouses and certain transfers at death.

A house held by one family for years can carry a bill that looks small next to what its new owner sees on the first full roll. The assessment cap, which the state's 2026 chart sets at 2.7%, applies only while the same owner keeps the homestead. If you are moving within Florida, the portability form can carry up to $500,000 of your accrued benefit to the new homestead, filed with the exemption application by March 1.

The deed also carries documentary stamps at $0.70 per $100 of price, paid through the Clerk at recording. Anyone named on the deed is liable, even when the contract assigns payment to one side.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What should a Putnam County seller check before listing?

Check three things before listing: the current bill is paid or will be settled at closing, no tax certificate exists, and the exemption record matches how the house is used. Homestead ends if the unit is rented or stops being the permanent home.

The Tax Collector and the appraiser are both in Palatka, and the roll is public. Print the parcel record and the bill, and hand both to the closing agent. Putnam parcels can carry MSBU road assessments and a solid waste charge, so ask whether any are unpaid, since they ride on the same bill as the taxes.

Frequently asked questions

How much can I save by paying a Putnam County bill early?

The discount starts at 4% for November, then steps down by a point each month through February. March carries none. Bills open for collection November 1.

What is the Putnam County delinquency date?

April 1. Anything unpaid after March 31 is delinquent the next day and heads for a certificate sale by June 1.

Does Putnam County offer a payment plan?

Yes. The quarterly plan needs an application in by April 30 and an estimated bill over $100, and its first three payments carry 6%, 4.5% and 3% discounts.

Where do I file for homestead in Putnam County?

File with the Property Appraiser in Palatka, or at the Crescent City or Interlachen satellite during the winter filing season. The cutoff is March 1 after you buy.

Can I lose my Putnam County house over unpaid taxes?

Eventually, yes. Once two years pass a certificate holder may seek a tax deed and the house can go to auction, though paying the full amount before the sale keeps it yours.

Levy County, FL Property Tax Guide: Offices, Dates and Selling With Tax Due

Cash Home Buyers in Florida
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Levy County, FL Property Tax Guide: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is
  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Levy County, FL Property Tax Guide sale

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Where do Levy County owners pay and question property tax?

Levy owners pay at the Tax Collector's Bronson headquarters, 310 School Street, Suite 102 (352-486-5172), or at one of two branches. Valuation sits with a different office, the Property Appraiser, on the same street in Bronson at (352) 486-5222.

  • Bronson main office: 310 School Street, Suite 102, Bronson, FL 32621, Monday to Friday, opening 8:30 and closing 4:30
  • Williston branch: 551 SW 1st Avenue, Williston, FL 32696, (352) 528-6091.
  • Chiefland branch: 226 North Main Street, Chiefland, FL 32626, (352) 493-4646.

Address changes cannot be made at the collector's counter, for real property or tangible accounts alike; they go through the appraiser. A seller should update the mailing address there so a stray bill finds the right person after closing.

What are the Levy County property tax dates?

Bills fall due on November 1, and a balance still open after the following March 31 is delinquent from April 1. The state discount shrinks from 4 percent in November by one point per month to 1 percent in February.

Reminder letters on unpaid accounts go out by April 30. A delinquent list is prepared in May for the newspaper and the web, and the certificate auction usually runs by May 31, with Chapter 197 requiring a start no later than June 1.

Upstream of the bill, the state calendar is just as fixed: value as of January 1, exemption filings by March 1, a proposed-tax notice in August, and 25 days from that notice to petition on value.

How can you pay Levy County property tax online, and what does it cost?

Cards cost extra online and e-check does not. The collector's site lists 2.3 percent on credit cards, a flat $1.75 for charges below $76, and nothing for an online e-check (ACH); processor fees do not reach the county.

At the counter, every payment draws 2.3 percent and e-checks are unavailable. Anything processed after 11:59 p.m. counts as the next calendar day, a trap near a deadline. A seller wanting a clean payoff can use an online e-check before midnight to dodge both the fee and the next-day rule.

Cards accepted are Visa, Master Card, American Express and Discover. Call 352-486-5172 on a weekday if the system gives trouble.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

What happens when Levy County property tax goes unpaid?

Delinquent tax is sold off as a certificate, a lien instead of a transfer of the house. Its face amount stacks the unpaid tax, 1.5 percent a month for April and May, a 5 percent collector commission, the advertising charge and the cost of the sale.

Levy County tax certificate terms, from the Tax Collector's tax sale page
ItemAs the office prints it
Sale methodOnline auction through West Florida Business Systems, on or before May 31
Bid range0 to 18 percent in 0.25 percent steps, lowest rate wins
Minimum interest if redeemed on or after June 15 percent (not for zero bids)
Unbid certificatesIssued to the county at 18 percent
Certificate life7 years
Holder may seek a tax deedAfter two years from April 1 of the issuance year

The delinquent list runs weekly for three weeks ahead of the auction. Certificate buyers must wait two years, counting from April 1 of the issuance year, before contacting the owner.

What does a Levy County tax deed application involve?

An applicant must complete these steps, and the office says the fee amounts can change without notice:

  • File a signed tax deed application.
  • Redeem any other outstanding certificates and pay current tax if owed.
  • Pay a $150 title search fee and a $75 application fee.

The county clerk then schedules the sale and charges advertising, mailing and sheriff costs.

Where homestead is on the current roll, the opening bid adds half the assessed value to taxes and costs. A parcel nobody bids on can join the list of lands available for taxes, and land left unsold there for 3 years reverts to Levy County. Unpaid government liens survive a tax deed under s. 197.552.

Timing is the practical point for an owner planning to sell. Get a payoff figure from the collector for any certificate before listing, since a title company will want each lien cleared at closing.

What should Levy County sellers know about agricultural classification?

Farm classification stays with the seller, not the land. The appraiser's page calls it non-transferable, so a buyer files a fresh application after any sale or transfer.

Filing runs January 1 through March 1. Per the statute the office cites, only land used mainly for bona fide agriculture, meaning good-faith commercial use, qualifies. Zoning alone earns nothing, and the use should exist on the January 1 assessment date, or a reasonable effort to start it must have been made.

Selling acreage? Tell the buyer which parcels carry the classification now, because a buyer who fails to qualify may face a higher assessment. Denials are mailed to the applicant, who can ask the appraiser to talk it through.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

How does the Levy County tax certificate auction treat bidders?

The sale runs online through West Florida Business Systems, and the Tax Collector says no deposits are required for the current format. Every bidder must submit a Participating Bidder Agreement after registering or logging in, plus an electronic W-9 each year.

The office also runs a test system so new bidders can practice, and bids made there do not carry over to the live sale. A certificate can be sold to another buyer if the endorsement form and a transfer fee of $2.25 per certificate reach the Tax Collector. The office warns that a certificate is not a guaranteed investment, and if no action is taken within the seven-year life while the tax stays unpaid, the certificate is cancelled. For an owner, this means the lien is held by a private investor who is barred from contacting you for the first two years but who may then apply for a deed.

Who lives in Levy County, and what do homes cost?

Levy County is rural: about 48,520 people live across 1,118 square miles, roughly 38 per square mile in the 2020 count, and the population has risen 13.1 percent since then.

Census data for 2020 to 2024 give an owner-occupied home a median value of $190,600, with 81.4 percent of 22,192 housing units lived in by owners, rent at $850 and household income at $56,750. Households number 18,562 at 2.43 people each, the median selected monthly owner cost with a mortgage is $1,297 and without one is $375, and only 16.5 percent of adults hold a bachelor's degree. Broadband subscriptions reach 80.8 percent of households, workers average a 30.4 minute commute, and builders pulled 244 permits in 2025. People 65 and over are 26.7 percent of the county, and 91.1 percent of residents stayed put in the previous year. Long tenure usually means a Save Our Homes assessment below market, which resets after a sale.

A Levy County deed carries Florida's 70 cents per $100 stamp tax, paid to the clerk at recording by whichever party the deal assigns, with every party liable.

Frequently asked questions

Where is the Levy County Tax Collector?

Headquarters: 310 School Street, Suite 102, Bronson. Branches: 551 SW 1st Avenue, Williston, and 226 North Main Street, Chiefland. All keep weekday hours.

Is there a fee to pay Levy County property tax online?

Cards add 2.3 percent, or $1.75 flat under $76, payable to the processor. Online e-checks cost nothing; office payments add 2.3 percent.

When does Levy County property tax become delinquent?

From April 1 following the bill. Reminders mail by April 30 and the certificate auction normally closes out by May 31.

Can a buyer keep my Levy County agricultural classification?

No, the appraiser calls it non-transferable. A buyer needs a new application by March 1 and must pass the bona fide agriculture test.

How soon can a tax deed be sought on unpaid Levy County tax?

Two years after the April 1 of the issuance year, a certificate holder may apply. If one exists on your parcel, request a payoff figure from the collector.

Which offices run property tax in Flagler?

In Flagler the Property Appraiser sets value. The Tax Collector sends notices and takes payment. Millage is set by the levying bodies: county commissioners, the school board, city commissions and others.

The Tax Collector's website, flaglertax.gov, has pages for property taxes, tangible personal property tax, tourist development tax, business tax receipts and veteran benefits. For questions about a value, an exemption or a classification, contact the Flagler County Property Appraiser directly and ask for the current forms and filing dates. Deeds are recorded, and foreclosure and tax deed auctions are run, by the circuit court clerk.

How are Flagler County property taxes billed?

Flagler bills after the year ends, and notices land around the start of November. The Tax Collector explains that the tax year runs January 1 to December 31 and payment begins November 1 of that year, and its homepage notes that real estate and tangible personal property bills are mailed October 31.

The process runs in a set order:

  • The Property Appraiser establishes values and applies exemptions to complete the tax roll.
  • The certified roll goes to the Tax Collector.
  • The Tax Collector merges in non-ad valorem assessments, which are set amounts that do not depend on value and appear on the same notice.
  • The notice is mailed to the owner's last address on the roll.

If a mortgage servicer pays from escrow, the servicer can request the bill under criteria set by the Tax Collector, and the owner gets a copy for information.

What else does the Flagler Tax Collector handle for property owners?

Beyond the real estate bill, the office runs several accounts that matter to landlords and sellers who own rental or business property. Its website lists these as separate service pages.

  • Tangible personal property tax, which applies to furnishings and equipment used in a rental or business.
  • Tourist development tax, owed on short stays in a rental.
  • Business tax receipts for operating a business in the county.
  • Veteran benefits information.
  • Online payments for tax bills.

An owner closing out a rental should ask the office to confirm that each of these accounts is current and closed, because a balance on one can surface long after the deed records. The same counter also handles driver license and vehicle registration work. Plates on passenger cars and similar vehicles expire at midnight on the owner's birthday, which is a useful reminder when you update your address after a move.

If you cannot visit in person, use the online payment page rather than a link from a text or email. The office has warned that fraudulent texts are circulating in the state agency's name.

What if a Flagler tax bill never arrives?

Nonreceipt is no defense. The Tax Collector cites section 197.122, which tells owners to learn the amount due and pay before delinquency, mailed bill or not.

This catches sellers who moved out, landlords whose tenants get the mail and heirs at a house with an outdated address. The Tax Collector's lobbies may close at 4 p.m. when crowded, and the office warns about text messages that falsely claim to come from the state motor vehicle agency, so check the account yourself on the official site.

Can Flagler owners pay in installments or defer?

Both options exist, and the Tax Collector takes the requests. Installment requests are due on May 1 during the assessment year, and a deferral request on Form DR-570 is due March 31 after it.

Deferral lets a homestead owner postpone the part of the bill that exceeds a share of household income. The share is 5 percent for most owners and 3 percent for a permanent resident 65 or older. Partial payments before delinquency are accepted only if the Tax Collector chooses to take them. Ask how Flagler handles an installment plan before you plan around it, since the May deadline falls well before bills are mailed.

Does my Flagler assessment cap follow the house to a buyer?

The new owner starts at full just value. The seller's capped assessment does not transfer, because a change of title resets the parcel the next January, with exceptions such as spousal transfers.

While a homestead is held, the yearly assessed increase stops at the lower of 3 percent or inflation. DOR's chart prints 2.7 percent for 2026. Sellers moving inside Florida can port part of that benefit to a new home if they claim it within three years. Both forms reach the Property Appraiser by that same March 1 deadline.

Which veteran breaks can Flagler County owners ask about?

The Tax Collector's site has a veteran benefits page, and the Property Appraiser handles the exemptions themselves. Florida's list is short.

  • A $5,000 cut in assessed value for a disabled ex-servicemember rated 10 percent or more.
  • A homestead discount tied to the VA rating for a veteran 65 or older with a permanent service-connected disability.
  • A deployment-based exemption on Form DR-501M.

Ask the Property Appraiser what proof each one needs, and bring discharge or VA rating papers to that conversation.

What if a Flagler County parcel reaches a tax deed auction?

After a certificate has aged two years, its holder may ask for a deed, and the clerk then auctions the parcel publicly. The tax collector assembles the notice list: titleholder, mortgagees, lienholders, the assessed party and any recorded contract buyer.

  • The top bidder leaves a nonrefundable deposit, set at the larger of 5 percent of the bid or $200.
  • The balance, stamps and recording costs are due inside 24 hours, excluding weekends and holidays.
  • An unsold parcel joins the county's lands-available list.

An owner who sells ahead of the auction can redeem from proceeds. Ask the Flagler Tax Collector for a redemption figure, since interest makes it move.

What happens to a Flagler tax bill at closing?

Closing agents confirm the account and pay what is owed from the seller's proceeds. Get the parcel balance from the Tax Collector's office. The clerk collects deed stamps at recording, at a statewide rate of 70 cents on each $100 of price.

A parcel with a certificate attached can still be sold. Settle the certificate at the table so the buyer gets a clean title.

Frequently asked questions

When does Flagler County mail property tax bills?

Around the start of November. The Tax Collector's site says real estate and tangible personal property bills are mailed October 31, and payment begins November 1.

What if I never receive my Flagler County tax bill?

You still owe the tax. Section 197.122 puts the duty on the owner to find out the amount and pay before the delinquency date, so contact the Tax Collector and the Property Appraiser.

Can I defer Flagler County property tax?

A homestead owner can apply on Form DR-570 by March 31 after the assessment year. Deferral covers tax above 5 percent of household income, or 3 percent for a permanent resident 65 or older.

Does my homestead cap transfer to the buyer of my Flagler County house?

No. A sale resets the property to just value the next January 1. You may be able to port part of your cap to a new Florida homestead.

Who sets Flagler County millage rates?

The levying bodies do: county commissioners, the school board, city commissions and other authorities. The Property Appraiser sets value, not the rate.

What makes Highlands County property tax different?

Highlands County is a large, mostly rural county, and that shapes how its tax roll works. The property appraiser says the county covers about 1,029 square miles of land, roughly 658,000 acres, with around 113,000 parcels, 60,000 buildings, 6,000 business accounts and 10,000 tangible personal property accounts on mobile homes.

Farmland is a big piece of that roll: about 75,000 acres of citrus, 275,000 acres of pasture and thousands of acres of cropland. The office also administers over 24,000 homestead exemptions. The tax collector serves the county from locations in Sebring and Avon Park, and the Highlands County Tax Collector posts the payment and deadline pages used below.

When is Highlands County property tax due?

Bills are mailed by October 31, collection begins in November, and the full amount is due by March 31. Anything unpaid or not postmarked by March 31 is delinquent on April 1, when interest and fees begin.

The appraiser's FAQ lists the early payment discounts as a four, three, two and one percent sequence running November through February. It adds that Highlands taxes are paid in arrears for the calendar year, January through December, which matters at a closing because the seller owes part of a year that the buyer will be billed for.

  • Installment plan: apply by April 30 for the next tax year; payments fall in June (6% discount), September (4.5%), December (3%) and March (final, no discount).
  • Missed first payment: an account without the first installment by July 31 is removed from the plan and gets a full bill in October.
  • Homestead deferral: the county tax collector lists January 31 as its filing deadline for the deferral program.

What dates should a Highlands County owner mark?

The county's calendar runs from the January 1 valuation through the April 1 delinquency, with a handful of deadlines that catch sellers off guard.

Highlands County property tax calendar from the tax collector and appraiser pages
MonthEvent
January 31Homestead tax deferral filing deadline
March 1New homestead exemptions and agricultural classification applications
April 1Unpaid taxes delinquent
April 30Installment plan applications due
On or before June 1Tax certificate sale
AugustTRIM notices mailed
October 31Bills mailed

In May, delinquent real estate accounts are advertised three times in a local newspaper, and delinquent tangible personal property accounts once.
