How do homestead and agricultural classification work in Highlands County?

New homestead exemptions must be filed with the Highlands County Property Appraiser by March 1. The appraiser says the exemption is free to anyone who qualifies, and that it can be handled in minutes at the office or at visits to municipal sites around the county.

The office warns that new owners sometimes receive mailings offering a reduction in taxable value for a fee. It says such offers amount to the savings the homestead exemption already gives, and that the paid service is generally just information on how to apply.

Agricultural land follows a different rule. An application must be filed with the appraiser before March 1 of the tax year, and only land used in good faith for commercial agriculture qualifies. Once granted, the classification renews each year. A dwelling on the parcel does not disqualify the land, though the home site is assessed at just value. Citrus is valued by variety, and the office adjusts assessments when disease or freeze damage affects production, and it avoids entering groves because of disease concerns.

How can a Highlands County owner challenge a value or exemption?

Petition the Value Adjustment Board before the deadline printed on the TRIM notice, with a notarized petition and a $50 filing fee per parcel. The board has three county commissioners and two school board members, and it usually appoints special masters who are independent of the appraiser's office to hear cases.

  • For a value dispute, bring sales of comparable properties from the prior year, before January 1, or an appraisal.
  • For an exemption denial, show you qualified as of January 1.
  • The board cannot reduce a bill for hardship or because the value rose from last year.
  • A losing petitioner may sue in circuit court under section 194.171.

The board's clerk mails a record of decision within 20 days of the ruling. The appraiser notes that millage is set by the county, cities, school board and water management districts, so neither the board nor the appraiser can change a rate. A household that cannot meet an increase may qualify for a deferral or the installment plan through the tax collector.

What happens if Highlands County property tax goes unpaid?

An unpaid Highlands County account goes to a tax certificate sale by June 1, once the newspaper notices have run. A tax deed application can be filed by the certificate holder once two years have passed since delinquency, and no later than seven years after the certificate was first issued.

Interest to the applicant runs 1.5 percent monthly, per the tax collector, from the month after the application until the account is redeemed or sold, and that the applicant is not guaranteed the property. The Highlands County Clerk of Courts schedules and runs the sale. Under state rules, a homestead parcel owing under $250 has its certificate issued to the county and not auctioned, and a homestead opening bid at a deed sale includes half of the last assessed value.

A seller facing a certificate can still close. Payoff from proceeds redeems the lien before a deed application is filed.

How should you handle Highlands County property tax when selling?

Order a payoff figure before listing, and decide whether the bill has been issued for the year. Bills go to the owner of record, and a recorded deed is what puts the new owner on the appraiser's roll.

The appraiser's database does not hold items such as special assessments for solid waste collection or fire and road improvement districts, though they appear on the tax bill. The complete bill, non-ad valorem charges included, comes from the tax collector rather than the property record. For a split lot or merged parcels, the appraiser says a survey is needed to split, all taxes on the parcels must be paid, and a mortgage holder must approve in writing.

The state's documentary stamp tax on a deed is a rate of 70 cents for each $100 paid, and a change of ownership returns the capped assessment to just value on the next January 1. For a current millage figure, check the TRIM notice or ask the appraiser.

Frequently asked questions

When is Highlands County property tax due?

The whole bill is owed by March 31, and April 1 marks delinquency. Bills are mailed October 31, and the discount starts at 4 percent in November, slipping a point a month to 1 percent in February.

How do I join the Highlands County installment plan?

Applications go to the tax collector by April 30 for the coming tax year. Payments are due in June, September, December and March, with discounts of 6%, 4.5% and 3% on the first three, and nothing on the last.

What is the filing deadline for a Highlands County homestead exemption?

March 1, filed with the Highlands County Property Appraiser. The exemption is free to qualified owners, and the office advises ignoring paid mailers that offer to reduce taxable value for a fee.

Can I petition the Value Adjustment Board in Highlands County?

Yes, before the deadline on your TRIM notice. The petition is notarized and costs $50 per parcel, and hardship or a rise in value from last year does not alone support a reduction.

Who runs the Highlands County tax deed sale?

The Clerk of Courts schedules and conducts the sale. A certificate holder applies through the tax collector's vendor after two years from the date of delinquency, and the holder is not guaranteed to obtain the property.

What deadline governs a Columbia County tax bill?

The regular annual bill is due by March 31, and unpaid taxes generally become delinquent April 1. The bill arrives in November, and the early-payment discount starts at 4% that month and falls one point each month through February.

A TRIM notice in August is a proposal, not the payment bill. The tax collector says a proposed-tax notice differs from the annual bill, so check it for values, exemptions and hearing dates. Qualifying payments get next-working-day treatment under Florida law when the due date lands on a weekend or holiday, though a close call deserves a phone call.

How can I pay a Columbia County tax bill?

Payment is possible online, by phone, at the counter, through the mail, or at the Lake City drive-through and drop box. The office lists a 2.5% card fee with a $2 minimum and a $1.50 e-check fee for online or phone payments, and says it receives no part of the card fee.

How does the Columbia County calendar run from month to month?

The tax collector publishes a year-at-a-glance calendar, and its main points are easy to plan around. Columbia County sellers and buyers can use it to see which weeks are likely to bring a bill, a discount change or interest on a late balance, and which dates matter most before a closing.

  • April 1: unpaid taxes generally become delinquent, and tangible personal property returns are due to the appraiser.
  • April 30: installment applications are due.
  • May: delinquent-tax advertising and certificate sale preparation begin.
  • June 30 and September 30: the first two installments fall due.
  • November: annual collection starts at the 4% discount.

The office stresses that the calendar is a planning guide, and that late-mailed bills, weekends and holidays can move a deadline. Follow the dates on your own notice and call about late-mailed bills.

How do the quarterly installments work in Columbia County?

The installment plan lets an owner prepay the current year in four payments if estimated tax is over $100 per notice. Submit Form DR-534 to the tax collector by April 30. The first payment confirms participation.

The first two installments use prior-year tax as the estimate, and later ones adjust to actual tax. A late first installment is accepted through July 31 without the June discount. The plan does not cover delinquent taxes.

Can I make partial payments on Columbia County property tax?

Yes, on current taxes from November 1 through March 31, by signing a partial-payment agreement with the office. No early-payment discounts apply to partial payments, and the full balance must be paid by March 31.

Tracking is the owner's job, and the published local plan mails no balance reminder before April 1. State law leaves partial payments to the tax collector's discretion before delinquency.

What homestead and tax relief programs apply in Columbia County?

The Property Appraiser decides homestead, disability, widow or widower, veteran, senior and agricultural benefits. March 1 is the usual filing deadline. The homestead exemption reaches $50,000, and its first $25,000 also lowers school tax.

Save Our Homes ties a homestead's yearly assessment growth to 3 percent or the CPI change, whichever is lower, and the next January 1 after a sale brings the parcel back to just value. A disabled ex-servicemember may take a $5,000 cut in assessed value. Veterans aged 65 or over with a lasting service-connected disability may receive a discount matching the VA disability rating. A deferral request for homestead tax is filed with the collector by March 31 after the assessment year.

The tax collector's page also mentions income-based help and certain vacancy reductions for service assessments. Call to confirm which one fits.

How is unpaid Columbia County tax handled at a house closing?

Closing agents usually pay the current year out of the seller's proceeds, and the collector can confirm what posted. Ask for an exact payoff for your closing date, since interest and costs change the amount.

Section 197.502 lets a certificate holder seek a tax deed once two years have passed since April 1 of the issue year, and the clerk's office holds the sale. Redemption is available until a tax deed is issued, unless the buyer has paid the clerk in full, so call the Tax Department at 386-758-1080 with your parcel number before any sale date. The office accepts cash, money order, cashier's check or card for certificate redemption and cautions against assuming a personal check works.

What else can appear on a Columbia County tax bill?

Besides value-based tax, the bill can carry non-ad valorem assessments for services such as fire, solid waste, paving or lighting, according to the parcel's location. The county, city or district that creates an assessment sets it, and the tax collector only bills what the tax roll certifies.

Business equipment is a different account. Business equipment returns generally reach the appraiser by April 1, and unpaid accounts can lead to tax warrants rather than a certificate sale. Anyone selling a house that hosted a business should ask both offices whether an equipment account is open under the same name.

Mailing address changes are another trap. The tax roll address comes from the Property Appraiser, so a new owner who wants the November bill sent elsewhere should ask that office to update the record. The collector also takes a forwarding request.

Contact the Property Appraiser first, then use the Value Adjustment Board if needed. A value petition reaches the clerk within 25 days of the Notice of Proposed Property Taxes, and an exemption denial can be appealed in the 30 days after a denial letter goes out.

Payment questions and value disputes go to separate offices, and a petition does not replace paying the bill the tax collector sends in November.

What does the Jackson County calendar say about delinquent accounts?

Real property tax left unpaid on April 1 picks up a 3% penalty. Can Jackson County owners spread payments over the year?

  • First payment: due on or before June 1, with cancellation if nothing arrives by June 30.
  • Second payment: before September 30.

Which homestead and assessment limits matter to a Jackson County seller?

Homestead in Jackson County works as it does statewide: live in the house on January 1, file DR-501 by March 1, and up to $50,000 comes off assessed value. Only the first $25,000 lowers school tax.

Growth in a homestead's assessed value is held to the lesser of 3 percent or inflation, and the state's chart lists 2.7 percent for 2026. Non-homestead parcels face a 10 percent cap. Selling ends both, so a buyer's first bill often exceeds the seller's last.

The notice said the discussion would cover the possible effect on local funding for public safety, fire and emergency services and special districts. It describes the amendment as proposed, so no figures appear.

The October 13 meeting started at 6:00 p.m. Central Time at the Endeavor Convention Center, was free to attend, and invited local governments, law enforcement, fire and emergency medical services and special taxing districts to take part. That guest list shows who relies on property tax revenue in the county, and who may adjust budgets if the rules change.

What changes depends on the ballot result and any law that follows. Check the Florida Department of Revenue and county budget pages for the effective year before relying on a number in a sale. Until new rules are posted, use the dates and amounts on your own bill.

Do mobile homes and business equipment follow the same dates in Jackson County?

Partly. The collector's calendar treats tangible personal property, such as business furniture and equipment, on the same discount schedule as real estate, but with the harsher 1.5% monthly interest charge once it turns delinquent.

Mobile homes have their own line. A mobile home that is not assessed as real property needs its decal renewed by December 31, and the calendar puts registration of mobile homes, trucks over 8,000 pounds and truck-trailers in the same December window. If you own a mobile home on land you are selling, ask the tax collector whether it is billed as real property or carries a decal, since that decides which deadline you face.

Both points are worth raising with the closing agent early. Tell them whether the property includes a mobile home or business equipment, so that every account tied to it is identified and paid before the settlement date.

What should a Jackson County seller line up before closing?

Get the payoff in writing, with the tax year it covers. The title agent then divides the current year between buyer and seller at the closing table.

  • Use the portal's tax-year search to check whether earlier years remain open.
  • If April 1 has passed, ask about the penalty and advertising costs.
  • Look for recorded liens in the Clerk's records.
  • Hand the closing agent your installment history.

A seller racing a delinquency or certificate sale date can set a quick cash closing, with the tax paid out of proceeds by the title agent.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

What is the final day to pay Jackson County property tax without a penalty?

March 31 is the cutoff for the gross amount. Paying early earns 4% in November, then 3%, 2% and 1% in the following three months.

What penalty hits an unpaid Jackson County bill on April 1?

Real property takes a 3% penalty. Business equipment is charged 1.5% interest a month instead.

When does Jackson County hold its tax certificate sale?

The collector fixes the date in March, ahead of the April 1 delinquency date. The collector's announcements give the exact day.

Does Jackson County allow installment payments?

Yes. File by April 30 for next year's plan and pay in June, September, December and March. Ask the office for the exact June date.

Will selling raise the next owner's Jackson County bill?

Usually, yes. The Save Our Homes cap and the 10 percent limit both end at a sale, and the next January 1 resets the property to just value.

Hendry County, FL Property Tax Guide: Offices, Dates and Selling With Tax Due

Where is Hendry County and who bills its property tax?

Hendry County's own website highlights Lake Okeechobee and the Caloosahatchee River, and its historic courthouse is in LaBelle. The tax collector's main office is at 25 E. Hickpochee in LaBelle.

Billing and collection sit with the tax collector, while value and exemptions sit with the property appraiser. The county, school board and cities act as levying authorities and choose the rates. The collector's office offers to help you find whom to call at each.

  • Tax collector: 863-675-5280, mail to P.O. Box 1780, LaBelle, FL 33975-1780. Payments do not require an appointment.
  • Property appraiser: 863-675-5270, the contact for homestead filings, assessed value questions, mailing address changes and parcel description errors.
  • Clerk of court: records the deed at closing and handles tax deed sales.

How does Hendry County define what gets taxed?

The tax collector's page separates three kinds of charge. Real estate tax falls on land, buildings and improvements, scales with the appraiser's value, and attaches to a parcel number. Tangible personal property tax applies to furniture and equipment in businesses and rental properties.

The third is non-ad valorem assessments, set amounts that the taxing authorities collect for things like storm water, street lighting, fire and rescue, and solid waste. They do not depend on what your house is worth. Landlords: furnishings and equipment left in a rental can create a separate personal property bill. Ask the property appraiser whether a rental you are selling has such an account. Read every section of a Hendry bill before listing, since a title company will want the flat assessments settled too.

When are Hendry County property taxes due?

Hendry's tax year is the calendar year, and the bill shows up in November. The collector reminds owners that paying is their duty even if no notice arrives, and asks them to call if November passes with no bill.

Taxes become delinquent on April 1. Real estate then carries 3 percent minimum interest plus ad costs, with a certificate sale to follow by June 1. Unpaid tangible personal property carries 18 percent interest annually, and warrants are expected on or about June 1. Delinquent payments must be in certified U.S. funds drawn on a U.S. bank, and the amount due depends on the date payment is received.

Earlier in the year, state deadlines apply: March 1 for exemptions, April 1 for business property returns, a TRIM notice in August, and 25 days after that notice to petition the value adjustment board, all listed by the Department of Revenue.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

How does Hendry County treat late business and rental equipment tax?

Equipment tax runs on a harsher clock than the house. The tax collector says unpaid tangible personal property takes 18 percent interest a year plus advertising and fees, and warrants are expected on or about June 1. The office describes this tax as covering furniture and equipment in businesses and rental properties.

A landlord selling a rental should call the property appraiser at 863-675-5270 and ask whether the address has an equipment account. Any balance there should be settled before closing, since it is a separate bill from the real estate tax and the buyer's title company can find it.

Whatever the tax type, delinquent payments must come in certified U.S. funds drawn on a U.S. bank. The tax collector adds that the total depends on the day payment is received, so a quote given weeks before closing may be stale. Ask for a fresh figure in the last days before you sign, and ask the closing agent to confirm the amount that was wired.

How does the Hendry County installment plan work?

Hendry's collector offers quarterly prepayment under s. 197.222 to accounts above $100 in tax. Sign-up opens each November 1 and closes April 30 of the year you want to join.

Hendry County quarterly plan, four payments
InstallmentAmount basisDueDiscount
1stOne quarter of prior year's taxesJune 306%
2ndOne quarter of prior year's taxesSeptember 304.5%
3rdCurrent liability less 1st and 2nd, divided by 2December 313%
4thRemaining current liabilityMarch 31None

The first installment must be in by July 31 or the account drops out and the full tax is due by March 31, though the 6 percent discount ends after June 30. The first notice is mailed by June 1. If June 15 passes without one, call the office. Enrolled owners are re-enrolled automatically in later years. The office says the plan usually gives a discount close to the 4 percent November rate, though the match can shift with exemptions and values. Any change in ownership, value or exemption shows up in the last two bills, so a house sold mid-year needs a payoff check before closing. Source: the tax collector's installment page.

What other payment help does Hendry County give?

The tax collector's office tells owners to contact it about partial payments, installment payments and homestead tax deferral plans. The office posts a partial payment plan agreement on its website, and the state page says the collector decides whether to accept partial payments before delinquency under s. 197.374.

  • Homestead deferral uses Form DR-570, filed by March 31 following the assessment year.
  • It postpones the share of tax above 5 percent of household income, or 3 percent for permanent residents 65 and up.
  • Several checks for one bill must travel in one envelope, and the bill is payable in a lump unless an installment or partial plan applies.

Anyone may pay the bill. A buyer, relative or closing agent can pay on your behalf. The collector's portal takes online payments. Put your account and phone numbers on a mailed check's memo line, and make sure the words and numerals agree.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What changes for a Hendry County seller with homestead?

An owner who claimed homestead enjoyed a cap on assessed value growth, and that cushion does not travel to the buyer. The state's cap chart shows 2.7 percent for 2026, 2.9 for 2025 and 3.0 for 2024, and the next owner starts at just value on January 1 after the sale. If you plan to buy again in Florida, ask the appraiser there about portability, which moves part of the saved amount to a new homestead set up within three years.

The exemption itself is filed with the Hendry County Property Appraiser by March 1. The property appraiser's number is 863-675-5270.

What should a Hendry County seller do about unpaid tax?

Ask the tax collector for a payoff, then pass it to the closing agent. The flat assessments, the tax and any April 1 charges come out of proceeds, using the figure quoted for the day payment arrives.

If a certificate was sold on your parcel, redemption has to be in certified funds, and the holder must wait before seeking a deed. A financed buyer might take longer than a cash buyer, which counts when time is short.

Frequently asked questions

Who do I call about Hendry County property taxes?

Bills and payments go to 863-675-5280 (tax collector). Value and exemption questions go to 863-675-5270 (property appraiser).

What is the installment deadline in Hendry County?

Sign-up ends April 30, and the 6 percent discount needs the first payment by June 30. Payment after June 30 and before July 31 receives no discount.

When do Hendry County taxes go delinquent?

April 1. Real estate then adds a 3 percent minimum interest charge and advertising costs, and a certificate sale follows by June 1.

What if I do not get a tax bill in November?

The tax is still yours to pay. The collector suggests calling 863-675-5280 or searching online.

Can someone else pay my Hendry County taxes?

Yes. The collector's page says anyone may pay. Options include online, mail to P.O. Box 1780 in LaBelle, or an office visit.

  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Suwannee County, FL Property Tax Guide sale

What is Suwannee County, and why do its parcels look different?

Suwannee County became Florida's 37th county on December 21, 1858, cut from the western part of Columbia County. The county's own history page says the river that gives it a name starts in the Okefenokee Swamp in south Georgia, winds about 240 miles and ends at the Gulf, with more than 70 springs along the way.

Live Oak grew up where the Pensacola and Georgia Railroad, begun in 1857 and finished in 1861, passed a large live oak tree and pond. Sawmills later defined the west side: a Dowling Park mill was one of the two biggest in Florida, and the same page estimates that the boom years produced some 300,000 barrels of turpentine and a million barrels of rosin. The Hal W. Adams Bridge to Mayo is described as the only suspension span in Florida.

The result for a seller is a mix of in-town lots, river and spring frontage, old farm tracts and mobile home sites. Legal descriptions and parcel numbers deserve a second look before any contract.

Who does what for a Suwannee County property tax bill?

One office sets worth, another sends the bill, and elected boards pick the rates. The appraiser's own page explains that the county commission, school board, city councils and water management district choose the tax rate, not the appraiser.

  • Property Appraiser: 215 Pine Ave SW, Suite B, Live Oak, phone 386-362-1385, weekdays from half past eight to five, closed on listed holidays including Good Friday and the Thursday and Friday of Thanksgiving.
  • Tax Collector: Live Oak office at 386-362-2816, serving Suwannee residents and making exceptions for property owners.
  • Planning and Zoning, which also handles flood plain questions: 224 Pine Ave. S.W., phone 386-364-3401.

The appraiser's site notes that working values can change daily until July 1, and that the 2026 rolls were certified, finally certified and post-VAB certified on notices posted June 24, October 7 and October 21, 2026.

Which filing dates matter for Suwannee owners?

March 1 is the big one for exemptions and special classifications, and April 1 is for business personal property. The collector adds a March 31 cutoff for indigent relief and for adjusting non-ad valorem assessments.

  • March 1: homestead, $5,000 disabled veteran, widow and widower exemptions, DR-501DV, DR-501M, agricultural classification (DR-482), conservation classification (DR-482C) and the conservation exemption (DR-418C).
  • June 1: financial information for the low-income senior exemption (DR-501SC).
  • April 1: tangible personal property return (DR-405).

Agricultural classification does not transfer. The appraiser states that a new application is needed when land changes hands, and that farm zoning alone does not earn the classification; the land must be in bona fide agricultural use on or before January 1.

What happens if a Suwannee County bill goes unpaid?

Real estate takes a 3 percent penalty on April 1, and certificates are sold on unpaid accounts on or before June 1 which adds charges for the owner. Business personal property accrues interest instead and may face a tax warrant.

The collector sets a firm rule on payment type: after April 30 only certified funds are accepted, and personal checks mailed or left in the drop box are returned. The office adds a 2.35 percent charge to card payments and does not run cards over the phone. A mailed payment is judged by postmark before April 1 and by date of receipt after.

A certificate holder may seek a deed two years after the April 1 of issuance. Anyone holding a recorded contract for deed gets notice ahead of a tax deed sale, and homestead land carries a larger opening bid. Request a written payoff covering all open years before you list.

How do Suwannee County installments and deferral work?

The quarterly plan needs an estimated bill above $100 and an application at the collector's office before May 1. It stays in force each year without a new form once the first payment is made on time.

Suwannee County installment schedule as printed by the Tax Collector
InstallmentDue byDiscount
First quarterJune 306%
Second quarterSeptember 304.5%
Third quarterDecember 313%
Fourth quarterMarch 31None

Payments after June 30 and through July 31 are taken without a discount, and a missed first payment drops the parcel from the plan. Deferral is a separate tool for homesteads: the owner postpones the part above 5 percent of household income, or above 3 percent at 65 or older, and all of it under $10,000 of income ($12,000 at 70 or older). The mortgage may not exceed 70 percent of assessed value, total liens plus deferred tax may not exceed 85 percent, and applications are due January 31 after bills go out. The deferred tax becomes a lien.

Which Suwannee exemptions end with a sale?

All of them. Homestead requires that the home be in your name and your permanent residence on January 1, and Suwannee's list shows a $25,000 exemption plus $5,000 each for disabled veterans, widows, widowers, disabled persons and blind persons.

First-time applicants should bring a deed or contract, Florida driver's license and vehicle tag details and Social Security numbers. Veterans 65 or older with a combat-related permanent disability may get a discount equal to their VA percentage. A veteran with a total and permanent service-connected disability may qualify for a full homestead exemption, which can carry to a surviving spouse married five years.

Save Our Homes limits yearly growth in assessed value to 3 percent or the inflation rate, whichever is less, but after a sale the parcel is reassessed at full just value when the new year begins. If you plan another Florida purchase, ask about portability on Form DR-501T.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What local rules affect a Suwannee County house sale?

Check building history first. The county Building Department says the 9th Edition (2026) Florida Building Code and the 2023 National Electrical Code apply to permit applications from January 1, 2026. The department's phone is (386) 364-3407.

Mobile homes get special attention. Permits issued after May 1, 2022 require the pad to be inspected before the home is installed, and failure can mean the home is removed. Permits are not issued until all subcontractors have signed the addendum, and the driveway permit fee has been $50 since October 11, 2021.

The appraiser's site also offers a property record search, a GIS map, subdivision plat maps and a form to report homestead fraud, all useful for checking a legal description before a contract. Call Planning and Zoning with the parcel ID to learn whether the lot is in a flood plain zone. The appraiser's office can supply the parcel number.

What should I expect at the closing table?

Your title or closing agent prorates this year's tax by the closing date; earlier unpaid years are paid from your proceeds. The collector's page asks a seller who has sold to hand the bill to the new owner or bring it back to the counter.

If the sale is a quick cash purchase of an inherited, vacant or behind-on-tax house, the same steps apply: the purchaser accepts the property in its present condition and a tax balance is settled out of the price. Compare an offer with what listing would net after commissions, repairs and carrying months, and confirm that the parcel number and legal description on the deed match the appraiser's file.

The Suwannee clerk files the deed, and the state deed tax is paid at filing. Afterward, ask the appraiser to update ownership and drop your exemption, and keep the signed closing statement for your records.

Frequently asked questions

When did Suwannee County become a county?

It was formed on December 21, 1858, as the 37th Florida county, taken from the western portion of Columbia County.

What is the Suwannee County Property Appraiser's address?

The office is at 215 Pine Ave SW, Suite B, Live Oak, FL 32064, phone 386-362-1385, open Monday through Friday between half past eight and five, apart from holidays.

Does Suwannee County let me pay property tax in installments?

Yes, if your estimated bill exceeds $100 and you apply before May 1. Four quarterly payments are due June 30, September 30, December 31 and March 31.

Can I defer Suwannee County property tax?

Yes, for a homesteaded home with low income against the bill. Applications are due January 31 after bills are mailed, and the deferred amount becomes a lien.

Is agricultural classification transferable to a buyer in Suwannee County?

No. The appraiser says a new application is required after a sale, due March 1, and the land must be in bona fide agricultural use by January 1.

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Where does Jefferson County sit on the Florida map?

Jefferson County is a rural Big Bend county that the county website calls the Keystone County, because it is the only Florida county reaching from the Georgia line to the Gulf coast. It was established in 1827, and about 14,000 people live in roughly 609 square miles of farms, ranches and timberland.

Monticello, the county seat, sits 25 miles east of Tallahassee. Three rivers cross the county: the Wacissa, the Aucilla and the St. Marks. Lake Miccosukee covers 6,200 acres in the northwest corner, and the St. Marks National Wildlife Refuge holds nearly 9,000 acres near the coast. Interstate 10 and five U.S. highways cross it, and commercial flights leave from Tallahassee, 35 miles away.

For an owner, the layout matters for taxes. A town lot in Monticello, a farm parcel in the north and a coastal tract do not sit in the same taxing districts, so two Jefferson County bills rarely look alike.

Who sends and who reads a Jefferson County tax bill?

Three independent offices share the work, and the county's own page points to jeffersonpa.net for parcel search and exemption filing.

  • Property Appraiser: sets the assessed value and takes exemption applications.
  • Tax Collector: mails statements on or before November 1, accepts payment and runs the certificate sale.
  • Clerk and Comptroller: keeps official records and conducts a tax deed auction if one is requested.

Each August the appraiser mails a TRIM notice with the parcel's value and the rates each taxing body proposes. The hearings printed on it happen before rates are set in September.

Which millage lines did the collector list for 2026?

The Tax Collector's millage page shows six lines. A house inside Monticello would see all six, while a rural parcel skips the city line. The collector's glossary defines one mill as one-tenth of a cent, or a dollar per thousand of taxable value.

2026 Jefferson County millage lines, from the Tax Collector's millage page
Taxing bodyPrinted rateIn mills
Jefferson County.007367307.3673
School, required local effort.003160003.1600
School, discretionary.002248002.2480
City of Monticello.006850106.8501
Northwest Florida Water Management District.000020100.0201
Suwannee River Water Management District.000269500.2695

Commissioners, the school board, the city council and the two water districts each vote separately. Charges for services show up apart from these lines, so ask the collector which ones apply at your address.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

What does the Jefferson County calendar look like from November to June?

The mailing deadline is November 1, and the early payer gets 4 percent off in November, 3 in December, 2 in January and 1 in February. After that the clock runs toward April.

  • April 1: unpaid real estate tax is delinquent and takes a 3 percent penalty.
  • Early May: unpaid accounts are advertised in the local paper.
  • By June 1: the online certificate sale.

Tangible personal property, such as business equipment, draws a 1.5 percent monthly penalty once late. The collector's glossary adds that a year's lien attaches at the start of that year.

How do Jefferson County homestead and other exemptions work?

Homestead can cut $50,000 from the taxable figure, the first $25,000 reaching every levy and the second $25,000 sparing school levies. Form DR-501 goes to the appraiser before the March 1 cutoff, for a house that was your permanent home on January 1. Renting the house or moving out ends it.

An income-tested senior add-on, worth as much as $50,000, exists only where the local government chose to adopt it. Disabled veterans and deployed servicemembers have state-listed benefits as well. Ask the Jefferson County Property Appraiser which local options are in force. Annual growth in a homestead's assessed value is capped, and that cushion ends at a sale.

Does Jefferson County land use affect a sale?

It can. The county says building in Jefferson County is a two-step process: a Development Permit from the Planning Department first, then building permits from the Building Department, and no building permit issues for a site without the first. Land Development Regulations reach every kind of development, including driveways and power poles.

The page also warns that any subdivision of land needs approval under the Land Development Code, and that approval should be confirmed before new deeds are recorded. If land is conveyed without it, later owners may be unable to get a building permit. A seller splitting off acreage should check this before a buyer's attorney does.

  • The Planning Commission meets the second Thursday of each month at 6:00 p.m. in the Courthouse Annex, 435 West Walnut Street.
  • The county holds a Community Rating System score of 8 under the federal flood insurance program, which earns premium discounts.
  • The adopted Comprehensive Plan 2045 and its maps are posted on the county's planning page.
Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What shape does the land and climate give a Jefferson County parcel?

The county describes four seasons, a mean annual temperature of 67 degrees, January averages near 51 and July near 81, with rainfall near 57 inches annually. Red clay hills, live oaks and pasture define much of the open land, and the Monticello historic district holds 42 nineteenth-century buildings across 27 blocks. The 1890 Perkins Opera House and the 1910 courthouse anchor it.

Older and historic structures bring their own questions at sale time, such as roof age, wiring and flood zone. FEMA's Flood Map Service Center, which the county links, shows the zone for a given parcel.

How should a Jefferson County seller handle the tax balance?

The seller carries the tax to the closing date, and older unpaid years have to be cleared for clean title. The closing agent normally requests a payoff from the collector and pays it at the table from the seller's side.

The collector notes that the roll is a working roll and amounts can change during the year, so a quote is a snapshot. Get the payoff in writing with a date near closing. With an escrowing lender, ask how soon any leftover balance returns.

  • Search the parcel on the collector's site and note every year with a balance.
  • Ask whether a certificate was sold, since redemption takes certified funds.
  • Confirm exemptions with the appraiser so the title company prorates correctly.
  • The clerk records the deed and takes the stamp tax at the counter.

What happens to unpaid Jefferson County tax?

The debt is sold to an investor as a certificate, which the collector describes as a lien created by paying the delinquent tax, not a purchase of the property. The sale is a reverse auction on interest that starts at 18 percent and goes to the lowest bidder.

Certificates last seven years, and the face amount includes the 3 percent penalty, a 5 percent collector's commission and advertising costs. A homestead whose face value is under $250 is issued to the county at 18 percent instead of being sold. If the 22 month period passes, the parcel can go to a tax deed sale, which the clerk runs after the holder applies once two years have passed. The opening bid on a homestead includes half the latest assessed value. A March 31 deferral application date may help an owner at risk.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

How big is Jefferson County, and where is the county seat?

About 609 square miles, with Monticello as the seat, 25 miles east of Tallahassee. The county says roughly 14,000 people live there.

When does unpaid Jefferson County real estate tax turn delinquent?

April 1 is the line, and a 3 percent penalty lands then. The local paper runs unpaid accounts in early May, and the online certificate sale follows by June 1.

Is the Monticello millage line on every Jefferson County bill?

No. The collector's 2026 list shows a separate Monticello line of .00685010, which applies to parcels inside the city only.

Can I build on Jefferson County land without a permit?

Yes. The county requires a Development Permit from Planning first, then building permits, and subdivisions need approval before new deeds are recorded.

Where do I file for homestead in Jefferson County?

At the appraiser's office or on jeffersonpa.net, on Form DR-501, before March 1. The county's property page points residents to jeffersonpa.net.

What is Hamilton County, Florida like for a property owner?

Hamilton County is a rural county in north central Florida with Georgia along its northern edge. Its county website calls it a peninsula within a peninsula, bounded by the Withlacoochee River on the west and the Suwannee River on the east and south, with the Alapaha River, known as the "River of Sand", running through the middle.

The county seat is Jasper, and the tax collector's millage table also lists the municipalities of Jennings and White Springs. The county's page puts the estimated population at 14,799 and notes that Hamilton County sits at the crossroads of I-75 and I-10, within reach of Jacksonville, Gainesville and Tallahassee. For a seller, that mix of farmland, small towns and highway access shapes who buys, and the tax bill depends on whether the parcel sits inside a town.

The county also reports a moratorium on single-site RV and camper living, with no electric permits issued for RVs. If the property you plan to sell has an RV hookup, ask the county before listing.

Which Hamilton County offices handle the tax bill?

The property appraiser, the tax collector and the clerk each own one step. The appraiser sets value and exemptions, the collector bills and collects, and the clerk runs the value adjustment board and tax deed sales.

  • Property appraiser: values every parcel, keeps the exemption rolls, and handles name, address and legal description changes. Call or visit the office in Jasper before March 1 to file for homestead.
  • Tax collector: online at hamiltontaxcollector.com, with a parcel search and online payment.
  • Clerk and value adjustment board: 207 NE 1st Street, Room 106, Jasper, phone 386-792-1288.
  • County commission: sets the county millage rate and handles questions such as the RV rule above.

Confirm office hours by phone before you drive in, since county offices post their own schedules.

What does the Hamilton County millage table show?

The tax collector publishes a table headed "Hamilton 2026 millage", in decimal form. Treat it as the collector's published listing and compare it with your TRIM notice and November bill.

Hamilton County millage lines as listed on the tax collector's property tax page
Taxing unitListed rate
County.00870250
School, required local effort.00307500
School, discretionary.00249800
Jasper.00795780
Suwannee River Water Management.00026950
Jennings.00700000
White Springs.00600000

Only one town line applies to a given parcel. A rural parcel carries the county, school and water lines, while a house in Jasper adds the Jasper line. Non-ad valorem assessments are separate, flat charges for services such as fire or solid waste, and they show up on the same bill.

The collector's glossary describes millage as one dollar per thousand dollars of taxable value, so each line shows how much one body adds. Appraisal is the value, assessment is the tax owed, and the tax lien dates from January 1 of the tax year, which is why a bill can follow a house across a sale.

What are the Hamilton County billing and late dates?

The collector mails statements by the first of November. Early payers get 4 percent off in November, then 3, 2 and 1 percent in the following three months. After March, the bill sits at full price until it goes late on the first of April, when real estate tax takes a 3 percent penalty and the parcel is listed in the local paper from May on. Unpaid business property accrues 1.5 percent monthly.

Unpaid real estate liens are sold online at the end of May or on June 1. Before any of that, the appraiser's January 1 valuation date, the March 1 exemption cutoff and the August TRIM notice come first. The state taxpayer page puts the window for a value petition at 25 days after TRIM, and the Department of Revenue lists the rest of the calendar.

How do I appeal a Hamilton County assessment?

You petition the value adjustment board through the clerk. The board only decides whether property is appraised at fair market value and whether an agricultural classification or exemption should be approved. It cannot change a value because you cannot afford the tax, and it has no control over rates.

  • The filing fee is $15, and $5 more for each extra parcel when contiguous parcels are combined on one petition.
  • If the property appraiser or tax collector denied a timely homestead exemption or homestead tax deferral, there is no fee.
  • Petitions need an original signature, and copies or faxes are not accepted.
  • A late petition is sent to the board attorney, and a hearing is set only for good cause.

The clerk encourages you to speak with the property appraiser before filing. The state form is DR-486, and a postmark by the deadline does not save a petition that arrives after it.

What relief programs matter to a Hamilton County seller?

Homestead is the main one, filed by March 1 and available only to the owner's permanent residence. The state guide limits the first layer of the exemption to $25,000 and lets a second layer reach up to $25,000 more, school taxes excluded.

A deferral under Form DR-570 is another route for owners with limited income, with the application due at the tax collector by March 31. For a seller, the cap that protected the old assessed value disappears when title changes hands, which explains why the buyer's bill is often higher than yours. If you are moving to another Florida home, ask the property appraiser there about carrying part of the cap forward.

What if a Hamilton County property goes to a tax deed sale?

The clerk conducts the auction once a certificate holder files an application. Hamilton County's tax deeds page says every property sells buyer beware and as is, with no promises on title, zoning, access or physical condition, and it cites s. 197.542(2) for the high bidder's nonrefundable cost deposit.

A holder may apply two years after April 1 of the issue year, and homestead land opens at the taxes due plus half its latest assessed value. Paying the collector before the sale takes the parcel off the block. If your house has an advertised date, plan the sale of the home around it.

How do I handle a Hamilton County sale when tax is unpaid?

Tell the closing agent about each unpaid year at the start. The agent gets a payoff from the collector and pays it from the sale proceeds, so you do not need cash in hand. Plan the timing around April 1, because the 3 percent penalty and the newspaper charge raise the payoff.

Ask for a draft settlement statement before the closing date and check that every tax line matches the collector's figure. Buyers who pay cash can often meet a tight schedule, a useful option when a certificate or sale date is near.

Frequently asked questions

When does a Hamilton County bill go late?

On April 1. The collector adds a 3 percent penalty to real estate tax on that date and lists the parcel in the paper beginning in May.

How much is the Hamilton County early payment discount?

It starts at 4 percent for November and falls one point each month through February.

What does it cost to petition the Hamilton County value board?

$15, plus $5 for each added contiguous parcel. Petitions over a denied homestead or homestead deferral request have no fee.

Can a house with a tax certificate be sold in Hamilton County?

Yes. Closing pays the collector, the lien clears, and the buyer gets clean title. Ask for a payoff figure that includes interest.

Who decides the rate on my Hamilton County bill?

The taxing bodies decide, such as the county, school board, towns and the river district. The appraiser only sets value and handles exemptions.

  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Franklin County, FL Property Tax Guide sale
  • Turn the Franklin County, FL Property Tax Guide offer down and you owe us nothing

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Behind on Franklin County property tax?

Who sends, collects and enforces a Franklin County tax bill?

Three offices share the work. The appraiser values the parcel, the tax collector bills it, and the clerk of court conducts any tax deed auction. The county commission, school board and the cities of Apalachicola and Carrabelle set the rates.

Franklin County lies in the northwestern Panhandle, roughly 80 miles southwest of Tallahassee, across 545 square miles and 348,800 acres. The county site cites more than 11,000 residents and a founding year of 1832. Outside the two cities, the commission serves as the local government.

  • Property appraiser: keeps the roll, takes exemption filings, mails TRIM notices in August. Per its home page, the office neither sets rates nor collects tax.
  • Tax collector: 33 Market Street, Suite 202, Apalachicola; (850) 653-9323. Prints bills, accepts payment, sells certificates.
  • Clerk: holds the courthouse auction of tax deeds and records your deed when you sell.

What is the Franklin County tax calendar?

Exemption paperwork comes first in the year, and the bill comes last. The table lists each step the county offices print on their own sites.

Franklin County property tax steps, from the appraiser and tax collector websites
WhenStepOffice
January 1 to March 1Window for homestead and agricultural classification filingsProperty appraiser
April 1Business personal property returns dueProperty appraiser
AugustTRIM notice, marked as a notice and not a billProperty appraiser
By November 1Statements mailedTax collector
November through FebruaryDiscount slides from 4% to 1%Tax collector
April 1 of the next yearReal estate bill late; 3% penaltyTax collector
On or before June 1Online lien auction for unpaid parcelsTax collector

Sources: the tax collector and the appraiser. Mailing a statement does not turn the TRIM notice into a bill, so wait for the November statement before paying.

What do the Franklin County millage lines mean?

Franklin County's tax collector posts a table labeled "Franklin 2025 millage". A millage figure is the tax per thousand dollars of taxable value, and the table prints it as a decimal. Ask the collector for the table covering the current year before you rely on these.

  • County: .00504590
  • School, local effort: .00194400
  • School, discretionary: .00224800
  • Northwest Florida Water Management: .00002070
  • Carrabelle: .00750000
  • Apalachicola: .00834570
  • Dog Island: .00400000
  • Eastpoint district: .00375000
  • Alligator Point: .00123040

Only one local line fits a given address. Eastpoint, Dog Island and Alligator Point appear as districts, and Carrabelle and Apalachicola are the two cities. County, school and water lines stack on top. Flat assessments for services are charged separately and print on the same statement, so check the lower portion of the bill too.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

What reduces a Franklin County bill?

A permanent residence qualifies for the Florida homestead exemption of up to $50,000 of value, described in the Department of Revenue guide. The filing window runs January 1 to March 1 at the appraiser's office, and renting the house out ends eligibility.

Once a homestead is in place, a statutory cap restrains how fast its assessed value can rise. A sale wipes out that cushion for the next owner, so the buyer's first Franklin County bill may look much larger than yours did.

Can the bill be paid in pieces in Franklin County?

The state permits quarterly prepayment under s. 197.222 if you apply to the tax collector by May 1 of the assessment year, and low-income homestead owners can defer part of the tax with Form DR-570 by March 31. Both come from the state taxpayer page. Whether either route helps depends on your income and timing, so phone the collector at (850) 653-9323 before the dates pass. Mortgage escrow lenders normally settle the bill themselves.

What happens after April 1 on an unpaid Franklin County parcel?

A 3 percent penalty lands on the real estate bill at the start of April, and in May the parcel is listed in the paper for three straight weeks at the owner's expense. Business equipment and mobile home attachments follow a harsher path of monthly interest and warrants.

Around the end of May, the collector auctions a lien certificate online. Bidders start at 18 percent and bid the rate down, and the low rate wins. The winner pays your tax and holds a lien, and you owe them the bid rate. A buyer cannot take your house at that point. The glossary says a deed application is allowed two years after April 1 of the issue year, and the collector warns that a certificate left unredeemed for 22 months can end in a deed sale.

Homestead parcels owing under $250 are not offered to the public. The county holds those at 18 percent a year until the total passes $250.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

How does a Franklin County tax deed sale work?

The clerk's office runs the sale. Franklin County sales, when scheduled, are generally held on the first Monday of the month at 11:00 AM inside the main courthouse at 33 Market Street, Apalachicola, and the clerk tells people to call to verify before attending. Notice runs in the Apalachicola Times once a week for four weeks.

  • You can redeem by paying the tax collector before the sale, or before the clerk receives the winning bidder's full payment.
  • For homestead property, the opening bid adds half of the latest assessed value to the taxes, interest and fees.
  • The winning bidder posts a nonrefundable deposit of 5 percent or $200, whichever is greater, and pays the balance within 24 hours.
  • Documentary stamps of $.70 per $100 of the bid and recording fees are due from the bidder.
  • Some government liens survive the deed, and every property is sold as is.

The clerk's page adds cautions for anyone on either side. Governmental liens can survive the deed, and the clerk warns that most title insurers want a quiet title lawsuit before they will insure a tax deed property. The deed gives the buyer a right to immediate possession, but the clerk says legal action may still be needed to get it. For an owner, the lesson is simple: a sale that you close before the auction date avoids all of that, and your own buyer gets a normal title search instead.

What does a Franklin County seller do about taxes at closing?

An unpaid balance is a lien the buyer's title company will insist on clearing. The closing agent can send the payoff to the tax collector out of the seller's proceeds. Request a figure good through the closing day, since a bill past April 1 grows by a 3 percent penalty and newspaper advertising.

The state also taxes the deed itself. Documentary stamps run 70 cents on each $100 of consideration outside Miami-Dade, and every party to the document is liable, according to the Department of Revenue. The clerk takes the payment at recording.

Frequently asked questions

Which month is the cheapest to pay in Franklin County?

November. The tax collector prints a 4 percent discount for November, 3 percent for December, 2 percent for January and 1 percent for February.

Does the appraiser or the collector set my rate?

Neither. Per the appraiser's home page, that office does not set rates, and the tax collector's millage page says the county commission, school board and each city or district do.

Is a house with a tax certificate on it still sellable?

Yes. Closing pays the redemption to the tax collector, which then repays the certificate holder. Ask (850) 653-9323 for the redemption total.

When is the Franklin County exemption filing cutoff?

March 1. Filing opens January 1, and the appraiser notes the home must be your permanent residence.

How fast can a tax deed auction happen?

Slowly. A certificate holder waits two years after April 1 of the issue year to apply, and you can redeem up to the point the clerk receives the winning bidder's full payment.

Owe Washington County Property Tax? Get a Cash Offer

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Behind on Washington County property tax?
We buy Washington County houses as-is, and the title company pays unpaid tax from the proceeds.
Get My Cash Offer →

Where do Washington County owners go in Chipley for property tax questions?

Three separate offices in Chipley handle a Washington County parcel, and each answers a different question. The property appraiser sets value and takes exemption filings at 850-638-6205. The tax collector sends the bill and accepts payment at 1331 S. Blvd #101 (mailed payments go to PO Box 1038) and is staffed Monday through Friday, eight to four Disputes land with the circuit clerk's board records desk at 1293 Jackson Avenue, Suite 101.

The appraiser's FAQ describes the November bill as a relay. One office prices every parcel at its January 1 market level, each taxing body then chooses a rate to fund its budget, and a third office mails the result. The appraiser never levies or collects anything. Calling the wrong desk costs a day, so pick the office before you dial.

  • Parcel value, ownership records, exemption filings: property appraiser.
  • Balance owed, the installment plan, certificates: tax collector, 850-638-6275.
  • Petitions about a value or a refused exemption: the board's clerk, 850-638-6233.

Which levies stack up on a Washington County tax bill?

Seven rate lines appear on the collector's 2026 millage page, and just two belong to towns. Chipley and Vernon charge their own rates, so land outside both towns has no municipal line. The county line comes from the five-member commission, one seat per district, while the school board and the regional water district control the rest.

Seven 2026 rate lines on the Washington County collector's millage page
LinePrinted rate
County.00850000
City of Chipley.00700000
City of Vernon.00499760
School, required local effort.00314500
School, capital outlay.00150000
School, discretionary.00074800
Northwest water management.00002010

Source: Washington County Tax Collector, millage rates. The page labels these figures current, never adopted, so check final numbers with the office before repeating them. Each rate is printed as a decimal; .00850000 reads as 8.5 mills.

Which months drive the Washington County tax calendar?

The collector's deadline page opens with a discount and closes with a penalty. Payment made after March 31 counts as late.

  • November: collection starts, and paying by the 30th earns the largest discount, 4 percent.
  • December: the discount drops to 3 percent.
  • January: 2 percent.
  • February: 1 percent.
  • March 31: the full gross amount.
  • April 1: delinquency begins; real property takes a 3 percent penalty and business equipment starts accruing monthly interest.
  • Within 45 days: delinquent parcels run in a local newspaper, and the printing charge joins the balance.

The appraiser's calendar sits upstream. Value and residency are fixed on January 1, personal exemption filings run through March 1, the TRIM notice lands in August, and the board petition window shuts in September.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Can a Washington County owner pay in four installments?

Yes, and the collector lists each date. The first payment is due by June 1, and a participant who has not paid it by June 30 is dropped. Number two follows before September 30, number three by December 31, and the last by March 31. Current participants stay enrolled without reapplying.

New applications for the following year close April 30, a day earlier than the state's May 1 cutoff described on the Department of Revenue taxpayer page. Owners whose lender escrows the taxes gain nothing from it, since the lender settles the whole bill in November.

What happens to a Washington County parcel when a tax certificate is sold?

Someone else pays your late tax and gets a lien in return, with no claim to the land itself. The collector's page says the sale starts by June 1 for the previous year's unpaid real estate tax, after a three week newspaper notice.

The certificate amount adds the unpaid tax, any non ad valorem assessments, the penalty, a five percent commission for the collector and ad costs. Bids open at 18 percent interest and fall; the lowest bid wins, and that rate is what you pay to redeem. Where the earned interest would fall short of five percent, a five percent minimum is charged.

Two details involve small balances and old liens. Homestead land with a face amount below $250 skips the public sale, and the county holds that certificate at 18 percent. Every certificate dies after seven years. The collector accepts only certified funds in US dollars to redeem, and warns that missing the 22 month redemption period can end in a tax deed sale. A link to an online sale site sits on the collector's front page.

What does the Washington County appraiser want to see for a homestead claim?

The appraiser's exemption page lists a homestead benefit of up to $50,722, claimed in person on Form DR-501 before the March 1 cutoff. A flat $25,000 hits every levy, schools included. The page puts the second layer at up to $25,722 for 2025; it sits on value above $50,000, excludes school taxes, and is complete at $75,000 of assessed value.

The appraiser treats residency as a finding of fact, weighing your statements, workplace, voter registration, license, vehicle tags and the address on your federal return. Bring the following:

  • A recorded deed or a bill in your name, and a Social Security number for each owner.
  • Florida driver licenses for you and a spouse.
  • A Washington County voter card or a Declaration of Domicile, plus Florida registrations for every vehicle you own.
  • The trust agreement, if a trust holds title.
  • For a mobile home, the title or registration; you must also own the ground under it.

Spouses together get a single exemption. Skipping March 1 forfeits that year, although a late application can be taken to the Value Adjustment Board.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Which extra breaks does the Washington County appraiser list?

The page names several smaller breaks, some with conditions that matter at a sale.

  • Senior break: up to $50,000 more for a homestead owner who turned 65 by January 1, if household income stays under a ceiling that began at $20,000 and rises with a cost of living index. It touches county millage only and needs a sworn income statement by March 1.
  • Five thousand dollars each for unremarried widows and widowers, total and permanent disability, blindness, and veterans with at least a 10 percent service disability.
  • Full exemption for an honorably discharged veteran who is totally and permanently disabled through service; it may pass to a surviving spouse.
  • A granny flat reduction, limited to 20 percent of assessed value, for permitted quarters housing a parent or grandparent who is 62 or older.

Each one ends or must be refiled when ownership changes, so a buyer begins with nothing.

How does a Washington County owner challenge a value or a missed exemption?

Ask the board for a hearing by petition, delivered to the clerk. The clerk's page sends you to the appraiser (850-638-6205) or the board clerk (850-638-6233) for the cutoff date, and the appraiser's FAQ says it usually falls in early September.

The clerk lists several rules. A $50 fee is charged and not refunded, except for appeals of a timely homestead denial or a deferral denial. The state form must be printed and carry an original signature, since copies and faxes are turned away. A representative needs written authority from the owner, and a late filing needs written reasons for good cause.

Talk to an appraiser first. The office walks through each property at least every third year, adjusts values between visits when sales shift, and will show the data behind a figure. Its FAQ defines a usable sale as one between a willing buyer and seller under no pressure, so a below-market family transfer does not move the market. Non-homestead assessments cannot climb more than 10 percent annually, so a larger leap on a rental or empty lot suggests new building or a sale.

What should a Washington County landlord or small business know about equipment tax?

Business and rental equipment sits on a separate account with separate penalties. Anyone holding such assets on January 1 files by April 1; the appraiser's FAQ says late returns draw 5 percent a month, capped at 25 percent. The collector adds its own monthly interest on delinquent equipment tax after April 1, begins warrant work May 1 and advertises the list once.

There is no reporting floor, and fully depreciated items still count. A business buyer inherits the tax, including any January 1 shortfall. A landlord selling a furnished rental should tell the appraiser so the account closes and no stray bill follows.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

What should a Washington County seller with unpaid tax do before closing?

Get a payoff letter from the collector that runs through the closing day and pass it to the title agent. A sale before April 1 sidesteps the penalty and the ad charge. Deed stamps cost seventy cents per hundred dollars of price outside Miami-Dade, and the Department of Revenue holds every signer liable, so name the payer in the contract.

Do not expect the seller's bill to repeat. The state's Save Our Homes guide says the cap lapses with a sale and value jumps to market the next January 1.

Frequently asked questions

What date makes a Chipley area tax bill late?

April 1. That day the collector attaches a 3 percent penalty to real property and starts monthly interest on business equipment.

How much do I save by paying in January?

Two percent off. The collector's list steps down from 4 percent in November through 3, 2 and 1 in the following months.

Could a tiny balance cost someone a homestead?

Not through a public sale at first. A homestead lien under $250 is issued to the county at 18 percent and can be sold to a buyer only after the amount plus interest passes $250.

How long does a certificate stay alive?

Seven years, counted from the sale's opening day. The owner's redemption window is 22 months under the period the collector cites.

Where can I read the latest rate lines?

On the collector's millage page, which prints seven 2026 lines. The page does not call them adopted, so phone 850-638-6275 to confirm.
